rows.key_quote: Abeona reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $13.5 million for ZEVASKYN, an 18% increase from the prior quarter and a beat against expectations given the manufacturing shutdown and batch failure in Q2. The company announced the acquisition of APT-1011 (now ABO-801), a Phase III-ready oral therapy for EoE, with top-line results anticipated around end of 2028. Management expressed confidence in the commercial foundation and the ability to advance the new asset without distracting from ZEVASKYN launch.

Kyivstar reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $349 million (up 18% YoY) and EBITDA of $189 million (up 10% YoY), driven by strong digital growth. Management raised its full-year 2026 outlook, projecting revenue growth of 15%-17% and EBITDA growth of 10%-12% in dollars. The company highlighted the acquisition of GigaCloud to strengthen its cloud position and noted that Q4 guidance implies a slowdown due to seasonality and specific operational headwinds.

Medicus reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $15.2 million versus $16.0 million a year earlier on lower operating expenses of $14.5 million versus $15.4 million; nine-month net loss widened to $35.9 million from $27.3 million, including a $10 million acquired IPR&D charge tied to the Pfizer CD228V deal. Cash plus restricted cash was $13.1 million at September 30 versus $8.7 million cash at December 31, 2025, with total liabilities of $25 million driven by the Streeterville debenture. Management offered no numerical guidance but said it anticipates a substantial reduction in operating expenses in coming quarters and is prioritizing CD228V, the proposed SkinJect SPAC combination at a $135 million pre-money valuation, and Teverelix partnering. There were no revenue or EPS figures, no formal guidance, and the quarter reflects a pre-commercial clinical-stage company funding development.

Lantronix reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $32.4 million, representing an 8% year-over-year increase and sequential growth. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 45.3%, while non-GAAP net income rose 50% to $2.2 million ($0.05 per share). Management raised the Q2 revenue guidance range to $32.5-$34.5 million, citing double-digit year-over-year growth expectations.

H&R Block reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $224.3 million, a 10.2% increase driven by international services, tax protection/identity services, small business services, and U.S. tax preparation. The company reaffirmed its full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue between $4.11 billion and $4.16 billion and adjusted EBITDA between $1.11 billion and $1.14 billion. Management highlighted strong retention from the expanded 'Second Look' program and successful pilots of a new consultative client experience ahead of tax season 2027.

First quarter FY2027 organic net sales declined 6.7% year-over-year to approximately $18 million adjusted EBITDA, driven by volume mix losses and cost inflation despite a 320 bps improvement in adjusted gross margin from the snacks divestiture. Management highlighted progress on SG&A realignment but emphasized significant headwinds including supply disruptions, weather impacts, and elevated energy costs. The company reiterated its focus on completing the international sale to Aurelius and managing upcoming debt maturities while maintaining a cautious outlook due to ongoing lender discussions.

loanDepot reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net loss of $31 million versus a $29 million loss in Q2, with origination volume down 12% sequentially to $7.0 billion (within the $6.25-8.25B guide) and adjusted revenue of $302 million versus $307 million. Pull-through weighted gain-on-sale margin came in at 399 bps, above the 360-390 bps guide and up from 345 bps on a HELOC-driven mix shift, while expenses fell $8 million sequentially and cost to produce improved 16% year-over-year. Q4 guidance calls for origination volume of $4.5-6.5 billion and lock volume of $3.25-5.25 billion, both down sharply seasonally, with pull-through gain-on-sale margin guided to 425-465 bps. Management declined to detail debt refinancing plans for upcoming maturities, and the CEO flagged an unexpected late-Q3 purchase-lending decline from rates above 7%, while projecting break-even profitability by first half or mid-2027 if rates hold.

Revenue rose 12.6% to $159.2 million, the 14th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, on an 11% increase in ending student population and 14.2% adjusted start growth. Adjusted EBITDA grew 30.8% to $17.4 million with margin up 150 bps to ~11%, and net income rose 24% to $4.7 million ($0.15 diluted EPS). Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $600-605 million from $590-600 million, but adjusted EBITDA ($76-80 million), net income, EPS ($0.74-0.83) and capex were only reiterated, and start growth guidance was narrowed to 10%-12% from 10%-14%. The company repurchased ~871,000 shares for ~$21 million and increased its buyback authorization to $70 million.

Sanmina reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $3.86 billion (up 84% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.43, significantly exceeding the high end of its outlook. The company also beat full-year FY2026 expectations with revenue of $14.5 billion and non-GAAP operating margin expansion to 7.4%. Management raised guidance for fiscal year 2027, projecting revenue between $17.5 billion and $19.5 billion.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $164.2 million from $252.4 million a year ago, a $88.2 million decline, with Bitcoin mining revenue down $83.1 million as average Bitcoin price fell 37% (a $94.8 million revenue hit, partly offset by $11.7 million from higher production). Net income was $632.1 million, or $1.28 per diluted share, versus $123.1 million/$0.27, inflated by an $885.3 million non-cash fair value gain on digital assets; adjusted EBITDA rose 117% to $857.7 million. Hashrate grew 18% to 71.2 EH/s and cost per petahash improved 2% to $30.8, but blocks won fell 7% quarter-over-quarter. Management said two AI/HPC lease signings are still targeted before year-end but could slip into next year, while citing FERC approval for the 485 MW Long Ridge plant, a Matagorda site of up to 2 GW, $1.4 billion (37%) of debt reduction, and a new $500 million buyback authorization.

monday.com reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $378M, up 19% YoY, with record non-GAAP operating income of $89.4M and a record 24% operating margin (up from 15% a year ago); net income was $93.6M and diluted EPS $2.14. However, NDR fell to 108% (guided to ~107%), gross margin slipped to 88% from 90%, and Q4 guidance of $380-382M implies only ~14% growth, a sharp deceleration from 19%. Management cited three headwinds — a ~20% workforce reduction, downmarket/SMB churn, and longer enterprise sales cycles — with the guidance assuming similar trends persist into 2027, while AI ARR reached $36M and headcount fell 690 since Q2 to 2,479.

Radiant Logistics reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $279.8 million, up 23.4% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA reaching $12.2 million (up 79.4%). Adjusted net income surged 91.1% to $8.6 million, driven by operating leverage and the non-recurrence of a prior period credit loss. Management raised guidance for full-year adjusted EBITDA from $50-55 million to $55-60 million.

Microvast reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of roughly $45.8 million, down 62.8% YoY ($77.5 million decline), on a 62.2% volume drop to approximately 190 MWh from 502 MWh. Gross margin collapsed to 5.2% from 37.6%, including a $9.3 million obsolete-inventory write-down worth 20.4 points, and GAAP net loss was $76.8 million with adjusted EBITDA of -$60.8 million versus +$21.9 million a year ago. Management gave no forward guidance and instead flagged a going-concern doubt, a $35.7-35.8 million long-lived asset impairment, and ongoing lender negotiations to refinance, extend, or restructure near-term debt. Declines spanned Europe (-64%), APAC (-65%), and the U.S. (-31%), with management citing softer commercial vehicle demand, pricing pressure, and Chinese tax/rebate changes.

NESR reported Q3 2026 revenue of $504.7 million, up 70.9% year over year but down 3.1% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $95.9 million (19.0% margin) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.38. Management guided to roughly $2 billion of full-year revenue (plus or minus), ~20% adjusted EBITDA margin, $220-$225 million of CapEx, and 30-35% free cash flow conversion, while reaffirming the multi-year 3B3 $3 billion revenue strategy. The quarter was pressured by ~$5.5 million (~110 bps of margin) in incremental freight and logistics costs and continued Iraq disruption, and Q3 free cash flow was negative $45.9 million on working capital, though a meaningful portion of delayed receivables was collected early in Q4. The company announced its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share and completed a ~$747 million refinancing that extends maturities.

NRG reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.0 billion, free cash flow before growth of $1.2 billion, and adjusted EPS of $4.68, with all four key financial metrics up at least 50% year-over-year on LS Power contributions, higher capacity revenue, and consumer growth. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance across all four metrics, expecting to finish slightly below the adjusted EBITDA midpoint despite ERCOT power prices averaging nearly 40% below the original plan, and introduced 2027 guidance at $5.75 billion adjusted EBITDA, $3.15 billion FCFbG, and $9.05 adjusted EPS (excluding the announced asset sale). The quarter's key change was the $4 billion sale of six generation facilities (~4.9 GW) to LS Power at an unsolicited 8x 2027E EBITDA, paired with a $1 billion increase to planned buybacks ($3 billion total across 2026-2027) and $2 billion of planned debt reduction at close. The 2027 guide incorporates $185 million of net wholesale price pressure and $30 million higher RGGI compliance costs versus 2026, while long-term 14%+ EPS and FCF/share CAGR through 2030 is reaffirmed.

NeurAxis reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.0 million, up 150% from $811,000 a year ago, the strongest quarterly revenue in company history and the ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. Gross margin expanded 330 bps to 86.6% as the mix shifted from discounted financial assistance to full-reimbursement payers, lifting IB-Stim ASP 35% to $1,045 per device. GAAP operating loss widened to $6.6 million, but excluding a $4.3 million one-time stock comp charge it was $2.3 million, up only 9% YoY. Coverage footprint reached 147 million lives with two new payers added in the last 45 days (44 million incremental lives), though the company flagged that one new major payer is authorizing only one device rather than the full four-device course, an issue expected to be corrected shortly, and that commercial expansion will increase near-term expenses and cash burn.

Ocular Therapeutix is a pre-commercial biotech with no product revenue; the quarter's key financial disclosure was $530.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, with an expected runway into 2028 (excluding full AXPAXLI commercialization costs). The company reiterated its plan to submit the AXPAXLI NDA for wet AMD in Q4 2026, following a positive September pre-NDA meeting and alignment with the FDA on the 505(b)(2) pathway, which may shorten review by up to 60 days. Management disclosed a proactive change to SOL-R's primary endpoint from week 56 to week 40 to protect trial integrity ahead of the week-52 interim safety analysis, with a minimal alpha penalty of 0.0001 and SOL-R topline still guided to Q1 2028. SOL-X dosing was extended from every 24 weeks to every 48 weeks based on SOL-1 durability analyses.

Orthofix reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $207.9 million, up 2.3% year-over-year on a pro forma constant currency basis, but management said results were below expectations as U.S. Spine fixation fell 5% on market softness plus unplanned supplier and instrument-set delays. Adjusted EBITDA was $26 million (12.5% of pro forma sales), up from $24.6 million (12.1%), and adjusted gross margin was 70.7% on unfavorable geographic mix. Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to $825-830 million of net sales and $86-88 million of adjusted EBITDA, reflecting the Q3 miss, continued spine softness, and the accelerated distributor and portfolio restructuring. Management also flagged an approximately $22 million 2027 European MDR headwind and a temporary free-cash timing headwind from the European distributor arrangement, while declining to give 2027 guidance beyond saying core revenue should be positive ex-MDR.

Q3 revenue of $410M rose ~90% YoY and 19% sequentially, with EPS of $2.44 and gross margin of 57.6% (up 60 bps QoQ, 300 bps vs Q4 2025) and operating margin of 32.6% (up 260 bps QoQ); revenue, operating margin and EPS all exceeded the high end of guidance. Q4 guidance was raised to $430-450M (over 7% sequential growth at midpoint, ~$2.69 EPS) with gross margin expected to tick up another 0.5 pt to slightly above 58%. Backlog rose 20% to a record $1.3B, and management projects sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027 with roughly 50 bps per quarter of gross margin expansion.

Q3 revenue rose 4% YoY to $350 million despite a 7% YoY delivery decline (3,806 units) and a $10 million regulatory credit headwind, while gross margin improved to minus 74% from minus 105% in Q2, largely on a ~$200 million lower impairment charge ($94 million vs $300 million). Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed ~20% sequentially to $726 million and free cash outflow fell 30% QoQ to just over $1 billion, with roughly $800 million of the $1.4 billion 2026 cash-improvement target delivered. PIF expanded the credit facility by $1.75 billion, lifting pro forma liquidity to $3.75 billion into Q4 2027. Management guided H2 deliveries above H1 and further but smaller Q4 cash improvement, deferring formal 2027 guidance to year-end results; the company remains deeply unprofitable with heavy ongoing investment in AMP-2, Midsize, and robotaxi.

Kaspi reported Q3 constant-currency revenue growth of 18% and EBITDA up only 1%, with net income marginally positive for the first time in a while; e-Commerce GMV grew 17% but Marketplace slowed to 8% and take rate reached 16.3%. FY GMV guidance was cut sharply to ~12% from ~20%, attributed entirely to KZT appreciation cutting ticket sizes, while FY EBITDA growth was reiterated at ~5%. The quarter featured a large new strategic bet — 42 partner convenience stores piloting at 15% store-level EBITDA margin, targeting 300 stores in 2026 and a 3,000-store midterm aspiration — alongside the Kasper AI assistant (1.4M users) and Hepsiburada fintech rollout in Türkiye.

Zeta reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $493 million, up 46% YoY (30% excluding Marigold and political candidate revenue, accelerating from 28% last quarter), $22 million above the guidance midpoint. Adjusted EBITDA was $121 million at a 24.6% margin (up 140 bps), free cash flow $82 million (up 73%), GAAP diluted EPS $0.14 versus a $0.02 loss a year ago, and non-GAAP EPS $0.38 (up 58%). The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $37 million to $1,855 million at the midpoint, lifted Q4 revenue guidance by $15 million to $523 million, and increased full-year adjusted EBITDA to $414.6 million, FCF to $271 million, and GAAP EPS to $0.23 from a prior $0.10. Super-Scaled Customers grew to 212 (up 18%), quarterly ARPU expanded 22% to $2 million, and RFPs were up over 100% YoY.

Quantum reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $89.6 million, beating the high end of guidance ($84M-$86M) driven by a 43% year-over-year increase and strong demand in secondary storage. GAAP gross margin expanded 170 bps sequentially to 41%, while non-GAAP operating income turned positive at $9.9 million, significantly exceeding expectations. Management raised the Q3 revenue guidance range to approximately $91 million plus or minus $2 million, citing improved component availability and continued strong bookings.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Q3 FY2026 total operating revenue fell to $130.3 million from $146.6 million a year ago, with a net loss of $4.5 million versus $23.9 million of net income in the prior-year period, and adjusted EBITDA of $17.3 million versus $24.9 million. The year-over-year decline was driven by lower third-party coal sales (down ~400,000 tons), a $9 million increase in purchase power costs, and a $5.7 million loss on debt extinguishment. Management gave no formal financial guidance but pointed to contracted capacity and energy pricing of $59/MWh in 2027 rising to $75 by 2031-2035, roughly 95% of accredited Merom capacity contracted through 2035, and reiterated a Turtle Creek FID target before year-end with COD in 2H 2028. Management guided that reported losses will likely widen before Turtle Creek runs as full construction-loan interest is expensed.

Hyperfine reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.0 million, up 73% year-over-year and 53% sequentially, with 14 units sold versus eight a year ago. Gross margin hit a record 56.7%, up ~300 bps year-over-year, operating loss narrowed to $7.3 million, and net cash burn fell 29% sequentially to $5.6 million, the first quarter revenue exceeded burn. Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $20-22 million and net cash burn at $26-28 million, while the low end of gross margin guidance was raised from 50% to 52.5% (range now 52.5%-55%). Management cited broad-based contributions across U.S. hospital, U.S. office, and international verticals with a record ASP and no one-time items.

Q3 consolidated revenue was $1.03 billion, up 3.3% YoY and below guidance of up mid-single digits, with adjusted EBITDA of $170 million falling short of the $180-220 million guided range. Multiplatform Group revenue of $562 million fell 4.9% versus guidance of approximately flat, and segment adjusted EBITDA dropped to $68 million from $119 million on non-cash co-marketing costs. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was reset to $550-600 million and free cash flow to approximately $50 million, with Q4 EBITDA guided to $135-185 million including roughly $100 million of net non-cash marketing headwind. Offsets were Digital Audio revenue up 13.8% to $389 million (podcasting up 24.6% to $174 million) and Audio & Media Services revenue up 22.6% to $82 million.

Ionis reported Q3 total revenue of $243 million (+55% YoY ex the prior-year $280M sapablursen payment), with commercial revenue of $136 million (+18%) driven by DAWNZERA product sales of $37 million (+~40% QoQ) and TRYNGOLZA sales of $9 million in its first full sHTG quarter. Management cut full-year TRYNGOLZA net product sales guidance to approximately $50 million, citing a more gradual launch ramp, while reiterating DAWNZERA guidance of $110-$120 million and total 2026 revenue of $875-$900 million, non-GAAP operating loss of $425-$475 million, and year-end cash above $1.6 billion. Cash flow break-even was pushed from 2028 to 2029, attributed to the TRYNGOLZA ramp plus Phase III disappointments in eplontersen (ATTR-CM) and pelacarsen (Lp(a)). Management kept its confidence in >$3 billion peak TRYNGOLZA sales and cited improving prescriber breadth, repeat prescribing, and 33% commercial formulary coverage to date.

Take-Two reported Q2 FY2027 net bookings of $1.6 billion, missing the guidance range of $1.62B-$1.67B, driven by a 9% decline in recurrent consumer spending (RCS) for NBA 2K and mobile titles. GAAP net revenue decreased 16% to $1.5 billion while operating expenses fell 9% due to lower user acquisition costs. Management reiterated full-year FY2027 net bookings guidance of $8B-$8.2B, citing extraordinary pre-orders for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI launch.

Kodiak reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $402 million, up 25% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $224.5 million (+29% YoY) and net income of $71.5 million ($0.70 per diluted share). Compression infrastructure revenue rose 7% with adjusted gross margin of 70% (up 170 bps YoY), while power infrastructure revenue grew 28% sequentially to $42 million at a 75% adjusted gross margin. Management raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $850 million, lifted the compression margin range to 69.5%-70.5%, and raised the low end of power margin guidance, though power growth CapEx was trimmed to $350-$400 million as some turbine deliveries slipped into 2027.

Roivant reported Q2 FY2026 (ended Sept 30) with $31M in net revenue from LISRAYA, reflecting strong initial demand five weeks post-approval but noting it is too early to extrapolate full trajectory. The company highlighted transformative clinical data for IMVT-1402 RA (Period 2), NIU, and Mosliciguat PH-ILD, while announcing a strategic decision not to progress in Sjögren's due to competitor futility. Financially, the quarter showed a net loss of $153M with cash at $4.2B following Moderna litigation receipts.

Net sales of $169.2 million in Q2 FY2027 were impacted by delayed customer orders and lower tariff pass-throughs, resulting in a significant miss against prior year results. Management revised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance downward to net sales of $715-$740 million from the previous $780-$800 million range due to these near-term dislocations. While management noted improving trends in October and secured nearly $60 million in new annualized business awards, the outlook remains constrained by inventory realignment issues and soft DIY demand.

Powerfleet reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $115.7 million (up 4% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $24.9 million, with margins improving to 21.5%. Management affirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $468M-$473M and adjusted EBITDA between $111M-$114M, citing strong recovery from a Q1 manufacturing constraint and ahead-of-schedule progress on the South African National Treasury contract.

Mesa Labs reported Q2 FY2027 revenues of $143.6 million (up 2.6% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $17.3 million (up 21.1% YoY), beating consensus estimates. Management provided full-year 2027 guidance for revenues of $250-$255 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $66-$68 million, representing a conservative outlook that accounts for a deliberate revenue decline in the Clinical Genomics segment and timing shifts in Biopharmaceutical Development. While Sterilization and Disinfection Control showed strong organic growth of 14.6%, the overall tone was cautious due to ongoing delivery reliability issues in one SDC product line and the strategic decision to restructure Clinical Genomics for profitability rather than scale.

First half net income was JPY 856.2 billion, driven by JPY 538.7 billion in KIOXIA sale and valuation gains and JPY 317.5 billion in adjusted profits. The company recorded JPY 30 billion in impairments on investees in Greater China and expects a JPY 190 billion loss from KIOXIA in Q3, keeping the full-year net income forecast unchanged at JPY 530 billion despite the volatile holding.

Roivant reported Q2 FY2026 (ended Sept 30) with $31 million in net revenue from the five-week commercial launch of LISRAYA for dermatomyositis, alongside strong Phase II data for IMVT-1402 in RA and mosliciguat in PH-ILD. The company posted a non-GAAP loss of $133 million and repurchased $280 million of stock, while cash returned to $4.2 billion following Moderna litigation receipts. Management expressed high confidence in the clinical data but noted that guidance for 2027 is not yet available pending FDA discussions on the RA program.

Total revenue decreased 43% year-over-year to JPY 75.5 billion ($480 million), driven by a 56% drop in marketplace trading volume and a 26% decline in customer assets due to crypto price drops. The company reported a net loss of JPY 4.14 billion ($26.3 million) and an adjusted EBITDA loss of JPY 4,020 million ($25.6 million), primarily impacted by a JPY 2,962 million impairment loss on the Aplo subsidiary. Management outlined a strategic pivot to optimize core operations for cash generation while winding down Aplo in Europe.

Digital Turbine reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $179 million, up 27% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA growing 46% to $39.8 million. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance by $20 million to a range of $670-$690 million while reaffirming the EBITDA outlook. The beat was driven by strong growth in both On-Device Solutions (ODS) and App Growth Platform (AGP) segments, with ODS international revenue expanding 50% year-over-year.

KKR reported record results for a second consecutive quarter: FRE per share of $1.42 (+24% YoY), total operating earnings per share of $1.88 (+21%), and adjusted net income per share of $1.78 (+26%), with FRE margin near 71%, the highest in company history. Management fees were $1.2 billion and grew 16% YoY ex catch-up fees, while capital markets fees of $290 million were the third-highest on record. Guidance was reiterated rather than raised: strategic holdings operating earnings of more than $350 million for 2026 and $1.1 billion by 2030, plus an expectation of a third consecutive record ANI-per-share quarter in Q4, aided by the USI sale (~$3.3 billion after-tax proceeds, ~$2 billion ANI). Other notable items include $25 billion of Q3 fundraising, $20 billion deployed, $146 billion of dry powder, and $567 million of buybacks from early Q3 through November 4.

Kaltura reported record Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $47.3M (+8% YoY) and subscription revenue of $45.9M (+9% YoY), beating the high end of guidance for revenue, subscription revenue, and Adjusted EBITDA ($6.0M, 13% margin, +325 bps YoY). It raised full-year guidance for the third time this year, now expecting total revenue of $185-185.7M (+2-3%) and Adjusted EBITDA of $19.5-20.5M, which exceeds 2025's $18.6M. However, Q4 guidance implies a sharp deceleration to just 1-3% total revenue growth, and M&T segment revenue fell 10% YoY with elevated gross churn expected to persist into Q4. Bookings more than doubled sequentially (strongest since 2024) and the AI-related pipeline grew over 40% to ~$24M potential ACV.

Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% YoY to $26.7 million on revenue of $79.5 million, down from $83.4 million a year earlier; nine-month revenue fell about 5% to $236.3 million. RNG production grew 5% YoY to 1.3 million MMBtu, but management now expects full-year RNG production modestly below its prior guidance range and only expects to meet the low end of Adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing continued D3/D4 RIN price volatility. Fuel Station Services Adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $13 million with volumes up 3% to 40 million GGEs; Q4 is guided to resemble Q3 or slightly higher, with 2027 production guidance deferred and only directional double-digit EBITDA commentary given. Jon Maurer announced retirement as Co-CEO effective March 31, 2027.

Sable reported its second full quarter of oil sales with revenue up 13% QoQ and volumes sold up nearly 30% QoQ, but its sole crude purchaser cut purchases in early October, leaving roughly 900,000 barrels of October production unsold and forcing the company to remarkarket crude to three additional LA refiners. Q4 sales guidance of 20,000-30,000 bpd excludes the proposed 1.3 million barrel bulk crude sale, which management hopes to close in November; with about $38 million of cash, $165-175 million of Q4 cash spend including ~$53 million of Dec 31 amortization/interest, management flagged the $100 million unsecured loan basket and a potential PIPE as liquidity backstops. Platform Hondo restart is targeted for the week after Thanksgiving with full 15-well ramp in December, and management expects differentials to hold near current levels with no improvement until term contracts are negotiated.

Revenue fell 31% YoY to $20.5 million from $29.8 million, and the company swung to a GAAP net loss of $3.8 million versus net income of $6.9 million a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $2.4 million from $11.9 million, with $2.3 million of one-off items (a $1.3 million disallowed tax credit write-off and $1 million of out-of-period compensation) plus margin compression from lower ad revenue. Management expects only a small margin improvement in Q4 on better monetization, and explicitly said it has seen no material traffic recovery. Offsets cited include blended RPM up 15% month-over-month to $28.99 in September and content production up 15% sequentially, driven by InfoSentience and Cutter Studios, neither yet material to revenue.

The Trade Desk reported Q3 revenue of $736 million, down 0.5% year-over-year, but meaningfully ahead of its August outlook, including a roughly 3-point one-time benefit from a strategic partner; adjusted EBITDA was $266 million at a 36% margin. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.08 and adjusted EPS $0.33, with free cash flow of $153 million. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of at least $755 million and adjusted EBITDA of at least $280 million, with management signaling it does not expect the normal seasonal Q3-to-Q4 uplift. The company also outlined a roughly 15% workforce reduction producing about $100 million in 2027 gross savings and flagged a one-time $44 million restructuring charge.

Q3 FY2026 U.S. BRIUMVI net revenue was $233M (up 52% YoY), total net product revenue $240M and total revenue ~$260M (up 61% YoY), EPS $0.35 diluted, with operating income $86M vs $29M in Q3 last year. U.S. BRIUMVI guidance was raised to $915M-$920M from $890M-$905M, and full-year global revenue guidance to approximately $1B. Gross margin held steady (87% U.S. product, ~84% consolidated), and the company repurchased $100M of stock (~2M shares at ~$49). Spending guidance was unchanged at $450M-$500M, and BRIUMVI grew sequentially for the 14th straight quarter.

Target reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 30% YoY to ~$129M and adjusted EBITDA up 59% to ~$34M, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding ~480 bps to 27%. WHS revenue rose 116% to ~$80M on utilized beds above 6,200, while HFS-South contributed ~$33M and Government ~$14M against a prior-year $12M PCC closeout. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $435-445M revenue and $105-115M adjusted EBITDA and reiterated an exit-2027 run rate above $750M revenue and $300M EBITDA, based entirely on contracted minimum take-or-pay revenue. Since January the company has secured over $1.7B in multi-year awards (10,000+ beds), and the actionable pipeline rose to 25,000 beds from 20,000.

Turkcell reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of TRY 82 billion, up 6.2% year-on-year in real terms, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 44.2% from 43.9% a year earlier and net income of TRY 6.7 billion. Management reaffirmed full-year real revenue growth and EBITDA margin guidance, with operational CapEx at 22.2% of sales versus a 25% full-year target. Digital Business Services revenue rose 65% to TRY 10.5 billion on large project renewals, but management flagged a slower Data Center and cloud trajectory due to RAM and memory supply constraints delaying enterprise demand. The main negative was the Data Center/cloud slowdown and higher FX losses, while positives included 701,000 postpaid net adds, churn down to 1.6% from 2.6%, and margin expansion despite lower-margin hardware and POS mix.

Q3 FY2026 revenue of $55.2M grew 7% YoY and exceeded the guidance range of $49.2M-$50.6M, driven by stronger Telos ID performance. Adjusted EBITDA of $10.6M topped guidance of $6M-$6.8M at a 19.2% margin, the highest since the 2020 IPO, with cash gross margin of 43.1%. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $198.2M-$200.7M (from $187M-$200M) and Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised sharply to $32.3M-$34.1M (from $20.6M-$28M). Management also flagged a $32M 2027 revenue headwind from the phase-out of low-margin third-party software resale, partly offset by $58M of new Xacta bookings expected to produce $20M of 2027 revenue.

Total net product revenue was ~$17.2M vs $3.3M a year ago, including ~$15M of TONMYA sales, up 37% QoQ, with TONMYA prescriptions of 16,375 up 28% QoQ. R&D rose to $25.8M from $9.3M and SG&A to $45.6M from $25.7M, leaving cash of $162.8M versus $207.6M at year-end 2025 and runway guided only into early Q3 2027. Management said Q4 trends have continued post the September 1 sales-force expansion to 150 reps, but gave no formal revenue guidance, and disclosed an October 1 Paragraph IV ANDA filing from Dr. Reddy's that it will litigate, with core patents running to 2034. No EPS figures or explicit numeric guidance were provided on the call.

Net sales rose 27% YoY to $151M, driven by Modern Oral net sales up 103% to $74M (gross sales +114% to $94M), with Modern Oral at 49% of consolidated net sales versus 31% a year ago. However, adjusted EBITDA fell 41% YoY to $18M on higher sales and marketing investment, and Stoker's gross margin contracted 416 bps to 56%. Zig-Zag net sales declined 15% YoY to $37M. Management reiterated the September 21 full-year outlook: Modern Oral gross sales $330-350M, net sales $260-270M, and adjusted EBITDA $70-80M, unchanged.

Trevi reported Q3 2026 cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $299 million with a runway extending into 2030, funding IPF and non-IPF ILD programs through key data and the LAKE trial; no revenue, EPS or margin figures were discussed as the company is pre-commercial. The company aligned with the FDA on a ~120-patient phase II dose-ranging study in non-IPF ILD, planned to start Q1 2027 with top-line data in H1 2028, and reconfirmed OCEAN-1/OCEAN-2 guidance for H2 2027 and H1 2028. LAKE SSRE results are now expected in early Q1 2027 versus a prior December timeframe, which management attributed to holiday timing, with full LAKE results still guided to H2 2027. A new patent on dosing in hepatically impaired patients and non-IPF ILD extends protection to 2041.

Uniti reported Q3 FY2026 revenue at the midpoint of guidance, but pro forma consolidated revenue and Adjusted EBITDA fell 10% and 22% year-over-year respectively, driven by legacy copper/TDM declines, higher DSL churn, and a one-time TDM conversion charge. Full-year 2026 consolidated revenue guidance was reiterated at approximately $3.68 billion (with a slight increase from Fiber Infrastructure), while Kinetic revenue and contribution margin guidance was reduced to $2.11 billion and $855 million due to higher DSL churn and lower fiber ARPU. The company raised its generative AI opportunity estimates, with upfront payments, one-time cash revenue, and recurring annual cash revenue expected 36%, 33%, and 90% higher than prior estimates, and noted record fiber net adds and passings at Kinetic.

ZipRecruiter reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $124.4 million, an 8% year-over-year increase that landed at the top end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $20.8 million with a 17% margin, representing a 9 percentage point expansion year-over-year and exceeding expectations. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to 4%-5% growth, citing record engagement metrics driven by AI integrations and product improvements.

Revenue was $3 million, down quarter-over-quarter from raw material shortages (dysprosium oxide, samarium metal) that limited LCM and Stillwater output; gross margin was pressured by higher input costs. GAAP net income of $12 million was driven by a $137 million non-cash warrant/earnout fair value gain, while adjusted net loss was $126 million, or $0.44 per share, on operating expenses of ~$121 million including ~$60 million of M&A/legal costs. Cash was $1.2 billion after $190 million net paid for Serra Verde, $148 million operating cash use, and $106 million capex. Q4 guidance is at least 325 tons of TREO from Serra Verde, with 2027 targets of 4,000 tpa TREO stage 1 steady state in Q2 and 6,400 tpa by year-end; the prior $550-650 million EBITDA run-rate target was not reaffirmed.

Q3 consolidated net sales were $66.9 million, level with Q3 last year and up 5% sequentially, with record cannabis sales of $55 million (up 3%). Gross margin fell to 44% from 48%, cannabis gross margin to 48% from 55%, and adjusted EBITDA was $18.2 million versus a record $20.7 million last year, though up 18% sequentially; net income was $10 million or $0.08 per share versus $10.8 million or $0.09. Drivers were a roughly 75% year-over-year decline in spot Canadian trim pricing and a mix shift to bulk flower, partially offset by international exports up 75% to $20.8 million at unchanged EU GMP pricing. Management said trim pricing troughed in Q3 and expects normalization in Q4, Delta 2 and Groningen capacity ramps are on track for 2027, and no formal numeric guidance was provided.

Via reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $144 million, up 31% YoY, with an adjusted gross margin of 40.5% (up from 39.6%) and an adjusted EBITDA margin of -2%, versus -8% a year ago. Adjusted EPS rounded to break-even against a $0.37 loss in Q3 FY2025, and customers reached 868 (+22%) with pipeline more than doubling YoY. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $556.7-558.4 million (28.2-28.6% growth) and guided Q4 to $150-151.7 million with the first positive adjusted EBITDA of $0-1.5 million; Q4 growth of 26.1-27.6% decelerates from Q3's 31%, and Germany was roughly flat at $18.4 million.

Virtus reported Q3 FY2026 AUM of $141.4B, down 7% sequentially on $6.1B of net outflows (worse than Q2's $5.6B) and $4.3B of negative markets; total sales fell to $4.3B from $6.1B. Adjusted EPS rose to $5.86 from $5.54 and the adjusted operating margin improved to 28.7% from 26.1% (up 50 bps normalized), helped by lower employment expense. The quarter was dominated by continued quality-equity outflows, including a disclosed $7B institutional redemption (sub-average fee rate) that transitions in mid-October; management guided Q4 employment expense ratio up to 54%-56% on lower average assets. Offsets include 2% dividend increase to $2.45, $10M of buybacks, debt paydown, and improving equity relative performance (58% of equity assets top-half vs 22% prior quarter).

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $362.8 million, within the $358-368 million guidance range, down 4.0% reported but up 0.2% constant currency; Adjusted EBITDA was $2.2 million, near the $0-5 million midpoint. Gross margin expanded 3.6 points to 25.5%, operating loss narrowed to $9.2 million and GAAP loss per share improved to $0.06, but Japan revenue fell 18% and global MPU dropped 3.1%. Q4 guidance calls for 9-12% constant-currency revenue growth ($371-381 million, ~10.5% midpoint) and Adjusted EBITDA of $0-5 million, with only a small RI Games contribution and a timing shift of IP revenue from Q3 into Q4. Management reiterated double-digit growth exiting the year, driven by Korea, advertising and recovering Japan paid content, while flagging continued Japan and Rest-of-World paid content softness.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $123.1 million including $110.4 million of exome/genome revenue, adjusted gross margin expanded to 72% from 70% in Q2 and 69% in Q1, adjusted net income swung to $8.6 million from near break-even in Q2, and blended average reimbursement rate rose 5% sequentially to $3,436. Full-year revenue guidance of $475-490 million was reaffirmed but now expected at the low end, while adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to approximately 71% and adjusted net income to at least $12 million. However, full-year exome/genome volume growth was cut to at least 28% and exome/genome revenue growth to at least 17%, reflecting deliberate upfront documentation controls that created a near-term volume headwind. Q4 guidance calls for at least $135 million total revenue and approximately $12 million adjusted net income, and management quantified a mid-single-digit PAMA headwind to 2027 revenue that it expects RCM improvements to more than offset.

Select reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $412 million, net income of $23 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $93.5 million, at the high end of the $90-$94 million guidance range, with record Water Infrastructure revenue of $110 million (+40% YoY) on produced water volumes of 1.7 MMbpd (+14% QoQ, >30% YoY). YTD Adjusted EBITDA of $264 million already surpassed the full-year 2025 record, and management expects to exceed the high end of its 25%-30% annual growth guidance before any Pilot Water contribution. Q4 EBITDA is guided to $95-$100 million, as a partial Pilot Water contribution offsets the full-quarter loss of Peak Rentals (~$7-$10 million EBITDA impact) and seasonality; Pilot is expected to finish 2026 at $250-$270 million revenue and $100-$110 million EBITDA, progressing toward a $120-$130 million 2027 outlook. The company closed the $900 million eight-year 7.5%-8% senior notes offering and a new $500 million undrawn revolver, with pro forma leverage near 2x net debt to Adjusted EBITDA.

Sohu's Q3 FY2026 total revenue fell 26% YoY to $133 million, with online game revenue down 30% YoY to $114 million and marketing services up 10% YoY to $15 million; GAAP and non-GAAP net loss attributable to Sohu.com Limited was $15 million versus net income of $9 million a year ago. Q4 guidance points to continued softness: marketing services of $30-40 million implies an 18-24% YoY decline and a 6-13% sequential decline, while online game revenue of $111-121 million implies an 8% decline to 1% growth YoY and a 3% decline to 6% growth sequentially, with a guided net loss of $17-27 million. Management attributed the Q4 advertising softness to project timing shifting into Q3 and a less robust Double 11 e-commerce event, and said it has no new buyback program planned after the current $150 million program, of which $134 million had been used as of November 5, 2026.

First call after the Paramount/WBD combination closed. Standalone Paramount Q3: revenue +5% YoY, Paramount+ revenue +21%, $1 billion adjusted EBITDA above the top end of guidance, and full-year Paramount standalone guidance maintained at the high end ($3.9 billion adjusted EBITDA). Warner Bros. film slate underperformance creates a $200 million Q4 adjusted EBITDA headwind, and the company is moving to annual guidance with 2027 outlook deferred to next quarter. Management reiterated the $6 billion synergy program (30% run-rate by end-2027, 70% by end-2028), $4 billion cost to achieve, medium-term targets of mid-single-digit revenue growth, mid-20% adjusted EBITDA margins and $10 billion FCF in 2030, and expects to be free cash flow break-even or better in 2027.

Paysign reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $30.8 million, up 42.6% year-over-year, with GAAP net income of $6.7 million ($0.11 per diluted share) and Adjusted EBITDA of $11.0 million (35.7% margin). Gross margin expanded to 64.7% from 56.3%, and operating margin more than tripled to 23.8% from 7.3%, driven by patient affordability revenue doubling to $16.6 million on ~55% higher claim volume. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was maintained at $114-$117 million, while margin, net income, and Adjusted EBITDA outlooks were raised even after absorbing a plasma customer transition of 113 centers expected to cut Q4 revenue by $1.5 million and gross profit by $700,000.

RB Global reported Q3 FY2026 total GTV of $4.7 billion, up 20% (about 14% organic), service revenue up 10%, adjusted EBITDA up 13%, and adjusted EPS up 11%. Service revenue take rate fell 186 bps to 19.8%, with management attributing most of the decline (130 bps) to strategic portfolio expansion (GSA, BigIron, acquisitions). The company raised its 2026 outlook to 14-15% GTV growth and 9.7% adjusted EBITDA growth at the midpoint, and repurchased $350 million of shares in the quarter.

Q3 revenue was ~$396 million, up 15% YoY from $345 million, and Adjusted EBITDA was $21 million versus a $46 million loss in the prior-year quarter, with YTD Adjusted EBITDA of $101 million. However, roughly $12 million of the quarter's EBITDA came from a ~$7 million favorable 2025 CMS ACO reconciliation and ~$5 million non-cash ACO JV liability release, leaving underlying Q3 Adjusted EBITDA near $10 million. Management raised the low end of FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance from $80 million to $90 million and lifted the midpoint from $95 million to $100 million (range $90-110 million), while flagging a Q3 step-up in medical expense (notably outpatient/professional, concentrated in Nevada) and a medical loss ratio of ~90.6%. At-risk membership fell to ~105,000 from ~116,000 a year ago due to deliberate portfolio exits, and cash stood at ~$44 million.

Plug reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$201 million, up ~13% YoY and ~13% QoQ, with gross margin of -2.7% versus -68% a year ago but slightly below Q2. GAAP EPS of ~$0.07 was driven entirely by ~$192 million of non-cash mark-to-market gains on convertible notes and warrants; excluding those, the company reported a net loss, though smaller than a year ago. Net cash usage fell to a record-low ~$28 million from $61 million in Q2, with no capital raised. Full-year revenue growth guidance of 15%-16% was reaffirmed (not raised), implying ~$280 million of Q4 revenue, and management targets positive EBITDAS in Q4 with net cash usage roughly flat, but excluded any Stream asset-sale proceeds from the Q4 forecast.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 13.2% to $55.2 million with organic growth of 5.1%, up from 3.9% in Q2. Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.1% to $12.8 million at a 23.2% margin, down from 23.6% a year ago on higher holdco costs, while adjusted EPS fell to $0.33 from $0.36 on an 18% larger diluted share count. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed at $213-216 million revenue and $48.5-50.5 million adjusted EBITDA, unchanged from the raise last quarter, with no lift from the Reevemark acquisition. Government relations grew 7.5% organically while CCPA fell 1% year-to-date ahead of the election.

PubMatic reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17... no, actually revenue grew 17% YoY with adjusted EBITDA more than doubling to $26 million (33% margin vs 16% a year ago), and GAAP net income of $5.5 million ($0.11/diluted share). Gross margin reached nearly 70% versus 63%, aided by 5 points of operational improvement plus 2 points from a server useful-life change. Q4 guidance is $91-93 million (15% growth at midpoint) and full-year revenue $312-314 million (11% growth), with Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $31-33 million and full-year $79-81 million (up 30%); CapEx guidance was raised to $24-28 million. Growth accelerated for a third consecutive quarter, but management flagged a stable-not-growing legacy DSP relationship and prudence embedded in the Q4 outlook around political pacing.

Qualys reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $188 million, up 11% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.12, Adjusted EBITDA of $89.9 million (48% margin vs 49% last year), and free cash flow of $100 million (53.2% margin). Full-year revenue guidance was nudged up to $736.9-738.9 million from $732-738 million, and EPS guidance was raised materially to $8.07-8.14 from $7.74-7.88. Current billings grew 14% following 16% in Q2, but management guided Q4 calculated current billings to about 8% and framed the recent beats as driven by a strong federal quarter rather than a durable acceleration. Net dollar expansion was unchanged at 105%, and direct revenue declined 2%.

Q3 2026 revenue was $35.0 million, up 6.3% sequentially but down 13.1% year-over-year from $40.2 million (down 8.6% pro forma excluding a terminated diagnostics program and Akoya pre-acquisition revenue). Non-GAAP gross margin improved 150 bps to 47.4%, but adjusted EBITDA was a $12.2 million loss and cash usage was $16.2 million, ending at $80.7 million with no debt. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to approximately $142-$146 million, with non-GAAP gross margin of 48%-50% and year-end cash of about $70 million; the Q4 midpoint implies roughly $40 million. Management framed the sequential improvement, near-record spatial consumables, roughly 2x Accelerator book-to-bill, and doubled LucentAD test volume as early signs of a turnaround, while citing continued academic and pharma market softness.

QCi reported record Q3 revenue of $9.5 million, up from $384,000 a year ago and exceeding the $9.2 million generated in all of the first half of 2026, driven mainly by acquired photonics products for aerospace, government and industrial customers. Gross profit was only $428,000 for a 4.5% gross margin, while operating expenses rose to $29 million from $10.5 million, producing a net loss of $15.1 million or $0.07 per share versus prior-year net income of $2.4 million. Management gave no formal guidance, citing order timing lumpiness, but said it expects a strong year-end finish, a solid backlog entering 2027, and backlog of $39.1 million (down slightly from Q2) that should largely convert within 12-18 months. Cash and investments totaled roughly $1.3 billion, with Fab 2 spending of $70-80 million planned through mid-2027.

RadNet reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $638.3 million, up 22.1% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $105 million, up 23.8%, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.30 vs $0.24 a year ago. The company raised 2026 imaging center guidance for revenue (+ $15 million at both ends to $2.385-2.435 billion), adjusted EBITDA (+ $5 million to $350-363 million), and free cash flow (+ $5 million to $120-130 million), citing outperformance in each of the first three quarters. Digital Health revenue grew 32.6% to $32.9 million with ARR of $112.6 million, up 67%, though segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.0 million from $3.5 million on integration investment and Gleamer dilution. The main negative was the final 2027 Medicare rule, which management estimates will reduce 2027 revenue by about $5 million, worse than the previously expected sub-$1 million impact.

SIGA reported zero product sales in the third quarter, a net loss of about $3 million and a diluted loss per share of $0.04, versus net income of about $6 million and $0.09 per share for the nine-month period, which included roughly $42 million of product revenue ($26 million IV TPOXX to the SNS, $13 million international) mostly booked in Q2. Q3 revenue was limited to about $1 million of R&D revenue, and the company gave no firm timeline for a new U.S. government procurement contract, saying only that an award remains uncertain in timing and details but is still expected. The pediatric Phase I readout is still expected by year-end, but the PEP supplemental NDA filing has slipped to 2028 after FDA requested additional validation work. A new CDND contract worth up to about $15 million ($9 million firm over three years) adds international revenue starting 2027, and the balance sheet holds $116 million in cash with no debt.

Rocket Lab reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $267.8 million, up 73% YoY and above the $250-265 million guidance range, with GAAP gross margin of 33.6% and non-GAAP 38.4% also above guidance. Backlog rose 52% sequentially to roughly $3.6 billion (117 launches, 55+ spacecraft), driven by $1 billion-plus in launch bookings and eight Neutron missions at a new $70 million base price. Q4 guidance calls for $270-290 million revenue, GAAP gross margin of 34-36% and non-GAAP 39-41%, with adjusted EBITDA loss improving to $14-20 million. Offsets include a Neutron first-launch slip to 2027 after propellant tank voids, a wider GAAP loss of $0.12 per share versus $0.08 prior quarter, elevated operating expenses and a $2.4 billion ATM raise to fund the pending Iridium acquisition.

Total Q3 revenue was $153.4M, up 97% YoY with a full KUBRA quarter, 13.6% organic including ~9 points from political media and ~5% normalized organic ex-political. KUBRA contributed ~$65M, up ~8% pro forma (accelerating from 6% in Q2), and cost synergy run-rate exiting 2026 was raised to $11M from $8M, while political media guidance rose to $16M-$18M from $8M-$10M. Offset by core consumer payments organic growth of only 0.3% and a cut to normalized organic growth guidance to 5%-6% from 7%-9%, plus a free cash flow target reduction (30% to 20%-25% unadjusted; 35% to 25%-30% adjusted) tied to a $14M bank channel investment and $5M expected in Q4. Full-year revenue of $490M-$500M and adjusted EBITDA of $168.5M-$176M were reiterated, and free cash flow was -$21.1M; adjusted EPS was $0.25.

Revenue rose to $13.5M from $10.8M a year ago, with staking revenue up 27% to $13.1M, and net income jumped to $751.4M from $104.3M on a $676.7M unrealized ETH gain and $75.2M of realized gains. Results were driven mostly by ETH appreciating about 72% in the quarter, from roughly $1,563 to $2,681, rather than by operations; SG&A fell to $11M from $12M after $3.1M of asset manager fees were eliminated. ETH holdings reached 895,117 as of November 2, cash was $47.9M versus $28.5M at year-end 2025, and no shares were issued through the ATM during the quarter. Management gave no numeric guidance, framing priorities around growing ETH per share, treasury deployment, and ecosystem investment.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $18.6 million, up 29% sequentially but only 13% year-over-year, with nine-month revenue a record $52.5 million (+15%). Tokenization revenue rose 29% to $11.5 million while asset servicing fell 6% to $7.2 million on lower AUA, and Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to about $2 million from $5.5 million in the prior quarter, though GAAP net loss was $66.3 million ($0.41/diluted share), roughly $60 million of it non-cash business-combination charges. No explicit forward revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; management framed funds as the near-term revenue driver and tokenized equities as a mid-to-long-term opportunity, and announced a planned River One acquisition plus a $50 million buyback through 2027. Q2 revenue had come in below expectations, so the sequential recovery is the most important change versus the prior period.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $19.6 million, up ~140% YoY and a new record, with U.S. revenue up ~160% to $16.8 million and OUS up ~65% to $2.8 million. Gross margin expanded to ~62% from ~43% a year ago, though SG&A nearly doubled to $32.3 million and net loss widened to $32.7 million ($0.50 per share) from $19.5 million. Full-year revenue guidance was raised for the third time this year to $68-$70 million from $62-$66 million, gross margin outlook updated to north of 60%, while opex guidance was nudged slightly above the prior $150-$160 million range and cash utilization at the high end (~$120 million). Management stated it will be a $100 million company next year, with Beta Bionics pump launch expected in coming weeks and Freedom targeted for a 2028 launch.

SGC reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $146 million, up 5% YoY, accelerating from 3% in Q2, with EPS of $0.17, down slightly YoY. Branded Products grew 8% to $92 million with EBITDA up 31% and gross margin up 160 bps, and Contact Centers grew 7% to $24 million with EBITDA up 22%, but Healthcare Apparel revenue fell 3% to $31 million amid a $4 million inventory write-down, a $1 million credit loss charge, and a 580 bps gross margin decline. Consolidated EBITDA fell to $6.7 million from $7.5 million, offset by lower interest expense on $25 million less average debt and $31 million YTD operating cash flow versus $1 million prior year. The full-year outlook was tightened upward at the low end for sales to $578-585 million (from $572-585 million) and adjusted EPS to $0.60-0.66 (from $0.54-0.66), and the $27 million Select VoiceCom acquisition closed, expected accretive in Q1 2027.

Somnigroup reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.4 billion, record adjusted EBITDA of $448 million, and record adjusted EPS of $1.04, up 10% YoY, though results were 'a bit below our expectations' due to a cautious consumer and an unexpected ERP disruption at Dreams. Tempur Sealy North America like-for-like sales fell 4%, Mattress Firm same-store sales declined 2% and reported sales fell 6%, and Leggett's full-quarter like-for-like sales were $973 million. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $2.85-$2.95 on a sales midpoint of approximately $8.65 billion, with the global bedding industry now expected down mid-single digits in the back half. The Dreams ERP issue cost approximately $50 million in sales and $25 million in adjusted EBITDA, partly offset by $20 million in tariff refunds and $25 million in Mattress Firm synergies.

OraSure reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $30.9 million, up 14% year-over-year and about 1% sequentially, with GAAP gross margin up 173 bps to 45.2% (non-GAAP 45.9%) and GAAP operating loss of $13.0 million (non-GAAP operating loss $10.2 million). Q4 guidance is $30-32 million, implying full-year revenue of $119.5-121.5 million and 3.8-5.6% growth at a 4.7% midpoint. The key negative change is that management pushed its cash flow from operations breakeven target from entering 2027 to the second half of 2027, citing the CT/NG submission withdrawal and slower-than-expected Ebola ordering timing. Management said 2027 revenue growth should accelerate over 2026 but deferred detailed 2027 guidance to the Q4 call.

Q3 FY2026 revenue grew 49% YoY to $890M, the second straight quarter of acceleration, though the figure excluded $18M of deferred weight-loss membership revenue to be recognized in Q4. Subscribers rose 13% YoY to 2.8M but fell a net 100,000 sequentially as management deliberately paced domestic weight-loss marketing; GAAP net loss was $33M while adjusted EBITDA rose 37% QoQ to $82M (9% margin) and gross margin fell ~7 points QoQ to 57% on branded international weight-loss mix. Domestic revenue grew 21% YoY to $657M and international revenue more than quadrupled to $233M, including ~$135M from Eucalyptus. Management framed the marketing pullback as trading near-term subscribers for a stronger Q4/Q1 setup around the Lilly and Novo assortment expansions, CagriSema, multi-month subscriptions, and brand consolidation in the U.K., Germany, and Australia, saying benefits would begin to appear in Q1.

GSL's Q3 FY2026 call emphasized strategic and balance-sheet progress rather than quarterly P&L, with no revenue, EPS or margin figures disclosed; the hard numbers given were $636 million of cash ($141 million restricted) and contracted revenues of $3.4 billion over an average 3.5 years. Management raised the supplemental dividend 25%, lifting the annualized dividend to $2.75 per share, and detailed 17 newbuild orders (15 chartered ex-yard for an average 7.1 years, expected to generate over $1 billion of adjusted EBITDA against a $1.33 billion cost) plus a $1 billion seven-year syndicated facility at SOFR+1.5%. Charter coverage stands at 100% for 2026, 98% for 2027 and 74% for 2028, with four vessel sales agreed for an anticipated ~$33 million gain. The main change versus prior periods is the newbuild-led fleet renewal and the third increase to the supplemental dividend.

Clearway reported Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $435 million and CAFD of $173 million, with YTD Adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion and YTD CAFD of $410 million; management called execution solid and maintained the 2026 CAFD guidance of $430-$470 million that was revised downward last quarter. The company initiated 2027 CAFD guidance of $520-$590 million (midpoint $2.70/share) and rolled forward a 2031 CAFD/share target of $3.20-$3.40, representing 7%-8%+ CAGR from 2025. Growth visibility expanded with the identified investment pipeline up 27% QoQ to ~6.4 GW and ~$4.1 billion of 2026-2030 corporate capital planned. No hard beat versus prior guidance was disclosed; the quarter tracked in line with revised expectations.

Revenue rose 25.6% YoY to $302.3 million with colocation up 26.7%, and adjusted EBITDA grew 44.3% to $132.1 million as margin expanded to 47.8% from 40.5%. Annualized bookings reached a record $66.1 million (14th straight sequential gain) and annualized revenue backlog jumped to roughly $114 million from $76 million, with about $104 million commencing in the next 12 months. Full-year guidance was set at $1.14-1.16 billion revenue and $490-500 million adjusted EBITDA; renewal spreads hit ~17% (vs ~8% normalized), but the GAAP net loss widened to $88.1 million on ~$58.6 million of IPO-related costs and net leverage stands at ~8.4x against a 6x-7x target.

Cannae reported Q3 FY2026 total operating revenues of $68 million versus $81 million prior year, with the decline driven primarily by the $10 million revenue loss from the Brasada Ranch sale; operating expenses rose to $95 million from $89 million, including $18 million of mostly restaurant-group goodwill impairments. Holding company expenses fell to $7 million in the quarter from $9 million, and are down 70% or $59 million year-to-date to $25 million, with roughly $3 million of additional annualized savings identified. Black Knight Football revenue grew 34% to $118 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, but EBITDA fell to $11.6 million from $95.7 million on lower player-trading profit ($5 million vs $80 million); adjusted EBITDA excluding player trading was $6.6 million versus $15.8 million. The company returned $54 million to shareholders in the quarter ($131 million year-to-date, including 7.7 million shares repurchased), closed the Watkins and Brasada sales, wound down O'Charley's for an expected ~$16 million annual cash savings, and said the 99 restaurant transaction remains unresolved and delayed.

Consolidated revenue fell 1% YoY to $4.4B, with ag net sales down 2% to ~$2.9B and construction up 5% to $777M. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.16 and adjusted net income $205M, aided by $71M of net IEEPA tariff refunds ($32M ag, $39M construction); ag adjusted EBIT margin rose to 6.0% from 4.6% but slips to 4.8% excluding refunds. Full-year ag sales guidance is unchanged at roughly flat with EBIT margin narrowed to 5.1%-5.4%, construction sales raised to up 8%-10%, industrial FCF raised to $300-450M and EPS to $0.44-$0.48. Separately, CNH agreed to watch 70% of its construction business to Kobelco at a $1B enterprise value (~10x adjusted EBITDA), with $700M cash to reduce debt and a 30% retained stake, closing by end-2027.

Q3 FY2026 LOQTORZI net sales were $14 million, up 3% QoQ and 25% YoY, falling short of the company's previously stated 10%-15% sequential growth target, and full-year LOQTORZI revenue guidance was cut to $54 million-$57 million from prior expectations. Cash used in operations was $34 million, down 43% from the H1 2026 quarterly average, with $83.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, and the 10-Q included going concern disclosures with runway stated as less than 12 months. The company announced a ~30% headcount reduction (about 140 to 100 FTEs) delivering $6 million-$7 million per quarter in savings, lowering the LOQTORZI revenue needed to cover core burn from $30 million-$35 million to $25 million-$30 million per quarter. Management reaffirmed a $15 million LOQTORZI quarter in Q4 and detailed a strategic pivot to esophageal cancer for tagmokitug, with 33.3% confirmed ORR in second-line and 89% ORR in first-line ESCC, plus plans to engage a financial advisor for ex-U.S. partnering.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 2% YoY to $29.1 million, with licensing up 2% to $16.3 million and royalties up 3% YoY (18% sequentially) to $12.7 million, but licensing came in below management's expectation because a significant multi-year connectivity deal slipped from Q3 into early Q4. Non-GAAP EPS rose 18% YoY to $0.13 on an 18% sequential increase in non-GAAP net income, while GAAP gross margin fell to 85% from 88% and non-GAAP operating income declined to $2.5 million from $3.1 million. Management guided Q4 revenue to $34-38 million (~24% sequential growth at the midpoint, the highest quarterly revenue in company history) and trimmed full-year non-GAAP expense growth to ~7% from ~8%.

Constellation reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $5.19 and adjusted operating earnings of $5.06, $2.02 above Q3 of last year, driven by Calpine accretion, strong commercial performance and higher PJM capacity prices, partly offset by lower PTC revenue. Full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance was raised and narrowed to $12.50-$12.80, with the low end now equal to the top of the prior Q2 range and $0.50 above the top of original March guidance. The company disclosed roughly 4,560 MW of new long-term agreements signed since last quarter, bringing year-to-date contracting to over 8,500 MW into the 2040s, plus ~1,200 MW of uprates costing ~$4.3 billion and a conditional $5 billion DOE loan commitment. No explicit 2027-2028 figures were given; management deferred updated guidance to the year-end call.

Q3 revenue exceeded $404M, up 105% YoY (legacy CECO organic +30%), adjusted EBITDA $70.1M (+201%, 17.3% margin, +550 bps), and adjusted EPS $0.60 vs. $0.26. Orders were $778M (+234%), book-to-bill ~1.92x, backlog hit a record $2.19B (+205% YoY), and adjusted free cash flow was $154M, cutting net leverage to ~2.0x. Full-year 2026 revenue ($1.3–1.375B) and EBITDA ($200–225M) guidance was maintained, while FY orders were raised to $2.5B+ and FCF to ~100% of EBITDA. Initial 2027 guidance calls for ~$2.2B revenue and ~$500M adjusted EBITDA (~22.7% margin), with preliminary 2028 double-digit growth and ~23.5% margin.

B&W reported Q3 2026 revenue of $290.8 million, up 109% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $17.7 million (up $9.4 million), operating income of $13.8 million (up $3.4 million) and net income of $93.9 million (up $35.1 million, aided by warrant revaluation). Bookings were $228 million, up 112%, and backlog reached $2.5 billion, up 571%, with record parts and services bookings. Management reaffirmed the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA target of $80-$105 million and issued a new FY2027 target of $125-$140 million, which it described as intentionally conservative pending large bookings expected in Q4 2026 and early 2027. Gross margin was pressured by construction-heavy mix and a labor availability issue on one project expected to finish by year-end.

Total revenue fell 34.1% sequentially and 50.9% year-over-year to $2.9 billion, with GAAP net income of $44.1 million driven mainly by a $71.5 million unrealized mark-to-market gain, while adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $4.3 million versus a $13.5 million profit a year ago. Digital asset sales revenue dropped 52% YoY at a 15 bps margin, down from 20 bps a year ago, and staking revenue fell 24.1% YoY with the take rate down to 5.9% from 9.7%. No formal forward guidance was given; management framed the weakness as market-driven, cited improving operating efficiency and the NYDIG acquisition, and bought back about $25 million of stock.

Bakkt reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $149.2 million versus $402.2 million a year ago, with TTV of $147.9 million down from $168.8 million in Q2. GAAP net income was $14.3 million or $0.31 per diluted share, but that included a $26.8 million non-cash Transchem warrant gain; the operating loss was $14.4 million and adjusted EBITDA a loss of $11.8 million. Management reiterated its ~$3 billion full-year TTV target, implying ~$2.44 billion in Q4 against $557.9 million year to date, and set a new ~$6 billion H1 FY2027 TTV target, both resting on client activations that began in October. Management declined to provide a stabilized gross margin assumption, citing developing transaction economics.

Pre-revenue clinical-stage quarter with no product revenue or EPS; the news was operational. FORTIFI-HN01 reached 'substantial enrollment' to enable a top-line interim analysis still expected mid-2027, and management newly confirmed plans to include an interim overall survival analysis without giving timing, statistical details, or whether the trial needs upsizing (it says it does not). R&D rose to $56.5M from $33M and G&A to $19.2M from $7.7M, with cash of $442.3M funding runway into 1H 2029. Management acknowledged a peer's recent positive head and neck dataset as class validation while asserting depth and durability should differentiate FICERA's own OS profile.

Atea reported no product revenue as a clinical-stage company, with $191.2 million in cash and marketable securities as of September 30, 2026. The quarter's central event was the July C-BEYOND Phase III readout, where bemnifosbuvir/ruzasvir met its primary endpoint with 94% SVR vs 95% for SOF/VEL, within the pre-specified 5% non-inferiority margin, with comparable safety. Management guided to C-FORWARD top-line in early 2027, an NDA submission targeted for mid-2027, and Phase I HEV data early 2027, and announced a Hercules credit facility of up to $200 million with $65 million drawn at the November 6 close to fund operations into mid-2028. Management also cautioned that the Cassidy HCV elimination bill is unlikely to proceed in the new Congress and stated payer discussions have not yet begun pending approval.

AST SpaceMobile reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $42.3 million, driven by commercial gateway deliveries and U.S. government service milestones, and said results were consistent with internal plans and up sequentially and year-over-year. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200 million was reiterated, with management flagging potential upside from Q4 revenue opportunities and the J-LEO program. Non-GAAP adjusted opex excluding cost of revenue rose to $109.4 million from $95.9 million in Q2 (within the $105-115 million guide), while capex of ~$310 million came in below the $350-425 million guide on timing; cash and restricted cash exceeded $3.2 billion. The quarter's headline developments were strategic rather than financial: a ~$1 billion Japan J-LEO subsidy, a ~$100 million U.S. Space Force award, 100+ BlueBirds under launch agreements, and a new in-house Blacklift rocket with ~several hundred million dollars of incremental 2027 capex.

APEI beat guidance on every key metric in Q3 FY2026: revenue rose 3.6% to $169.1 million (above the $164.5M-$167M range), net income grew 6% to $5.9 million, diluted EPS rose 6.7% to $0.32, and Adjusted EBITDA of $17.5 million exceeded the $14M-$17M range. Q3 Adjusted EBITDA margin still fell to 10.4% from 12.7% and Military+ segment EBITDA margin fell to 27% from 32%, driven by ~$6 million of revenue shifted into Q4, higher watching and promotion spend (24.7% of revenue vs 22.1%), and bad debt tied to Title IV disbursement delays. The company raised full-year guidance on revenue ($695M-$701M), net income, Adjusted EBITDA ($98M-$105M), and diluted EPS ($2.59-$2.84), while Q4 Military+ registrations are guided up 21.7%-27.7% against a shutdown-hit prior year. Health+ revenue grew 9% to $86.4 million but still posted a $1.9 million operating loss, and the Online+ non-healthcare portion is declining.

Revenue rose 10% to $580M with project revenue up 9% to $446M, energy assets up 21% to $75M, and O&M up 20% to $37M. Gross margin expanded to 18.7%, above the 17%-18% guidance range, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.88 (down to $0.60 excluding full JV consolidation, versus $0.78 adjusted EBITDA pre-consolidation). New awards of $875M and $737M of contract conversions drove total backlog to nearly $7.2B, up ~40% YoY, with awarded backlog over $4.5B. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated only for HLBV/tax accounting and 100% JV consolidation, with management stating adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP EPS guidance would otherwise be unchanged.

AMG reported record Q3 FY2026 results with Adjusted EBITDA of $354 million, up 41% YoY, and Economic EPS of $9.50, up 56% YoY, driven by fee-related earnings and share repurchases. AUM reached a record $974 billion, up 3% QoQ, with net inflows of $21 billion, including record alternative inflows of over $31 billion. Q4 guidance calls for Adjusted EBITDA of $405-475 million and Economic EPS of $11.37-13.43, with full-year net performance fees of $145-205 million, in line with the five-year average. The company raised its full-year 2026 repurchase guidance to more than $900 million and reiterated 15-20% long-term Economic EPS growth, with 2026 growth expected at approximately 50%.

AMC Global Media reported consolidated revenue growth of just 1% in Q3 FY2026, with consolidated AOI of $70 million and free cash flow of -$52 million including an $85 million litigation settlement payment (positive $33 million excluding it). Domestic revenue rose 2% on 4% streaming growth (7% excl. ALLBLK) but affiliate revenue fell 11% and domestic advertising fell 7%; international revenue declined 5% to $73 million. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of $2.4-2.45 billion revenue and $410-420 million AOI, holding the range despite the ALLBLK divestiture, with free cash flow of approximately $150 million. Key changes: ALLBLK (600,000 subscribers) was sold to MACRO, and a $120 million Walking Dead settlement ($85 million paid in Q3, $35 million in January) was reached with no impact to adjusted operating income.

AlTi reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $58 million, up just 1% year over year, with recurring management and advisory fees of $55 million up 7% but investment distributions down 17%. Adjusted EBITDA was just over $6 million, up 1% YoY and 15% sequentially, at an 11% margin unchanged from the prior year, while a GAAP operating loss of $6 million and net loss of $11 million were reported. Operating expenses fell 25% YoY to $64 million on zero-based budgeting and an 8% headcount reduction over 12 months. Net wealth management outflows were about $250 million, and management flagged a further expected $20-23 million non-cash unrealized loss on the Zebedee stake in Q4; the special committee strategic review has nothing new to report.

Archer reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.1 million, which beat consensus on the first engine deliveries to Anduril for Omen, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $178.5 million at the low end of the $170M-$200M guided range. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $5M-$6M, up from Q3, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $185M-$205M. The quarter's key operational change was FAA issuance of a Market Survey Special Airworthiness Certificate for Midnight, enabling piloted CTOL operations in Los Angeles, while the Boeing/Wisk/SkyGrid/Insitu acquisition remains one approval short of closing.

Revenue was over $10M versus roughly $9M a year earlier, mostly research fees; R&D fell to about $44M (down ~$12M YoY) and SG&A dropped to $14M from $25M, narrowing the net loss to $41M, or $0.13 per share, from $57M. The quarter's centerpiece was positive Phase 2 ABCL635 VMS data (placebo-adjusted 50% reduction in hot flash frequency, 46% in severity at four weeks) and a $200M oversubscribed raise, lifting cash and marketable securities to over $790M, or over $890M with government funding. No financial guidance was given; 12-week and open-label data shifted to early 2027 from prior expectations of end-2026, and late-stage ABCL635 development is targeted for 2027. Development of ABCL575 in atopic dermatitis will not proceed following discontinuation of competitor OX40 programs.

AAON reported record Q3 FY2026 net sales of $707 million, up 84% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.83 (up 124%) and adjusted EBITDA of $127 million (18% margin, up 100 bps sequentially). Gross margin was 26.7%, down 110 bps year-over-year on a 300-plus bps brand mix headwind but up 60 bps sequentially. Management raised full-year 2026 sales growth guidance to 72%-75% from 55%-60%, with gross margin approximately 26% and SG&A approximately 13% of sales. The quarter also included self-identified accounting errors that understated first-half 2026 revenue by $10.7 million and diluted EPS by $0.09, restated in amended 10-Qs, with a material weakness concluded in internal control over financial reporting.

Q3 revenue of $268.3M rose 9.1% YoY and 4.2% QoQ, well ahead of the roughly flat sequential cadence previously guided, and was the highest quarterly revenue in 17 quarters. Adjusted EBITDA of $162M grew 4.4% YoY but margin contracted to 60.4% from 63.1%. Management raised FY26 revenue guidance by $30.5M at the midpoint to $1.038-1.043B, raised Adjusted EBITDA to $625-630M (+$12.5M) and free cash flow to $10-20M, and pre-announced at least $1.1B of 2027 revenue, a year ahead of the prior 2028 target. Claims Intelligence grew 17.1% while Network fell 5.6% on $5.4M of non-recurring prior-year revenue and Payment & Revenue Integrity lagged plan, though it is expected to return to growth in 2027.

Barrick reported Q3 FY2026 gold production of 816,000 oz and copper production of 50,000 t, with adjusted net earnings of $0.82/share (up 41% YoY per Mark, though Helen cited 37%), attributable Adjusted EBITDA up 22% to about $3.5 billion and free cash flow of $1.2 billion. Full-year production and cost guidance was unchanged for both gold and copper, with Q4 gold slightly higher than Q3 and copper rising on stockpiled Lumwana material; management said the year should land around the midpoint or slightly above. Costs remain pressured in Africa by diesel, royalties, and FX, with copper costs expected near the top end of the range, while the Lumwana expansion stays on budget at $2 billion and the North America IPO S-1 is due this month. Adjusted net earnings figures for YoY growth were stated inconsistently (41% vs 37%).

GCM Grosvenor reported Q3 FY2026 fee-related revenue of $115 million, up 10% YoY, fee-related earnings of $54 million, up 15%, and adjusted net income of $45 million, up 20% ($0.22 per share, up 16%). FRE margin expanded to 47% from 45%, AUM reached $98 billion (+13%) and fee-paying AUM $78 billion (+11%), with $2.7 billion raised in the quarter and $10 billion over 12 months. Management guided Q4 private markets management fees up 7%-9% and ARS management fees up mid-teens YoY, and stated full-year 2026 fundraising should rival 2025 while reaffirming Investor Day 2028 adjusted net income guidance. Unrealized carry reached a record ~$1.1 billion gross ($592 million firm share, up ~$100 million from June 30), though the ARS multi-strategy composite fell 2% gross in the quarter partly on SpaceX movement.

Dole reported Q3 revenue up 3.8% to ~$2.4 billion (2% like-for-like) and Adjusted EBITDA up 4.1% to $84.1 million, but adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.16. Fresh Fruit EBITDA rose 6% to $28.8 million despite revenue down 8% to $818.7 million, while Diversified EMEA EBITDA fell 3.1% to $39.5 million and Diversified Americas rose 22.8% to $15.8 million. Management cut FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $380-390 million from ~$400 million, citing higher European fuel/shipping costs (~$16 million full-year impact), pineapple quality issues (NDF), and adverse weather/El Niño. Free cash flow rose to $110.4 million in the quarter and net leverage fell to 1.3x helped by the Ecuador port sale.

Goosehead reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue up 17% YoY to $110 million and Core Revenue up 13% to $95 million, with policies in force up 14% to 2.1 million and total written premiums up 11% to $1.3 billion. New business commissions rose 21% to $9.1 million and new business royalties 13% to $9.4 million, while ancillary revenue doubled to $10.3 million; retention improved to 86%. Full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance of 12%-19% and written premium growth of 12%-20% was reiterated, not raised. The quarter was overshadowed by a restatement of 2023-2025 and Q1-Q2 2026 financials tied to an SEC comment letter on agent compensation cost accounting and franchise fee reclassification, and Core Revenue growth decelerated from Q2 on steeper-than-expected Texas pricing declines.

Forward Air reported Q3 FY2026 operating revenue of $674M, up $42M YoY, operating income of $44M vs $15M a year ago, and consolidated EBITDA up almost 30% to $101M (15.1% margin, +280 bps). Expedited Freight OR improved 330 bps to 89.2% and EBITDA rose 50% to $45M, while Omni margin expanded 170 bps to 11.3% and Intermodal returned to 14.3% margins. Management gave no explicit FY guidance, only qualitative Q4 commentary expecting typical seasonality and fewer working days, and provided no 2027 margin targets.
