The Intermodal divestiture was paused, and a two-year agreement with a major customer secures retained services projected to exceed $250M in 2025 revenue.

Fervo placed its first 33 MW GeoBlock at Cape Station into commercial operation on September 30, ahead of the contractual deadline, with brine flow and temperature in line with modeled expectations. Q3 revenue was effectively nil as the asset entered service on the last day of the quarter; G&A was $39.4 million (including $14 million stock comp) and operating loss was $43.7 million, while net income of $11.7 million reflected $15.4 million interest income plus non-recurring swap and tax-credit items. The 396 MW Google PPA lifted binding contracted capacity roughly 60% to 1,054 MW (~$11.9 billion backlog), and a revised DeGolyer and MacNaughton study doubled Cape Station capacity potential to 8.4 GW. CapEx guidance for the second half of 2026 was cut to $700–750 million from $850–900 million on construction efficiencies, while Q4 and 2027 revenue expectations were reiterated as unchanged from the Q2 call.

Ferguson reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $9.0 billion, up 9.5% (7.0% organic, 2.7% acquisition), with operating profit up 8.9% to $962 million at a flat 10.7% margin and diluted EPS of $3.43, up 7.9%. Gross margin was 30.9%, down 40 bps year-over-year on prior-period supplier price timing, and U.S. sales grew 10.2% with non-residential up 15% and residential up 6%. Management raised full-year net sales guidance to approximately 7% growth from mid-single digits and lifted the low end of its operating margin range to 9.6%-9.8%, while flagging incremental pressure in new residential construction. Acquisitions including FloWorks added roughly 3% to annual growth and leverage sits at 1.7x net debt to adjusted EBITDA with buybacks paused.

Q3 2026 revenue was $91 million, down 1% YoY, with core charging network revenue up 29% to $72 million offset by eXtend revenue falling $16 million to $16 million on lower construction revenue. Daily throughput per stall fell 4% YoY to 283 kWh (utilization 20% vs 22%), though excluding OEM credits it grew 7% to 270 kWh; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.5 million from $5 million. 2026 guidance was lowered on stall cadence and revenue, now 1,075-1,275 new stalls (from prior plans, with some builds sliding into 2027), revenue of $375-$400 million reflecting lower throughput, and adjusted EBITDA loss of -$30 million to -$15 million; 2027 adjusted G&A guided at least 15% below prior expectations. LS Power made an unsolicited non-binding $2/share take-private offer for shares it does not own, and the board formed a special committee; management declined further comment.

Xenon's Q3 FY2026 call was dominated by clinical and commercial progress rather than financial results; the only hard financial figure disclosed was $1.2 billion in cash, equivalents and marketable securities, funding operations into 2029. The company submitted its azetukalner NDA for focal seizures in Q3 and now guides to X-NOVA2 phase III MDD top-line data in December 2026, pulled forward from Q1 2027. However, X-NOVA2 and the broader psychiatry program remain under a voluntary enrollment pause following neuropsychiatric adverse events, with next steps contingent on unblinded data and FDA discussions. Pain assets XEN1701 and XEN1120 will advance to phase II acute-pain studies in the first half of 2027.

TMTG reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of roughly $3 million, up 78% sequentially and over 200% year-over-year, driven by Truth API subscriptions, Truth+ and Truth Social advertising, and Truth.Fi ETF management fees. Operating expenses ex-digital-asset items fell 45% sequentially to $26.5 million as legal fees dropped from over $20 million to $2.4 million after the July resolution of SPAC-related matters. GAAP net income of $409.7 million was driven almost entirely by a $378.1 million mark-to-market gain on digital assets as Bitcoin rose 42% to about $84,000, while adjusted EBITDA remained a $12.3 million loss and operating cash flow was negative $28.4 million year-to-date. No formal forward guidance was issued; management reiterated closing the TAE merger by year-end, repaying the ~$1 billion convertible notes with cash and credit without issuing equity, and preserving Bitcoin, while disclosing the planned February 2 token distribution has been discontinued.

Pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech; Q3 FY2026 results were operational, not commercial. R&D expense rose to $46.1M from $31M and G&A to $26.1M from $14.7M YoY, while net loss narrowed to $51M from $67.3M on warrant fair-value gains and higher interest income; cash and investments stood at ~$1.05B versus $411.6M at year-end 2025, with runway guided into 2030. Management reaffirmed the DT120 NDA filing for 1H 2027 on the back of three positive Phase III studies (Emerge, Voyage, Panorama) and two breakthrough therapy designations, and disclosed initial positive DT402 signals in a five-patient ASD study. No revenue, EPS, or formal financial guidance was provided; all forward detail on regulatory strategy, pricing, and launch economics was deferred to future disclosures.

Delcath reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $35.1M, up 71% YoY from $20.6M, with HEPZATO KIT revenue of $32.7M (volume +19% QoQ, +72% YoY) and CHEMOSAT $2.4M. Gross margin was 89% vs 87%, net income $7.0M vs $0.8M, adjusted EBITDA $11.5M vs $5.3M, and operating cash flow was $8.2M. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $115M-$117M and expects at least 41% HEPZATO volume growth with positive adjusted EBITDA. Q4 guidance of $25.8M-$27.8M implies a step-down (~25%-34% YoY growth) attributed largely to roughly two holiday weeks lost and fewer new patient starts than the 0.6 per site per month seen in Q3.

Docebo reported a strong Q3 FY2026 quarter with EBITDA growing approximately 34% while top-line revenue grew 12.8% in Q4 (guidance), following sequential growth of 12.4% in Q3. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to a midpoint of 14%, citing a rebound year and strong pipeline, particularly in the government vertical which exceeded expectations. The company announced an approximate $60 million one-time special dividend funded by remaining debt capacity, leaving a net debt position of approximately $108 million.

SABESP reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net revenue of BRL 6 billion (organic growth of 9%) and adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3.6 billion (up 14% YoY), driven by a 7.7% price contribution and 2.1% volume gain, partially offset by higher refunds and mix effects. Cash generation remained solid with operating cash flow at BRL 2 billion, while CapEx accelerated to BRL 4.5 billion in the quarter. Management provided no specific revenue guidance for the full year due to high uncertainty regarding El Niño rainfall impacts on consumption volumes.

Consolidated net revenue declined 3.2% year-over-year to ARS 270.1 billion, driven by a 6.3% drop in cement volumes and a 23.2% fall in concrete revenues due to soft activity and adverse weather. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 74 basis points to 20.1%, while the railroad segment turned negative at -11%. Management noted that September's volume rebound suggests demand is responsive to weather, but bagged cement recovery remains uncertain pending real economy improvements.

Mercer International reported Q3 FY2026 operating EBITDA of -$3 million, an improvement from -$21 million in the prior quarter, driven by a lower non-cash inventory impairment of $8 million compared to $29 million previously. The company executed a pre-packaged Chapter 11 restructuring agreement reducing senior note debt by approximately 88% and injecting liquidity via a new rights offering, with completion expected by the end of 2026. While pulp sales realizations remained flat due to soft demand and maintenance downtime, management noted that supply constraints are beginning to balance market weakness.

MTD reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.1 billion (up 6% in USD and local currency) and adjusted EPS of $12.57 (up 13%). Management raised full-year 2026 local currency sales growth guidance from 4-5% to approximately 5%, while providing initial 2027 guidance for roughly 5% sales growth and adjusted EPS between $52.50-$53.50.

Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported record quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of $52.4 million and adjusted net income of $33.6 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by a 31% year-over-year increase in TCE rates to $20,414 per day. Terminal revenue surged 73% year-over-year due to new port operations, while the company generated $57 million in operating cash flow and completed a refinancing that lowers borrowing costs. Management expressed confidence in firm market fundamentals for 2027 but declined to provide specific guidance on terminal growth or Q4 results.

Pembina reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1.128 billion, a 9% year-over-year increase driven by premium propane prices in Asian markets and higher NGL margins. The company updated its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range to CAD 4.45-4.55 billion (raised from the prior CAD 4.35-4.55 billion) and stated it is trending toward the upper end of this range. Management highlighted strong execution on new assets like RFS IV and Greenlight, with nearly CAD 3 billion in projects sanctioned since April.

PPL reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.49 and adjusted earnings from ongoing operations of $0.54, beating the narrowed full-year forecast range of $1.92-$1.96 with a midpoint target of $1.94 for the nine months ended. Management raised the long-term annual EPS growth target to 7%-9% through 2030 and extended the capital plan to $25 billion from 2027-2030, driven by strong data center pipeline conversion in Pennsylvania and Kentucky. The company announced a collaboration with QTS for approximately 2 GW of generation capacity in Pennsylvania via Invitium Energy, providing meaningful upside potential.

Q3 FY2026 QPU-related services revenue grew 53% YoY to EUR 3.1 million, but total revenues declined to EUR 3.3 million from EUR 5.7 million in the prior year due to a lack of QPU sales and lower government grants. Management explicitly stated that the quarter was not strong on reported financials, noting that order book levels remained stable rather than growing significantly.

Ready Capital reported a GAAP loss of $0.40 per share and a distributable loss of $0.53 per share for Q3 FY2026, driven by $53.9 million in realized losses from asset resolutions. While recurring revenue improved to $20.7 million and operating expenses declined to $47.6 million, the company reduced its dividend to $0.01 per share following the completion of a liquidity plan that repaid $649 million of debt. Management targets breakeven distributable earnings in early 2027.

RGA reported Q3 FY2026 pre-tax adjusted operating income of $736 million ($8.49 EPS), driven by strong investment income and favorable claims experience across all regions. Management highlighted a robust pipeline in the U.S. PRT and U.K. longevity markets, with new business momentum continuing globally. The company returned $139 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends while fully deploying Ruby Re capital.

The E.W. Scripps Company reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $546 million ($373M Local Media + $173M Networks), which was up 19% YoY primarily due to record political advertising revenue of $81 million in Local Media, while core advertising revenue declined 13%. Segment profit surged to $151 million compared to $50 million a year ago. Management provided Q4 guidance expecting Local Media revenue growth in the low-to-mid-40% range and Scripps Networks revenue down in the high single-digits due to soft direct response markets, noting that core advertising will be displaced by the election cycle.

SiriusPoint reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with core gross written premium growing 14% to $991 million and net earned premiums up 19%. The company achieved a core combined ratio of 90.1%, resulting in underwriting income of $76 million, while operating earnings per share rose 19% year-over-year to $0.88. Management announced a Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) agreement with RiverStone to remove legacy runoff exposures, which is expected to free up over $200 million in capital and increase the BSCR ratio by approximately 20 points upon completion.

Apple Hospitality reported Q3 FY2026 comparable hotels RevPAR growth of 7.3% and total revenue growth of 8.2%, driven by a shift toward higher-rated business travel and group bookings. Management raised full-year guidance for RevPAR growth to a midpoint of 5.6% (up 235 bps) and Adjusted EBITDA margin to 35.25% (up 105 bps), citing strong October performance and limited new supply. The company sold three hotels for approximately $72 million, bringing total dispositions since early 2025 to $154 million.

Suzano reported Q3 FY2026 results with combined EBITDA down 14% quarter-over-quarter due to operational challenges at the Pine Bluff mill and higher SG&A/logistics costs, though pulp sales volumes remained solid. Management updated full-year 2026 cash cost guidance from BRL 800/ton to approximately BRL 825/ton citing persistent Middle East conflict impacts on energy/commodities and a stronger USD. The Arbex acquisition is integrated with Q3 results in line with plans, but the company remains focused on deleveraging and efficiency capture rather than new capital allocation.

Interface reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $366.7 million, a slight miss on the low end of guidance due to timing shifts in retail billings and softer European demand. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.68 beat expectations, driven by margin expansion that offset higher input costs from tariffs and energy prices. Management reaffirmed full-year earnings guidance but lowered the net sales outlook to reflect the challenging macro environment in Europe.

VEON reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.31 billion (up 17.2% YoY) and EBITDA of $577 million (up 10.1% YoY), driven by a 46% surge in digital services revenue. Management raised the lower end of full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue growth of 16%-18% and EBITDA growth of 10%-12%. Operating cash flow increased 47% year-to-date to $1.3 billion, while leverage improved to 1.05x.

Third quarter revenue was $76.2 million, up from $44.8 million in the prior quarter, driven by HPC lease revenue of $63.0 million representing 83% of total revenue. GAAP net income swung to a profit of $709.9 million compared to a loss in Q2, primarily due to non-cash fair value adjustments and gains on asset sales. Management reaffirmed cost guidance for the WULF Compute project at approximately $8.9 million per megawatt, within the original range, while highlighting robust demand and secured financing structures including Google credit support.

Under Armour reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.2 billion, a 7% decline year-over-year, with adjusted operating income meeting the lowered outlook but missing prior expectations due to macro headwinds and inventory actions. Management maintained full-year guidance for mid-single-digit revenue declines while narrowing the gross margin outlook range, citing extended Middle East conflict costs and higher freight expenses. The quarter highlighted strategic shifts including a 50% SKU reduction and a transition of the youth apparel business to an expanded licensing model.

Under Armour reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.2 billion, a 7% decline year-over-year, with adjusted operating income meeting expectations despite the miss on top-line growth. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance at a mid-single-digit decline but lowered the gross margin outlook by 50 basis points due to elevated supply chain costs and inventory actions. The company emphasized a strategic shift toward simplifying its product assortment and improving marketing efficacy to stabilize North American demand.

Senstar reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $13.1 million, up 37% year-over-year from $9.5 million, which management said was in line with its financial plan. Net income was $1.5 million, or $0.07 per share, versus $1.0 million and $0.04 a year ago, with operating income of $1.9 million (from $1.1 million) and Adjusted EBITDA up 55% to $2.1 million (15.7% margin). Growth was broad-based: U.S. revenue up 23%, EMEA up 50%, APAC up 50%, Canada up 62%, and LiDAR sales more than doubled to about 20% of total sales. Gross margin slipped to 66.3% from 67.3% year-over-year on product mix but rose roughly 210 bps sequentially; cash fell to $8.4 million from $22.5 million at year-end 2025, reflecting the EUR 10.4 million cash-funded Blickfeld acquisition, and the company carries no debt. No explicit forward guidance figures were provided beyond commentary that demand trends are favorable and the U.S. has returned to pre-shutdown levels.

AirSculpt reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $31.9 million, an 8.7% year-over-year decline driven by a 9.6% drop in case volume and higher customer acquisition costs due to Google AI Overviews. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($144M-$146M vs $151M-$157M) and adjusted EBITDA ($9M-$10M vs $12M-$14M), assuming Q3 trends will persist into Q4. The company successfully refinanced its term loan to 2031, ending the quarter with approximately $20 million in total liquidity.

Third quarter adjusted net EPS increased to $0.11 from $0.09 last year, driven by favorable weather and new rates, though GAAP earnings missed due to wildfire insurance costs and higher OpEx. The company remains on track to meet its full-year 2026 adjusted net EPS guidance of $0.35-$0.37 per share. Management reaffirmed the 2027 guidance range of $0.38-$0.42 per share while noting that the recent sale of Suralis was largely neutral for 2026 due to tax impacts.

Third quarter sales increased 3% to $499 million driven by volume growth in Performance Chemicals and Class I crossties, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 18% to $58 million due to higher raw material and logistics costs. Management revised the full-year 2026 earnings outlook lower to reflect these persistent cost pressures that outweighed benefits through September. While year-to-date free cash flow hit a record $92 million, pricing actions to recover absorbed costs are not expected until January 2027.

Chesapeake Utilities reported a strong third quarter with adjusted net income up 12% and adjusted EPS rising 9% year-over-year. Adjusted gross margin expanded 9% to approximately $149 million, driven by interim rate recognition of $2.7 million for the Florida City Gas case and contributions from transmission expansion projects. The company remains on track for its full-year capital guidance of $550-$600 million after investing $413 million year-to-date.

Fluor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.7 billion (up from $3.4 billion YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.77 (up from $0.68 YoY). The company delivered record new awards of $10.9 billion, raising backlog to $34.3 billion, while maintaining full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $500-$525 million despite a potential $2 billion scope reduction on one reimbursable project. Management expressed confidence in the pipeline and reiterated plans for continued share repurchases.

F&G reported adjusted net earnings of $96 million ($0.74 per share) for Q3 FY2026, which was in line with expectations but missed the prior year due to lower alternative investment returns and a one-time actuarial assumption adjustment. Gross sales reached a record $3 billion in the quarter, driven by core retail sales of $2.1 billion (up 24% YoY), while AUM before reinsurance grew 7% to $76.2 billion. Management maintained its long-term return expectations for alternative investments at 12% despite Q3 volatility and reaffirmed its disciplined capital allocation strategy.

Dauch Corporation reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $2.91 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.22, missing the prior year's adjusted EPS of $0.30 due to lower production volumes on Ram heavy-duty programs (down ~15% YoY) and GM downtime. Adjusted EBITDA was $358 million (12.3% margin), down from 13.0% last year, reflecting inflationary pressures and one-time commercial settlements. Management updated full-year guidance to a sales range of $10.8-$10.875 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.35-$1.375 billion, tightening the outlook from the prior $10.6-$10.8 billion and $1.36-$1.425 billion ranges respectively.

ACRE reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $10 million ($0.18 EPS) and Distributable Earnings of $6.7 million ($0.12 EPS), driven by a $300,000 realized gain on the sale of a North Carolina office REO property. The company ended the quarter with available capital of $116 million and a net debt-to-equity ratio of 1.9x, while fully repaying a term loan subsequent to quarter-end. Management maintains a cautious stance focused on resolving risk-rated four and five loans totaling approximately $160 million in carrying value.

FNF reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net earnings of $352 million ($1.32/share), missing the prior year's $439 million due to lower investment income and a sale of an F&G subsidiary, while GAAP net earnings were boosted by $29 million in recognized gains. Title segment revenue grew 11% YoY but margins compressed to 17.1% from 17.8% as the company invested heavily in recruiting (adding ~300 people) and acquisitions ahead of productivity ramp-up. Management noted a sequential decline in purchase orders driven by high mortgage rates and seasonality, with expectations for margin pressure in Q4 before potential recovery in 2027.

Gogo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $213.2 million, down 5% year-over-year and 4% sequentially, driven by the expected transition from legacy ATG to next-generation products. While Galileo shipments hit a record 172 units (up 59% sequentially) and military/government revenue grew 36% year-over-year, total service revenue declined 4% due to lower ATG volumes. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue of $870-$895 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $175-$185 million, noting that the revised range includes reduced litigation expenses following a court ruling.

Granite Ridge Resources reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with Adjusted EBITDAX rising 35% sequentially to $107.3 million and oil volumes growing 16%, driven by an 8% increase in average daily production and a recovery in Waha gas basis. Management raised full-year production guidance to a range of 34,000-35,000 BOE per day with a higher oil mix, while also authorizing a new $35 million share repurchase program. The company highlighted the successful transition to free cash flow positivity and the addition of Arete Creek Resources as a third operated partner in the Permian.

Baytex reported Q3 FY2026 production of 71,600 BOE/d (up 5% YoY) and generated CAD 139 million in free cash flow while returning CAD 165 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Management raised the full-year 2026 exploration and development expenditure guidance from CAD 625 million to CAD 665 million, citing improved Duvernay performance and heavy oil activity. The company accelerated its Duvernay commercialization plan, now targeting 25,000 BOE/d by late 2028 (1.5 years earlier than previously planned), supported by a three-year outlook of 8%-10% annual production growth.

Total revenue of $972 million beat the high end of updated guidance by approximately $7 million, driven by political advertising revenue of $198 million which exceeded its range and set a new record. Management raised full-year 2026 political guidance to $630-$640 million and provided Q4 political guidance of $319-$329 million. The company announced plans to reduce debt by an additional $175-$200 million in the fourth quarter using political cash flow.

Total revenue declined 7.5% year-over-year to BRL 123.3 million in Q3, driven by lower client activity and reduced capital market issuances due to election-related volatility. Management adopted a conservative balance sheet stance, reducing securities warehousing and leverage, while announcing an interim dividend of BRL 0.12 per unit. Forward guidance remains muted with expectations for deal delays rather than mortality, pending a resolution in the macroeconomic and political landscape.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners reported FFO of $717 million ($0.91 per unit) for Q3 FY2026, representing the third consecutive quarter of meeting its 10% FFO per unit growth target driven by organic growth and asset commissioning. Management reiterated confidence in closing the year with strong performance and achieving the full-year 10% FFO growth target, while noting that corporate simplification is expected to close on November 19th. The company deployed approximately $1.8 billion of equity year-to-date across new investments and organic projects.

Humana raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook from at least $9 to at least $9.50 based on Q3 performance that exceeded initial expectations. Management highlighted strong execution in Medicare Advantage membership and CenterWell growth, alongside a significant one-time tailwind from Bonus Year 2028 Stars results exceeding Top Quartile goals. The company expects to utilize some of this tailwind for investments while passing the remainder to shareholders, though specific quantification is pending further data.

Atmus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $510 million, a 14% increase year-over-year driven by organic growth and the Koch Filter acquisition, with adjusted EPS of $0.77 beating the prior year's $0.69. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $2.01 billion-$2.035 billion (midpoint +15% vs 2025) and raised adjusted EPS expectations to $2.90-$3.05, while maintaining the EBITDA margin guidance of 19.75%-20.25%. The company returned $25 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends and paid down $100 million in debt.

Third quarter revenue increased 2% sequentially to $827 million, but Adjusted EBITDA returned to positive at only $6 million after narrowing losses from the prior quarter. Management noted that revenue was slightly below expectations due to shipment timing issues, customer delivery delays, and component availability constraints. The company announced a major restructuring program targeting $100 million in annual cost reductions by 2029, alongside the discontinuation of hydrogen solutions and electric terminal tractor programs.

Revenue of $35.1 million beat the high end of guidance and grew 34% year-over-year, driven by record orders of $49.4 million including a record $23.9 million in back-end semiconductor orders. Gross margin expanded to 47.7%, exceeding guidance due to favorable product mix, while operating expenses remained flat sequentially. Management raised the full-year 2026 tax rate expectation to approximately 20% and provided Q4 revenue guidance of $34-$36 million.

DKL reported Adjusted EBITDA of $143 million in Q3 FY2026, which was in line with the prior year period and met expectations. Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $530-$560 million. The company completed its first sour gas compressor station and AGI well at the Libby Complex, driving an increase in Gathering and Processing EBITDA to $88 million.

Elanco reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.265 billion, an 11% increase on a reported basis and 9% organic growth driven by volume (5%) and price (4%). The company significantly outperformed guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS ($0.27), leading to a full-year guidance raise with organic revenue growth updated to approximately 8% and adjusted EPS raised by $0.06 at the midpoint to $1.17-$1.20. Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 56.1%, while net leverage improved to 2.9x.

KBDC reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.46 per share, up from $0.42 in the prior quarter, with a dividend coverage ratio of 115%. The company declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.40 per share for Q4 and maintained its commitment to sustain this base dividend through 2026 despite NAV declines driven by idiosyncratic credit losses. Management highlighted that SOFR expectations rising above 4% provide a tailwind, while new originations averaged 538 bps over SOFR.

Kingstone reported a record Q3 with net income of $17.6 million ($1.19 EPS), representing a 62% increase year-over-year driven by a 14.5% rise in direct premiums written to $86.8 million and an underlying loss ratio improvement of 10.6 points to 33.5%. Management raised full-year 2026 diluted EPS guidance to $2.70-$2.90 from the prior range of $2.20-$2.90, while narrowing the combined ratio outlook to 79%-83% and updating premium growth expectations to approximately 16%. The company noted that California expansion is significantly below initial plans due to market reopening and competitive pressure, though it remains on track for its $500 million direct written premium goal by year-end 2029.

VAALCO Energy reported Q3 FY2026 results with NRI production increasing over 20% quarter-over-quarter to 18,454 barrels per day and adjusted EBITDAX reaching $71.1 million, driven by the restart of Côte d'Ivoire and drilling in Gabon and Egypt. Management raised Q4 sales volume guidance to a range of 21,000-22,800 NRI barrels per day (approx. 18% higher than Q3 actuals) while maintaining full-year CapEx guidance despite expanding the Egyptian budget. The company highlighted strong pricing premiums in Gabon and Côte d'Ivoire, though noted $22 million in realized hedging losses.

Sylvamo reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $128 million (20% margin) versus $66 million in Q2, with adjusted operating earnings of $1.33 per share and free cash flow of $16 million. The quarter benefited from $25 million of favorable price/mix and a $38 million favorable maintenance outage comparison, partially offset by $6 million of higher input and transportation costs that are expected to repeat in Q4 and annualize into 2027. The company announced a put option agreement to divest its European business, which will be reported as discontinued operations, with closing expected by the end of Q1 2027. Management provided limited quantitative guidance, indicating North America volume will be relatively flat in 2027 and that certain non-repeating items will not fully recur, but declined to provide a formal 2027 EBITDA bridge.

FTAI Infrastructure reported record Q3 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of $95.3 million versus $70.9 million a year earlier, and $54.4 million excluding Long Ridge, also a record. The rail segment set all-time highs in carloads, rate per car, revenue ($104.2 million vs $61.7 million) and Adjusted EBITDA ($47.4 million vs $29.1 million). Management guided to continued double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth into 2027 and expects ~$19 million of annual Wheeling cost savings, with the Long Ridge sale (~$1.5 billion, ~$1.4 billion of debt eliminated) expected to close by month-end and the USD assets (~$50 million annual EBITDA) closing mid-November. Jefferson crude volumes averaged 41,000 bpd in Q3 but recovered to 85,000 bpd in October, and Repauno phase two is nearing completion.

Plains All American reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $711 million, benefiting from operating efficiencies, annual FERC tariff escalations, and lower environmental remediation costs versus Q2. Full-year EBITDA guidance midpoint is $2.88 billion with a narrowed ±$50 million range, and management expects to be at or slightly above the midpoint. Q4 is guided to about $700 million, roughly $10 million lower sequentially, on reduced market opportunities and transition costs from the Silver Creek acquisition, partly offset by a full quarter of Silver Creek. The quarter included a 10-year Midland gathering agreement covering 270,000 dedicated acres, closing of the Silver Creek acquisition (about 125,000 barrels/day, 915,000 dedicated acres), and a $1.5 billion junior subordinated notes raise used to redeem preferred units, expected to add roughly $60 million ($0.09/unit) of annual distributable cash flow to common unitholders.

Global Partners reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $52.4 million versus $29 million a year ago, with EBITDA up to $120.8 million from $97.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $122.9 million versus $98.8 million. Distributable cash flow rose to $70.1 million from $53 million with 2.3x distribution coverage. The gain was driven by wholesale product margin up $33.4 million to $111.4 million on favorable gasoline and distillate market conditions, partly offset by GDSO product margin down $8.3 million to $210.6 million on lower gasoline distribution volume. Guidance was largely intact, with maintenance CapEx raised $5 million to $65-75 million and expansion CapEx unchanged at $75-85 million, and the company declared its 20th consecutive quarterly distribution increase to $0.7850 per unit.

Galiano reported Q3 revenue of $172 million on just over 40,000 ounces sold at a $4,247/oz realized price, with adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million, basic EPS of $0.15 and adjusted EPS of $0.09. Net income attributable to shareholders swung to $40 million from a $39 million loss a year earlier, operating cash flow rose to $57 million from $40 million, and AISC improved 5% sequentially to $2,346/oz. Production of 40,922 ounces rose 19% from Q2 on 11% higher mill throughput and 11% higher feed grade, with nine-month output just over 110,000 ounces. Full-year production and AISC guidance ($2,300-2,600/oz) were reaffirmed, but 2027 cost and production details were deferred to early 2027.

TDS Telecom total operating revenue declined 3% (about 1% excluding divestitures), cash expenses rose 4%, and adjusted EBITDA fell as legacy copper and cable pressure more than offset fiber revenue growth of 14%. Management cut full-year telecom revenue guidance to $990M-$1.01B and adjusted EBITDA to $290M-$310M, and raised CapEx guidance by $100M to approximately $750M at the midpoint. Offsetting this, TDS Telecom posted record third-quarter fiber address delivery (~76,000, up 82% YoY) and record fiber net adds (~17,000, up 50% YoY), while Array's cash site rental revenue grew 20% (7% excluding T-Mobile MLA) with its outlook unchanged. TDS also exhausted its $520M buyback authorization and the board approved an additional $250M.

Fidus reported Q3 2026 adjusted NII of $0.54 per share versus $0.50 in Q2, with total investment income of $45.9 million ($2.4 million above Q2) on a 24% increase in interest income that was partly offset by a $0.9 million decline in dividend income. NAV was $774.4 million, or $19.47 per share, and no debt investments were on non-accrual; the board declared a Q4 total dividend of $0.54 (base $0.43 plus $0.11 supplemental). Originations of $51.8 million roughly matched repayments of $52.4 million, leaving the portfolio stable at $1.4 billion (102.8% of cost), and management guided to a higher level of origination and repayment activity in Q4 driven by an improved but still uncertain M&A market. A $11 million net realized loss on Virtex Enterprises, previously written down, was the main blemish.

Essent reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $163 million, or $1.82 per diluted EPS, up from $1.67 a year ago but down from $2.08 last quarter, with ROE of approximately 12%. Insurance in force was $250.1 billion, up 1% YoY but only $342 million from June 30, as persistency of 83.3% and affordability constraints kept portfolio growth muted. MI provision for losses rose to $51.7 million from $29.4 million last quarter and $44.2 million a year ago, with the default rate increasing to 2.75% from 2.53%. Management guided to a longer-term 35-45 combined ratio and roughly 80% persistency, and the board declared a $0.35 quarterly dividend and authorized a new $500 million buyback; no formal EPS or premium guidance was provided.

EOG reported record oil, NGL and natural gas volumes with all three streams above guidance midpoint, adjusted EPS of $4.87, adjusted CFO per share of $7.23 and $2.2 billion of free cash flow; per-unit cash operating costs and DD&A both came in below guidance midpoint. The company raised its regular dividend 8% to an indicated $4.40 annual rate, returned roughly $1.5 billion ($1 billion buybacks plus ~$540 million dividend), and reiterated 2026 capex of $6.5 billion with 5% oil and 14% total production growth. For 2027 management guided to low single-digit oil growth consistent with its three-year scenario and flagged modest service, steel and diesel cost inflation, with ~60% of 2027 services already contracted. Portfolio actions included an ENGIE JKM-linked gas agreement (140,000 MMBtu/day, 10-year, from 2030), a $300 million Janus processing expansion and $400 million of Barnett/Woodford divestitures.

Enbridge reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA up CAD 167 million year over year, with utilities and gas transmission benefiting from rate cases and customer growth, while Liquids Pipelines declined on lower Line 9 tolls and reduced Flanagan South throughput. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance and expects results at the midpoint, guiding to a 21st consecutive year of meeting guidance. The quarter was heavy with strategic actions: the Tallgrass crude business and Salt Creek crude gathering acquisitions, the CAD 2.7 billion Westcoast JV with KKR and Apollo, a CAD 3 billion common equity offering, the Long Lake Expansion sanction (CAD 200 million, in service 2028), and CEO Greg Ebel's year-end retirement with Michele Harradence to succeed him.

Emera reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of CAD 0.85 and adjusted earnings of CAD 260 million, a 3% year-over-year decrease, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.90 and adjusted earnings of CAD 887 million, up CAD 9 million. Management reaffirmed its 5%-7% compound EPS growth target through 2030 and stated 2026 will come in above that range, while introducing a CAD 21.5 billion five-year capital plan (about CAD 1.1 billion, or 5%, higher than last year's) driving 7.5%-8.5% rate base growth through 2031, up from 7%-8%. The board approved a 1% dividend increase, the 20th consecutive annual raise, and Tampa Electric is targeting a year-end contract for the first 350 MW at the Auburndale data center. EPS guidance will be rolled forward at the Q4 call in February.

Edenor reported Q3 2026 revenue of ARS 1,123 billion, up 14% year-over-year in real terms, with distribution margin up 5% to ARS 434 billion; nine-month EBITDA reached ARS 506 billion, up 58% excluding the ARS 266 billion 2025 CAMMESA one-off gain. Q3 net profit fell 25% to ARS 43 billion due to that prior-year one-off, though lower financial expenses (down 10%) partly offset. Tariff adjustments of 28.4% through September outpaced 23.6% inflation, OpEx fell 5%, and the pending MetroGAS 70% acquisition is expected to close before year-end. No formal forward financial guidance was issued; commentary was qualitative and optimistic.

Devon's first full quarter post-Coterra delivered oil and total production within guidance at all-time highs, discretionary cash flow of $3.5 billion (up over 20% sequentially), $2 billion of free cash flow at a 43% reinvestment rate, and cash costs 2% below the guidance midpoint; full-year 2026 production, cost, and capital guidance was reaffirmed with no raise. The company issued initial 2027 guidance of ~525 MBbl/d oil, ~1.6 MMBOE/d total, and ~$5.3 billion capital versus a pro forma 2026 baseline of $5.9 billion, implying low single-digit growth on meaningfully lower capital. Shareholder returns accelerated with $414 million of buybacks in Q3, guidance for more than $1 billion in Q4, $1.25 billion of debt retired since merger close, and $3.5 billion of expected Eagle Ford net proceeds in early 2027. Management acknowledged the stock has underperformed since the merger close and framed the completed portfolio review as closing a chapter to clarify strategy.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 16% YoY to $1.33 billion with MUPs up 13% to 4.1 million and average revenue per MUP up 3% to $109, but Adjusted EBITDA was -$317 million as Predictions investment ramped. Management cut FY2026 guidance sharply to revenue of $6.35-$6.55 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $175-$275 million from the prior $6.5-$6.9 billion and $700-$900 million, citing a higher Predictions investment of $650-$700 million plus incremental iGaming promotion and modestly customer-friendly sports outcomes. FY2027 guidance was introduced at revenue of $7.35-$7.75 billion (17% growth at the midpoint) and Adjusted EBITDA of $800 million-$1 billion, with core Adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and Predictions investment stepping down to $300 million at the midpoint. The core franchise held up—Sportsbook net revenue up 36% on 12% handle growth with margin up ~120 bps to 6.4%—but much of the call was spent defending payback assumptions against a possible mid-2028 Supreme Court ruling on sports event contracts.

Delek reported Q3 FY2026 net income of ~$1.13B ($18.22/share), adjusted net income of ~$843M ($13.55/share), adjusted EBITDA of ~$1.28B, and ~$1.04B adjusted EBITDA / $10.53 adjusted EPS excluding the 50% RVO adjustment and SRE impacts. Management raised the Enterprise Optimization Plan (EOP) target to at least $250M annual run rate (from an initial $100M) and increased the quarterly dividend ~18% to $0.30/share, with $50M of Q3 buybacks and a plan for ~$100M more in Q4. DKL raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to $530M-$560M, and the company expects ~$425M of SRE proceeds in Q4. Q4 throughput guidance totals 288,000-308,000 bpd with opex of $225M-$235M, G&A of $50M-$55M, and D&A of $115M-$125M; cash flow from operations was $567M with a ~$809M working capital outflow largely tied to SRE receivables.

Normalized FFO per share rose 20% YoY to $0.54 and normalized FAD per share rose 20% to $0.53, with normalized FFO up 37% to $129.2 million. Management raised the low end of FY2026 guidance to normalized FFO per share of $2.08-$2.09 and FAD of $2.04-$2.05, implying ~18.5% and ~16.2% growth at the midpoint. The company closed ~$740 million of Q3 investments at an 8.3% blended stabilized yield and ~$1 billion post-quarter, bringing YTD 2026 investments to ~$2.9 billion at an 8.1% blended yield. SNF EBITDA lease coverage set a record at 2.62x (EBITDARM 3.26x), and pro forma leverage stands at ~2.7x versus a 4-5x target range.

Q3 revenue was $7.3 million, up 67% year-over-year, with payments volume of $197.3 million (+121%) and Credova originations up 23%. Operating loss narrowed to $3.3 million from $9.7 million, net loss was $4.1 million versus $12 million, and operating cash burn was $1.7 million, down 26% sequentially from $2.3 million. Management reaffirmed the 2026 outlook of $32 million revenue and positive non-GAAP operating income, which requires a record ~$9.4 million Q4 against $22.6 million through nine months, plus a 2027 target of positive monthly operating cash flow. The quarter showed substantial cost and cash-progress, but the full-year reaffirmation now rests on the largest quarter in company history and a larger than-expected seller-financed EveryLife exit ($1 million cash, $4.5 million note).

TDS Telecom revenue declined 3% (1% ex-divestitures) with cash expenses up 4% and Adjusted EBITDA down, and management cut 2026 Telecom guidance: revenue to $990M-$1.01B and Adjusted EBITDA to $290M-$310M, while raising capex by $100M to ~$750M. Fiber execution was strong — a record ~76,000 addresses delivered (up 82% YoY), ~17,000 fiber net adds (up ~50% YoY, a company record), fiber revenue up 14%, and fiber churn improving 20 bps — but legacy copper and coax pressures (coax revenue down 7%, or 10% adjusted) offset the gains. Array's outlook was unchanged (revenue $205M-$215M, Adjusted EBITDA $220M-$235M) with organic cash site rental revenue growth of 7% excluding the T-Mobile MLA. TDS withdrew its offer for Array's minority interest after failing to agree on value, and nearly exhausted its $520M buyback authorization while approving a new $250M authorization.

Regency reported Q3 2026 same-property NOI growth of 5.1% and year-to-date growth of 4.4%, with total NOI up 7.6% YTD. Same-property occupancy reached a record 97% leased (shop 94.6%), commenced occupancy hit a record 95.1%, and cash rent spreads were 12% (GAAP 22%). Management raised full-year guidance again — same-property NOI midpoint to 4.25%+ and core operating EPS growth midpoint to 5.7% — and raised the dividend 6%. However, 2027 same-property NOI growth was guided to the mid-3% area (roughly 3.5%), below 2026's level, and refinancing of maturing debt is expected to be a 150-200 bps drag on the long-term earnings growth target.

Ring Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $102.3 million, down 2% sequentially despite a 12% decline in realized oil price, with total sales volumes up 3% to 20,635 BOE/d and oil volumes up 1% to 12,818 bbl/d. Adjusted EBITDA rose 5% sequentially to $57.1 million with margin improving to 56% from 52%, while adjusted free cash flow was negative as the company deliberately accelerated ~$64 million of capital spending. The company guided Q4 oil volumes to 12,900-13,500 bbl/d and 2027 oil volumes to 13,200-14,300 bbl/d with capital of $135-165 million, citing a shift to longer laterals and co-development for roughly 10% production growth on similar or lower capital. Leverage improved to approximately 1.5x from 1.7x, and the company expects to return to positive free cash flow in Q4 and remain positive for the full year.

Sunstone reported Q3 FY2026 total portfolio RevPAR growth of 11.4% (10.3% ex-Andaz Miami Beach) and total RevPAR up 10.5%, driving Adjusted EBITDAre of $54.5 million (+9% YoY) and adjusted FFO per share of $0.20 (+18% YoY). Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: rooms RevPAR growth to 9.5%-10.5% (up 200 bps at the midpoint), Adjusted EBITDAre to $254M-$259M and FFO per share to $1.00-$1.03, with the raise reflecting both stronger trends and buyback accretion. Since the start of Q3 the company repurchased $130 million of common and preferred stock, bringing YTD repurchases to nearly $200 million, and it guided to a 2027 quarterly dividend requirement of $0.11-$0.12 per share, roughly 20%-30% above 2026. The main blemish was EBITDA margin expansion of only 50 bps, which management attributed to renovation work at Hilton Key West and one-time items, estimating margins would have expanded nearly 200 bps excluding those impacts.

Starwood reported Q3 distributable earnings of $0.31 per share, or $0.41 excluding realized gains/losses from commercial lending resolution, with undepreciated book value of $17.22 per share. The quarter carried a $369 million reserve increase ($337M CECL to $822M, plus $32M REO to $217M) driven by the third-party macro model after the 10-year rose 80 bps, and four- and five-rated loans rose $290M and $440M respectively. Management reaffirmed its over-$800 million 2026 resolution target, noted no new non-accruals or foreclosures for a second straight quarter, repurchased $108M of stock, and grew the commercial lending portfolio to a record $17.8 billion. Barry Sternlicht argued the stock implies a 58% loss on the $4.5 billion of four/five-rated loans and REO, while flagging higher rates and a cautious borrower environment.

Q3 FY2026 GAAP NII was $35.3 million ($0.32/share, in line with the base dividend) versus $42.2 million last quarter, on total investment income of $75.0 million versus $83.7 million, reflecting a smaller portfolio post-deleveraging and new non-accruals. NAV per share fell $0.36 to $11.70, driven by $0.36/share of net realized and unrealized losses concentrated in older vintage positions. Non-accruals rose to 4.2% of fair value from 2.9% (7.3% at amortized cost from 5%), and portfolio company count on non-accrual grew from 10 to 11. Net debt to equity was cut to 1.21x from 1.35x, ~$15 million of shares were repurchased under the $75 million authorization, and the board declared a Q4 base dividend of $0.32 per share.

Gran Tierra reported a Q3 2026 net loss of $42 million versus $25 million net income in the prior quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of $68 million (down from $85 million QoQ), funds flow of $32 million (down 48% QoQ), and oil sales of $168 million (down 10% QoQ but up 13% YoY). Production averaged 39,904 boe/d, roughly 4% lower QoQ and 7% lower YoY, as lower Brent and wider South American differentials reduced cash flow by about $17 million and total opex rose 24% to $64 million. The quarter was dominated by the proposed ~$1.33 billion sale of the Colombian and Ecuadorian business to Maurel & Prom, which received stockholder approval and is targeted to close before year-end, plus ratification of the Azerbaijan SOCAR agreement and a new Q1 2027 hedge. Management signaled that shareholder returns and the 2027 budget will be set by the board shortly after closing.

Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income was $35.5M or $0.20/share versus $30.7M or $0.18 a year ago, but that GAAP result was lifted by ~$64M pre-tax of ASB realized/unrealized gains and burdened by a $50.7M Pacific Current impairment. Core net income and EPS fell to $23M and $0.13 from $32.8M and $0.19, with utility core net income of $27.6M versus $39.6M, driven largely by $13.7M of pre-tax hurricane storm costs now embedded in both GAAP and core results. Management filed in October to defer those storm costs for Z-factor recovery, with a PUC decision requested by December 15, 2026, and said a favorable ruling would reverse qualifying expenses in Q4. The pending rate rebasing request (5.3% base rate increase over two years) remains unresolved, with an illustrative PUC schedule pointing to new rates in early May 2027 and $83M of additional 2027 revenue if fully granted.

Q3 2026 total revenue fell 18.7% to $217.6 million from $267.8 million, with hospital division revenue down 19.7% and same-hospital revenue down 20.1%; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA fell to $63.9 million from $98.5 million and net income to $40.2 million from $55.4 million. Management attributed the decline largely to lapping the 2025 recognition uplift from IDR collections (collection percentage rising to ~80%), and said revenue per visit should remain in the ~$4,200 range absent changes. Offsets include hospital visits up 18.1% (same-hospital +12.4%), population health revenue up ~13% to $8.5 million, cash of $249.9 million and 9-month operating cash flow of $188.1 million, plus improving IDR case law and CMS audit findings. No formal guidance was given, though management signaled possible future disclosure of 2027 detail.

Plains reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $711 million, with Q4 implied at about $700 million (down ~$10 million) as lower market opportunities and Silver Creek transition costs offset growth. Full-year EBITDA guidance is narrowed to ±$50 million around a $2.88 billion midpoint, with expectations at or slightly above midpoint. The quarter included the $1.5 billion junior subordinated notes raise and preferred redemption (adding ~$60 million, or $0.09/unit, annual DCF), a new 270,000-acre Permian Midland dedication (contributing late 2027/early 2028), and the closed Silver Spur/Powder River acquisition. Permian production growth is now expected toward the high end of prior range (~200,000 bbl/d exit-to-exit 2026), but no 2027 guidance was given until February.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Vistra reported record Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.378 billion, up more than 50% YoY, with generation contributing $2.280 billion (vs $1.544 billion) on realized prices more than 10% higher per MWh, higher capacity revenue, and the Martin Lake Unit 1 restart. Retail added roughly $98 million; YTD adjusted EBITDA reached about $5.639 billion, up over 35%. 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $7.1-7.5 billion and FCF before growth to $4.3-4.7 billion with higher midpoints, and initial 2027 guidance was set at $7.7-8.5 billion EBITDA and $4.3-5.1 billion FCF. Management flagged softer near-term ERCOT forwards tied to slower load interconnection and a data center permitting pause, while reaffirming 4-6% ERCOT and 2-3% PJM load growth through 2030.

Orion reported Q3 2026 total revenues of $35.4 million, down from $37.1 million a year earlier, with a net loss of $3.3 million ($0.06/share) versus $69 million ($1.23/share) in Q3 2025. Core FFO rose to $11.4 million ($0.20/share) from $11 million ($0.19/share), and full-year Core FFO guidance was raised to $0.75-$0.78 from $0.72-$0.77, with net debt/EBITDA guidance improved to 5.8x-6.4x from 6x-6.8x. Occupancy improved to 78.3% from 72.1% a year ago and year-to-date leasing reached roughly 922,000 sq ft, but an analyst flagged significant contemplated Q4 deceleration and the strategic options process remains open with no assurance of a transaction. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $16.5 million from $17.4 million on fewer assets, while G&A was roughly flat at $4.7 million including $266,000 of strategic-review costs.

Wheaton reported Q3 2026 production of 231,000 GEOs (+13% YoY) and sales of 192,000 GEOs (+19%), generating revenue of $772 million (+62% YoY) on a 36% higher realized GEO price. Net earnings rose 12% to $410 million while adjusted net earnings rose 46% to $410 million, and operating cash flow was roughly $645 million; net debt fell from about $1.9 billion to $1.5 billion after a $372 million revolver repayment. 2026 production guidance of 860,000-940,000 GEOs was left unchanged with YTD output of about 640,000 GEOs, and the 1.2 million GEO target for 2030 and 2031-2035 was maintained. Management flagged a significant Q4 Salobo grade recovery and a sizable Peñasquito silver decline, both already embedded in plans, while noting first production from Koné and Kurmuk is not yet in the Q4 forecast.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $289.3M from $306.5M, adjusted EBITDA dropped to $82.2M from $97.8M, and adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 28.4% from 31.9%, though adjusted diluted EPS held roughly flat at $1.39 versus $1.40 on buybacks. Results were described as broadly in line with prior expectations. Q4 guidance calls for revenue down low-to-mid single digits YoY (similar or slightly better than Q3), EBITDA margin in the low-to-mid 30s versus prior year, and EPS up slightly. Organic Google referrals fell ~37% YoY after a ~23% drop a year earlier, a two-year decline over 50%, while management noted sequential margin improvement of 160 bps and a projected 10% year-end headcount reduction.

Franklin Templeton reported Q4 FY2026 adjusted operating revenue of $1.88 billion (up 3.7% QoQ) with adjusted EPS of $0.94, up 30.6% sequentially, and Q4 adjusted operating margin of 31.8%, up 380 bps QoQ and 580 bps YoY. Full-year adjusted operating income rose 23% to $2.02 billion and adjusted operating margin expanded 350 bps to 28%, with FY adjusted EPS up 38.3% to $3.07. Management guided Q1 FY2027 EFR to the mid-37 bps range and set a FY2027 adjusted operating margin target of approximately 30%, two years ahead of the original plan, while raising FY2029 targets for private markets fundraising to $150 billion, ETFs to $200 billion, Canvas to $100 billion, and the Q4 FY2029 margin goal to 35%. The company generated $84.1 billion in long-term net inflows for the year, with positive long-term flows in every quarter across every region and both channels.

Oklo reported a pre-revenue quarter: a year-to-date net loss of $123.3 million and an operating loss of $195.2 million, with operating cash use of $110.9 million and capex of $280.9 million through Q3 2026. The company held $3.1 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable securities after raising $2.3 billion through ATM offerings, and reaffirmed full-year guidance for operating cash use of $120-150 million and PP&E spend of $400-500 million. Management disclosed that Aurora-INL first-of-a-kind timing now spans 2028-2029, describing a modest pushout tied to commissioning and electrical-noise calibration lessons from Groves-1, and PJM withdrew one Virginia interconnection application with FERC dismissing Oklo's complaint. Tone was highly promotional around Groves-1 ($65 million build plus roughly $10 million of fuel) and fleet milestones, but there are no revenue, EPS, or margin results to score.

Canopy Growth reported Q2 FY2027 consolidated net revenue of CAD 81.4 million, up 22% year-over-year, with cannabis revenue up 30% to CAD 66.2 million and international revenue up 141% to CAD 12.3 million. Adjusted gross margin held at 31% versus 33% a year earlier, reflecting the Veterans Affairs Canada reimbursement cap, while SG&A rose only CAD 3.4 million despite absorbing MTL, and Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to CAD 2.9 million from CAD 3.3 million in Q1. Management reiterated its expectation of positive Adjusted EBITDA in the second half of the fiscal year, with full cultivation and manufacturing benefits landing in fiscal 2028. Storz & Bickel revenue fell 4% to CAD 15.1 million on soft consumer spending, and free cash outflow was CAD 15.6 million, an improvement of CAD 3.7 million year-over-year.

NOG reported record quarterly production (up 7% sequentially, 19% YoY) and record Adjusted EBITDA (up 11% QoQ, 15% YoY), with oil volumes up 10% sequentially and gas up 39% YoY. Cash margin per BOE improved to $30.74 on tighter oil differentials under $3/bbl and gas realizations at 98% of Henry Hub (versus 90% in Q2), and free cash flow rose 25% YoY to roughly $150 million. Full-year 2026 production guidance was raised to 147,000-150,000 BOE/day, with the capital budget of $850-900 million trending toward the high end and production expense guidance reset to $9.75-9.85 per BOE, above the prior range. Leverage fell below 1.5x net debt to LQA EBITDA a quarter early after a $500 million 7.5% notes offering, with total liquidity over $1.6 billion and buybacks of ~668,000 shares at an average of $23.96.

HHH's first full quarter as a combined real estate/insurance company showed solid operating trends against noisy GAAP results: same-store NOI grew 9% and operating asset NOI rose 8% to $73 million, Vantage's combined ratio was 94.9% (in line with 95% a year ago) with net income up 22% to ~$80 million and pre-tax income of $103 million, but MPC EBT fell to $89.5 million from $205 million on a prior-year 231-acre bulk land sale and a $19.4 million non-cash remeasurement loss, plus a $105.4 million GAAP loss from watching MUD receivables for $177 million of cash. G&A rose from $34 million to $51.6 million on Vantage consolidation and higher interest expense. Management gave no formal numeric guidance, but reiterated the asset-light/JV strategy with roughly a couple billion of potential proceeds by end-2027, flagged property reinsurance pricing as softening into a Stage 3/4 cycle, and noted Melia's 15% pre-sold in ~30 days versus 60-70% in 60 days historically.

Total investment income of $35.5 million was relatively unchanged year over year and sequentially; ANII before taxes was $16.3 million, or $0.36 per share, down from $17 million a year ago, and the $0.34 ANII figure was aided by approximately $600,000 of voluntary advisory fee waivers. NAV per share rose $0.05 to $16.56, and net increase in net assets was $18.1 million, or $0.40 per share, including $5.2 million of net fair value appreciation and an $11 million realized gain on the Core Transformers exit. Private loan investments fell by a net $11 million on slower-than-expected originations, and the declared Q1 2027 total dividend of $0.36 per share (including a $0.03 supplemental) is unchanged from prior quarters. Management characterized the pipeline as well above average and expects a significant origination move in Q4, while acknowledging quarterly origination is inherently lumpy and spreads have been flat since roughly March/April.

MSDL reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $40.3 million, or $0.48 per share, up from $0.45 in the prior quarter, while total investment income fell to $86.1 million from $88.8 million. NAV per share declined to $18.76 from $19.50, driven by $67.6 million in net unrealized depreciation and realized losses tied to the BrightPet restructuring and three new non-accruals ($17.2 million at cost). Management announced a management fee cut to 75 bps (from 100) and an incentive fee cut to 15% (from 17.5%) effective January 1, 2027, quantified as roughly 64 bps of NII return on NAV and about $0.03 of quarterly NII per share, and initiated a supplemental dividend ($0.015) alongside the $0.45 regular. New-deal median spreads widened to 538 bps from 475 bps, and the Capstone JV reached roughly 65% utilization, with full JV ramp still targeted for mid-2027.

Moderna reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.3 billion, up 29% year-over-year, with net income of $162 million and diluted EPS of $0.38 versus a $0.51 loss per share a year ago. The company raised its full-year revenue growth framework to 15%-25% from prior guidance of up to 10% growth, cut R&D guidance by $200 million to $2.7 billion, and lifted year-end cash guidance to $8.1-$8.3 billion. The quarter included FDA approval of mFLUSIVA, the first mRNA flu vaccine to reach the U.S. market, and positive Phase III intismeran melanoma data showing a 42% reduction in recurrence or death risk (HR 0.58). Offsetting these, the company declined to enroll an additional norovirus cohort after missing interim success criteria and deferred the MMA pivotal trial until after the PA readout.

Total revenue rose 7.5% to $208 million and YTD revenue of $583 million was up 14%, but Q4 guidance was explicitly tempered: sequential growth expected yet management is 'measured' and cites rate volatility plus a harder bonus depreciation comp. Adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $8.2 million in the quarter; net income was $1 million or $0.03 per share, and cost of services rose 160 bps to 64% of revenue on larger-transaction mix. The key change versus prior periods is tone around deal conversion: the 10-year moved ~80 bps in the quarter, widening bid-ask spreads and pressuring Private Client growth to just 4% against a 17% prior-year comp, while Middle Market (+17%) and large transactions (+20%) carried the quarter. Management frames 2027 as a maturing-debt catalyst with near-record inventory but no explicit numeric guidance.

Main Street reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $142.5 million, up 1.9% YoY but down 4.7% QoQ, with DNII before taxes per share of $0.98 in line with prior guidance but $0.09 below the year-ago quarter and $0.10 below Q2. NAV per share rose $0.30 (0.9%) QoQ to a record $34.22, aided by $40.9 million of net fair value appreciation, and annualized ROE was 14.7%. Q4 DNII before taxes guidance is at least $0.98 per share with potential upside, and the board declared a $0.30 supplemental dividend plus a 3.8% increase in Q1 2027 monthly dividends to $0.27. LMM investment activity was slow with a net $19 million decrease in the LMM portfolio, while the private loan pipeline was described as well above average versus an average LMM pipeline.

Q3 FY2026 revenue of $186 million exceeded the high end of guidance, up 11% sequentially and 11% year over year versus a ~7% rise in the average Lower 48 land rig count. Adjusted EBITDA rose 33% sequentially to $25 million (13.4% margin, up from 11.2% in Q2 and 12.7% in Q3 2025), with all three segments growing and Rockies segment Adjusted EBITDA doubling to $12.6 million on a 21.5% margin. The rights offering closed, cutting debt by about $101 million, lowering net leverage to 2.5x from 3.9x and lifting liquidity to $78 million. Q4 revenue guidance is $172-$184 million (about 14% growth at the midpoint), with management flagging a less severe seasonal decline but continued uneven gas-directed activity.

IAG reported Q3 revenue of $856.5 million from 199,900 oz sold at $4,277/oz realized, adjusted EBITDA of $503.9 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.42 versus $0.30 a year prior. Attributable production of 186,900 oz brought YTD to 558,600 oz, with consolidated production guidance unchanged but Côté now guided to the low end of 390,000-440,000 oz (100% basis) and Côté cash costs ex-royalties above the top end of the $900-$1,050/oz range. The company sits in a net cash position with $766.6 million cash and ~$1.6 billion liquidity, has repurchased 32.1 million shares for $592.6 million since December 2025, and will spend ~$525 million to watch back half the Franco-Nevada Côté royalty, cutting the effective gross margin royalty to 2.14% and Côté cash costs by ~$150/oz from 2027. Unit costs at Côté remain above target, offsetting a strong September in which the plant ran 37,100 tpd at $15.36/t milling.

Helios reported record Q3 sales of $230 million, up 4% reported and 13% pro forma, exceeding the high end of its outlook by $8 million, with adjusted EPS up 11% to $0.80 ($0.03 above the high end). Both segments contributed: Hydraulics rose 15% pro forma with margin down 20 bps to 32.3%, Electronics rose 10% with gross margin up 40 bps to 34.7%. FY2026 sales guidance was raised to $895-902 million (13% pro forma growth, a record year) while the adjusted EBITDA margin (20.2-20.4%) and EPS ($3.08-3.15) ranges were tightened rather than lifted, reflecting inflation and Radio Sound integration costs. Q4 guidance of $205-212 million implies roughly flat to down 3% reported, with management flagging an extra week in the prior-year quarter and $4-5 million of orders pulled forward into Q3 ahead of price increases.

Q3 2026 revenue was $40.0 million, up $0.3 million year-over-year, while a $24.6 million foreign currency transaction loss from redeeming the ILS 3 bond drove a reported net loss of $14.8 million; excluding that item, net income was approximately $9.8 million, up about $1 million, or 11%. Year-to-date revenue rose 4.5% to $120 million, AFFO was $55.9 million versus 2025 (+$2.5 million), and management reiterated 2026 projected AFFO of $74.5 million (+11.1%) and adjusted EBITDA of $129.5 million (+14%). The company collected 100% of contractual rents, held rent coverage at 2.24x, and kept the Q4 dividend flat at $0.17 per share. Management guided to roughly $123 million of acquisitions closing before year-end and a $400 million pipeline, plus an imminent $90 million tenant option purchase that will recycle about $83 million of net cash into new deals.

Consolidated service revenue of CAD 4.5 billion fell 1% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1.8 billion declined 5% (down 2% normalized for CAD 78 million of prior-year one-time items). Adjusted EPS fell to CAD 0.16 from CAD 0.24 and free cash flow dropped 35% to CAD 396 million; basic EPS was negative CAD 0.42 on an CAD 800 million non-cash TELUS Health goodwill impairment. FY2026 guidance was fully reaffirmed as updated in July (service revenue flat to -2%, adjusted EBITDA -2% to -4%, capex ~CAD 2.6 billion, FCF ~CAD 1.8 billion), with no raise. Management paired the soft numbers with a new CAD 900 million annualized cash savings program exiting 2028 (~50/50 capex and EBITDA, up to 80% telecom) and an AI/asset-monetization strategy; leverage stood at 3.6x versus a 3x-or-lower target by end-2028.

Banco de Chile reported Q3 net income of CLP 288 billion with ROAE of 19.9% and 9M net income of CLP 947 billion, up 2.2% year-on-year. Q3 revenue rose 3% year-on-year to CLP 758 billion, NIM was 4.4% versus 4.3% a year earlier, cost of risk was 0.96%, and the efficiency ratio was 39.1% for the quarter, temporarily lifted by a collective-bargaining bonus. Management raised full-year ROAC guidance to 22% from a 21%-22% range and improved the efficiency target to about 36% from 37%, while trimming nominal loan growth guidance to 5%-6% from about 6% and lifting the NIM forecast to 4.8% from 4.6%. The raised profitability guidance incorporates a CLP 68 billion tax charge in October tied to deferred tax assets.

NAV per share was $10.92 vs $10.94 at June 30, with NII of $27.2 million ($0.26/share) down from $0.28 last quarter and just covering the $0.26 dividend; the decline was attributed to lower dividend income from equity positions and a higher income-based incentive fee. The $0.26 Q4 dividend was declared unchanged, supported by $0.80/share of spillover income, though management confirmed funding costs will rise as the 3.3% notes are replaced by a $400 million CLO at SOFR+164, removing the November maturity. Credit quality softened modestly: risk-rated 4 and 5 assets rose to 7% of the portfolio from 6%, non-accruals ticked up to 1.1% (0.7% ex-Sierra), and PIK rose to ~10% of revenue from 7%, largely tied to one non-standard auto insurer now on PIK.

Concentra reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $622.1 million, up 8.6% YoY, with net income of $67.8 million ($0.52 per share) up 36% and Adjusted EBITDA of $140.2 million, up 17.9%, at a 22.5% margin (up 178 bps). Visits per day rose 4.9% to over 58,000, revenue per visit rose 3.3%, and growth was broad-based across all six regions. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.36-2.38 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $505-510 million, while free cash flow ($220-240 million) and capex ($70-80 million) ranges were unchanged. Q3 operating cash flow fell to $51.9 million from $60.6 million and free cash flow declined to $32.2 million from $40.2 million on working capital timing and higher cash taxes.

Calumet reported Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA with Tax Attributes of $347 million, with Specialty Products and Solutions at $248.1 million (more than triple the prior-year $80.2 million) and Montana Renewables at a record $80.4 million. Specialty material margin reached over $108 per barrel versus $62 a year ago, and consolidated net leverage fell to approximately 3x from over 9x at the start of last year. Management guided Q4 specialty EBITDA to remain roughly similar to Q3 outside normal seasonality, completed the Shreveport turnaround on time and budget, and began the MaxSAF tie-in at Montana Renewables with SAF run-rate targets of 80 million gallons by year-end and 120-150 million by end-2027. The main offset was Performance Brands Adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million versus $13.2 million a year ago on 60-90 day pricing lags.

Pro forma consolidated revenue fell 1.5% YoY and adjusted EBITDA declined 4% (3% ex-Cox transition costs), with pro forma residential revenue down 4.1% and residential revenue per customer relationship down 1.6%. Legacy Charter lost 156,000 internet subscribers versus 109,000 a year ago, and Legacy Cox lost 77,000, though mobile added 440,000 lines and video losses narrowed to 38,000 from 70,000. Management announced a new operating model with an incremental $2 billion of annualized opex savings over 18 months on top of more than $1 billion of Cox transaction synergies, and reaffirmed 2026 pro forma capex of ~$13 billion with 2027 at or below $11 billion. Pro forma net loss was $2.1 billion, driven by a ~$6.3 billion non-cash franchise impairment, partly offset by a $1.4 billion debt exchange gain; free cash flow was $674 million and leverage was 3.93x against a 3.5x target within three years of close.

CGBD reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $63 million, up from $62 million last quarter, and net investment income of $25 million, or $0.36 per share on both GAAP and adjusted bases, fully covering the $0.35 base dividend. NAV rose to $15.65 per share from $15.61, and the board declared a Q4 dividend of $0.35 while reauthorizing the $300 million buyback through November 2027; $6.1 million of shares were repurchased at a 32% average discount. Origination volume was muted ($81 million funded excluding JV activity) amid macro and geopolitical uncertainty, with management flagging continued softness in Q4 but more optimism for the first half of 2027. Two positions were added to non-accrual, bringing non-accruals to 1.1% of investments at fair value, and the SCP JV's 20.3% dividend yield was again inflated by delayed loan settlements, expected to normalize to mid-teens.

Q3 total revenue was $944M vs $929M, but roughly $13M came from a gift card breakage accounting change, leaving revenue essentially flat excluding that item. U.S. comps rose 1.9% on a 3.7% check increase while traffic fell 1.8%, and adjusted diluted loss widened to $0.17 per share from $0.03 last year, with adjusted operating margin down ~50 bps to 0.3% and restaurant margin down ~20 bps to 9.3%. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was tightened and raised to $0.97-$1.02 from $0.90-$1.00, but Q4 comps were guided to only 0%-1% with a ~2% traffic headwind and delayed pricing actions at Outback and Bonefish pushing Q4 EPS to $0.07-$0.12. An Outback franchisee, Out West, filed for bankruptcy and the company signed a stalking horse agreement for its 61 restaurants.

Brookdale reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $124.3 million, up 12% YoY and in line with its low-double-digit pacing, but RevPAR growth of 7.5% came in below the ~8.2% anticipated, and same-community occupancy rose only 70 bps sequentially versus internal expectations during the peak summer watching season. Management lowered full-year guidance to Adjusted EBITDA of $495-502 million and RevPAR growth of 7.4-7.9%, replacing the prior 8-9% RevPAR target, citing weaker occupancy pull-through, a modest Q4 marketing increase, and a few-million-dollar impact from the Clinton, Mississippi fire. Offsets included same-community operating margin up 50 bps to 29.2%, labor as a percentage of revenue improving 120 bps YoY, G&A down 15% YoY to $36.6 million, and leverage improving to 8.3x from 8.4x. Management reiterated confidence in mid-teens Adjusted EBITDA growth for 2027 and beyond.

Fee-related earnings rose 15% YoY to $864 million ($0.54/share) and distributable earnings rose 15% to $763 million ($0.47/share) on fee-bearing capital of $682 billion, up 13% over 12 months; $25 billion raised in the quarter and $123 billion year-to-date. Infrastructure fundraising hit roughly $50 billion, including $26 billion for the sixth flagship, which is on track to exceed its $30 billion target in early 2027. However, management said full-year earnings would be modestly below what was expected at the start of the year, citing the flagship's fee start pushed to January 1 and the BBU performance fee no longer expected in 2026 on the high-water mark. FRE margin was 54% for the quarter (55% trailing 12 months), with the first meaningful shareholder carry realization of $48 million.

Aura Minerals reported record quarterly revenue of $386 million (up 15% QoQ) and adjusted EBITDA of $237 million, with production of 96,000 gold-equivalent ounces (up 27% QoQ) driving the improvement; nine-month production was 253,000 oz. Management reiterated full-year production guidance of 340,000-390,000 oz and said AISC of $1,953/oz should meet full-year guidance, though year-to-date AISC is above guidance and Apoena's costs were elevated. Net income fell to $135 million from $165 million in Q2 due to a smaller non-cash gold hedge gain, while adjusted net income rose to $120 million from $97 million; recurring free cash flow was $124 million and the company declared a $0.72 dividend.

Anika reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $30.6M, up 10% YoY from $27.8M, with commercial channel revenue up 17% to a record $14M and OEM up 5% to $16.6M. Gross margin expanded to 62% from 56% a year ago but fell sequentially from 65% on mix, including the Hyalomatrix reintroduction. Adjusted EPS was $0.29 versus a GAAP loss of $0.02; adjusted EBITDA was $5.1M versus $0.9M a year ago. For FY2026, total revenue growth guidance was raised only at the low end to 6%-10% (from 5%-10%), OEM raised to 5%-9% (from 0%-5%) while commercial was trimmed to 9%-13% (from 12%-18%) on softer U.S. elective surgery trends, and adjusted EBITDA margin was raised to 15%-17% (from 13%-17%); 2027 guidance was reaffirmed at flat to 5% growth. Hyalofast's U.S. PMA was deemed not approvable by the FDA in October.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA rose to $29.4 million from $25.6 million in Q2 on 3.9 million tons shipped, up from 3.5 million tons, while met segment cost of coal sales increased to $106.93 per ton from $103.07. Realizations were roughly flat, with total weighted average met price of $124.52 versus $124.30. The company issued 2027 guidance of 13.1-14.1 million met tons, cost of coal sales of $104-$110 per ton, and capex of $145-$165 million, alongside a 2027 domestic book of 3.5 million tons at $135.48 per ton. DTA's damaged stacker reclaimer will be replaced rather than repaired on a roughly two-year timeline, and management noted 2026 met tons at the guidance midpoint are 87% committed and priced at $126.69 per ton.

Skyward reported Q3 operating EPS of $1.28 (up 22%), gross written premiums up 9% to $803 million and fee-generating GWP up 18% to $517 million. Consolidated combined ratio was 89.9 (88.1 ex-cat) with a 62.6 loss ratio including 1.5 points of cat losses, and Skyward Specialty's expense ratio improved to 25.7. Full-year growth is on track near the upper end of the original $2.65-$2.8 billion guidance range, while 2027 guidance was deferred to the Q4 call. Management flagged a lower net earned premium true-up from dairy/livestock take-up weakness, softer pricing (mid-single-digit ex-property), and a more competitive property/casualty environment. No prior-year reserve development was recognized; IBNR reached a record 77% of total reserves.

AHR reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO of $0.58 per diluted share, up 31.8% year-over-year, on total same-store NOI growth of 13.8% (accelerating from 13.2% in Q2). Management raised full-year 2026 NFFO per share guidance to $2.23-$2.26 from $2.15-$2.19, implying over 30% growth at the midpoint, and lifted same-store NOI guidance to 12%-14%, including a 500 bps raise for SHOP to 23%-26%. Net debt to annualized adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.9x, and the company closed about $1.69 billion of investments in the quarter, bringing year-to-date completions to $2.1 billion, with a $1 billion-plus awarded pipeline excluded from guidance.

Adjusted operating income fell to $86 million ($1.94/share) from $124 million ($2.57/share) a year ago, with last year's quarter boosted by a $30 million loss-expense benefit versus just a $2 million benefit this year. Net earned premiums and credit derivative revenues rose to $114 million from $98 million, and economic loss development was a $27 million benefit helped by Brightline. New business PVP reached $280 million in the first nine months, up 44% YoY, and management guided to more than $400 million of full-year financial guaranty PVP, signaling confidence in a pipeline of shorter-duration fund finance deals.

Ameren reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $2.42 versus $2.35 GAAP and $2.17 adjusted in Q3 2025, driven by higher sales, favorable weather (warmest St. Louis quarter in over 50 years), energy technology earnings and infrastructure investment returns, partly offset by higher O&M. Management raised 2026 EPS guidance to $5.35-$5.55 from $5.25-$5.45 and initiated 2027 guidance of $5.70-$5.90, an 8.4% midpoint increase over original 2026 guidance. It also raised long-term outlook to 8%-10% EPS CAGR from 2027-2031 and grew the five-year capital plan above 20% to $38.1 billion, supporting 13.3% rate base CAGR. Weather-normalized trailing-twelve-month Missouri retail sales grew only about 0.5%, and the plan relies on embedded 2.8-2.9 GW of signed electric service agreements.

Q3 2026 core FFO came in at $1.71/share, $0.02 above the $1.69 guidance midpoint, on higher third-party construction fees and interest income, while blended effective lease rates turned positive at +1.0% (new leases -2.0%, renewals +3.6%). Full-year core FFO midpoint was maintained at $6.75, but same-store guidance was trimmed: revenue growth to 0.0% from 0.5%, NOI growth to -1.0% from -0.6%, partly offset by expense growth improving to 1.75% from 2.5%.
