Q4 core FFO is guided to $1.63-$1.67 (midpoint $1.65), down $0.06 sequentially largely on the loss of California NOI and lower fees, and the company canceled two acquisitions and one land parcel and shelved two development projects.

Q3 revenue was $399 million at the high end of the outlook, recurring revenue $359 million also at the high end, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 beat the top of the range by $0.11. Total ARR grew 1% (2% constant currency) and cloud ARR grew 11%, while Q3 recurring revenue declined year-over-year against a first-half-skewed linearity comparison. FY26 revenue range was narrowed to the high end (-1% to 0%), recurring revenue to 1%-2%, and EPS guidance raised to $2.86-$2.90 with operating margin expansion now seen at ~200 bps versus 100 bps expected at the start of the year. Q4 guidance calls for recurring revenue down 2%-4% and total revenue down 4%-6% on upfront-recognition timing.

Taseko (TGB) reported Q3 F2026 revenue of CAD 342 million, up 100% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 161 million (a quarterly record) and cash flow from operations of CAD 122 million; consolidated copper sales were 37.4 million pounds. 2026 production guidance was raised by 5 million pounds to 115-120 million pounds, but management guided Q4 lower due to the transition to oxidized ore at Gibraltar, with recoveries averaging 77% and costs at $2.72/lb. Florence Copper produced 7 million pounds (up 35% QoQ) and C1 costs fell 25% to $3.54/lb, though sulfuric acid costs are expected to rise next year and leverage remains about 1x net debt/EBITDA.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 11% YoY to $152.9 million as behavioral subscription revenue dropped 22% to $113.9 million, partly offset by clinical revenue up 48% to $38 million (about 25% of total). Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $51.7 million at a 33.8% margin (vs 24.9%), net income was $15.1 million, and operating cash flow was $32.3 million. Total subscribers were about 2.3 million, with behavioral down 26% YoY to 2.1 million while Core+ grew to 546,000 (16% YoY growth, fourth straight sequential gain) and clinical fell sequentially to 174,000 from 197,000. Full-year guidance was narrowed: revenue $625-630 million (from $620-635 million) and adjusted EBITDA $110-115 million (from $105-115 million), with adjusted gross margin now about 74% versus prior expectation of above 72%.

TransMedics reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $203M, up 41% YoY (organic $194M, up 35%), the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with product revenue of $113M (+29%) and service revenue of $90M (+60%). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51 and adjusted operating margin 14.2%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $764M-$774M from $737M-$757M (26%-28% growth), inclusive of ~$14M from PAD Aviation, while the adjusted operating margin range of 12.5%-14% was maintained and no contribution from ENHANCE Part B or DENOVO is assumed.

Millicom reported Q3 2026 service revenue of $2.1 billion, up 6.1% reported and 5.4% organically (fourth consecutive mid-single-digit organic quarter), with adjusted EBITDA at a record $1.1 billion, up 7.7% organically at a 48% margin despite ~$30 million of severance. Equity free cash flow reached $316 million, up ~30% YoY, bringing nine-month EFCF to ~$870 million and leverage down to 2.53. Full-year guidance was maintained at ~$1.1 billion EFCF and sub-2.5x leverage, though management flagged Q4 margin moderation in Ecuador and continued home subscriber pressure. Key changes versus prior periods include the completed Colombia brand consolidation with a four-year investment plan, an Ecuador brand launch, a Guatemala litigation settlement, and home net losses of 86,000 driven by the Colombia earthquake and the deliberate more-for-more pricing strategy.

TripAdvisor reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $436 million, down 11% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million (16% of revenue). Experiences revenue fell 3% with segment EBITDA down 440 bps to 13% of revenue, while Hotels and Other revenue dropped 23% to $152 million and segment EBITDA fell ~650 bps to 22%. Management guided Q4 group revenue to decline in the low teens and group adjusted EBITDA margins to step down to low-to-mid single digits, with Experiences EBITDA roughly break-even. The quarter included a $369 million goodwill impairment in H&O, a global restructuring targeting ~$40 million in group annualized savings, and the announced CEO and CFO departures.

Watts reported Q3 sales of $728 million, up 19% reported and 12% organic, with adjusted operating margin expanding 240 bps to 20.9% and adjusted EPS of $3.40, up 36% YoY. The company raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 11%-12% (two points at the midpoint) and lifted adjusted EBITDA and operating margin outlook by 25 bps at the midpoint, while Q4 revenue guidance of 11%-14% reported with organic 9%-12% was below the Q3 organic rate. Growth was led by data centers, notably in APMEA (+30% organic) and Americas (+12% organic), offsetting continued weakness in residential and non-institutional new construction.

Q3 FY2026 medical-only revenue of $230 million rose 4% YoY and 4% QoQ versus medical-only baselines of $221 million and $222 million, exceeding guidance and outperforming seasonal trends on Georgia and Pennsylvania growth. Gross margin was 64%, up ~1 point YoY and sequentially, adjusted EBITDA was $89 million (39% margin), and operating cash flow was $74 million against $29 million of capex for $45 million free cash flow; net income was only $1 million, or $18 million / $0.09 per share excluding non-recurring items. Q4 revenue guidance is up low single digits sequentially with gross margin comparable to recent quarters but pressured by holiday promotions, and purchase accounting from the Harvest deconsolidation is expected to drive a fourth-quarter net loss; FY2026 operating cash flow is guided to at least $225 million while capex rises to ~$105 million from ~$95 million. Prior framing on 280E is unchanged, with the uncertain tax position covering 2019 to present including $102 million of IRS refunds and interest.

Total revenue of $601 million rose 6% YoY and beat the $585 million outlook; adjusted EBITDA of $234 million topped the $232 million guide at a 38.8% margin, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.29 versus $0.25 prior year. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $2.34 billion and net CAPEX to $400 million, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was held at $920 million as higher Q4 activations, transfers and D&I mix dilute flow-through. Modular units on rent inflected up 1.2% YoY, the first growth in five years, and the modular order book is up over 20% YoY, supporting initial 2027 views of low single-digit organic revenue and mid-single-digit organic EBITDA growth.

Q3 revenue was $244.7M, up 10.4% and within guidance, with retail +12.4% and e-commerce +4.8%; adjusted gross margin 54.6% (+40 bps) and adjusted EBITDA $28.6M at 11.7% of revenue (+10 bps). Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $966-976M (11%-12% growth) and now includes up to 1 point of Intelligent Eyewear contribution, with adjusted EBITDA of $117-119M; Q4 revenue guided to $243-253M (15%-20% growth) on a much larger marketing and launch spend. Active customers grew only 3% and management flagged softer September trends, weak category units, and pressure on cash-pay consumers, offset by eye exams +30%, insurance +22%, and the Nov 12 Intelligent Eyewear pre-order launch. Guidance was nudged with a new product contribution rather than raised on the core business.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $263M, up 17% YoY and $1M above the high end of guidance, with subscription revenue also up 17% to $246M. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 18.3%, 85 bps above the high end of guidance and up 560 bps YoY, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.72 (up from $0.46) reflects a newly applied 22% non-GAAP tax rate. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.041-1.044B and ~19% subscription growth remain essentially intact, with the non-GAAP operating margin outlook raised 25 bps at the midpoint to 18.2%-18.3%; management flagged that FX and sustainability tailwinds have subsided, contributing to a Q4 revenue guide that does not fully pass through the Q3 beat. CRPO grew 17% YoY (18% in constant currency), and the >$300K contract cohort grew 31%.

Revenue rose to $26.6M from $25.3M in Q2 and $24.3M a year ago, but GAAP net income of $3.1M ($0.34/share) fell from $3.7M ($0.41) in Q3 2025 and Economic Earnings declined to $4.4M ($0.48) from $5.7M ($0.64) year over year, with $1.7M of severance and higher taxes offsetting revenue. Still, income nearly doubled sequentially from $1.5M ($0.17) and Economic Earnings rose from $3.0M ($0.33). Firmwide AUM/AUA was $17.1B, with AUM net outflows of $0.3B and market depreciation of $0.6B in the quarter. No formal guidance was issued; the board declared a $0.15 quarterly dividend, and management cited a robust pipeline, ETF assets of $430M at quarter-end (about $460M since), and roughly $30M of new private capital commitments.

WES reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $708 million, up 12% YoY but down modestly sequentially, with DCF of $512 million and net income to limited partners of $325 million. Partnership-wide natural gas throughput hit a record 5.9 Bcf/d (up 8% sequentially, Delaware up 20%), and produced water set another Delaware record. Management now expects full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA above the midpoint of its already-raised $2.75-$2.95 billion range, with DCF and FCF guidance ranges unchanged and 2027 capex expected in line with 2026. The quarter's sequential softness came from West Texas contract mix and pricing, DJ Basin declines, lower NGL/skim oil, and seasonal O&M, partially offset by a full quarter of Brazos.

Wendy's reported Q3 FY2026 global systemwide sales down 5.9% and U.S. same-restaurant sales down 5.7%, with traffic falling 11.9% offset by average check growth of 6.2%; the U.S. comp improved 130 bps sequentially from Q2. Total adjusted revenue was $435.6 million (down 1.6%), adjusted EBITDA fell $24.6 million to $113.4 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.13, with G&A up $15.2 million including $11.9 million of Dave's Way investment and a $9.1 million doubtful-accounts charge for franchisee deferrals. Management gave no formal forward guidance beyond stating Q4 has started with early improvement and that trajectory details will come on the next call; net debt leverage was 5.2x. Key changes versus prior period: a location-optional breakfast strategy worth up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA, an LOI to acquire up to 163 Meritage restaurants, and rejection of an unsolicited acquisition offer.

Viatris reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $3.75 billion, described as in line with expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.71; North America grew ~7% and Greater China ~10%, while adjusted gross margin came in above expectations at 58%. Management narrowed and raised the midpoint of 2026 guidance across all key metrics (operational growth ~2% revenue, ~6% adjusted EBITDA, ~8% adjusted EPS), excluding Pacira. Offsets included ~$100 million of Q3 supply-constraint impact from Nashik (now OAI with manufacturing suspended) and an expected ~$100 million Q4 hit, while China growth is guided to slow below 10% in Q4 and toward low-to-mid single digits in 2027. The pending Pacira acquisition (tender launched October 30, close expected before end-November) is expected to be immediately accretive in 2027 and add >$1 billion of U.S. innovative medicines revenue.

VSE reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $541 million, up 91% (about 17% organic), adjusted EBITDA of $107 million up 126%, a record 19.8% adjusted EBITDA margin (up ~310 bps), and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.01 up 49%. Free cash flow was ~$47 million versus $18 million a year ago, and adjusted net leverage fell to 2.3x from 2.4x. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 65%-66.5% from 61%-64% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.9%-19.1% from 18.7%-19%. Q4 revenue is guided lower sequentially on seasonality and a tough December 2025 comparison, and 2027 guidance is deferred to the December investor day.

Verisk reported Q3 revenue of $809 million, up 5% GAAP and 7.4% on an organic constant-currency basis, with underwriting up 7.7% and claims up 6.7%. Subscription revenue grew 8.2% OCC (84% of total) while transactional revenue rose 3.2%, which management said was modestly ahead of expectations on data overages and Life Solutions services it does not expect to repeat in Q4. Total adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 56.7%, adjusted EPS rose 14% to $1.96, and GAAP net income fell 3% to $219 million on investment losses and higher interest expense. Full-year guidance was maintained (revenue $3.19-3.24B, EBITDA $1.79-1.83B, adjusted EPS $7.45-7.75) but management said results likely land toward the midpoint of the range.

Vivmark Residential's inaugural quarter reported Q3 Core FFO of $1.03/share, reflecting AVB as accounting acquirer before the Aug 17 merger close and the combined company after it. Full-year same-store revenue guidance was raised 20 bps to 2.2%, and projected gross synergies were lifted to $185M (net $135M) from $175M/$125M, with merger costs cut to $725M from $750M and run-rate accretion rising to ~3% from 2%. Q4 Core FFO guidance is $1.03/share at the midpoint, and 2027 building blocks include ~1% embedded same-store revenue growth, ~$70M incremental development NOI and ~150 bps of development contribution to Core FFO growth. Blended rate change was 3.1% in Q3 (up 150 bps YoY), occupancy just under 96%, and turnover fell 50 bps to 12.7%.

VieMed reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $80.7 million, up 12.2% YoY and 3.3% sequentially, with net income of $4.6 million ($0.11 per diluted share) up 32% YoY and about 68% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.1 million (21.1% margin), up 6% YoY and 24% sequentially but down from 22.4% a year ago as mix shifted toward lower-margin sales and services. Full-year revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $316-$320 million from $314-$320 million, but Adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $64-$66 million from $64-$68 million, cutting the top end. Ventilator rental revenue grew 7.4% YoY to $37.5 million and PAP patients rose 37.5% YoY, while free cash flow was only $4 million on AR timing and audit-related collection delays management expects to reverse in Q4.

Victory Capital reported Q3 revenue of $396.6 million, up 10% YoY and its second highest ever, with adjusted EPS of $1.98 up 21% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 53.5%, up 80 bps YoY and above the 50% long-term guide. Record long-term net inflows of $11.7 billion (13.8% annualized organic growth) and record gross flows of $30.5 billion drove total client assets to a record $355.5 billion, up 3% QoQ and 13% YoY. The 46-47 bps full-year fee rate guidance was reiterated (46.3 bps YTD) despite a Q3 dip to 44.8 bps from annual-fee timing, and the First Eagle deal remains on track to close by end-Q1 2027 with $280 million net expense synergy and 35% accretion targets unchanged. Management said Q3 flow momentum has continued into Q4.

Energy Fuels reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $29.2 million, including $28.7 million and $17.9 million of gross profit (about 63% margin) from uranium, with 320,000 lbs sold at an $88.90/lb realized price versus a ~$34/lb cost. The quarter produced a $52.2 million net loss, or $0.20 per share, driven mainly by $35.3 million of non-cash mark-to-market losses on marketable securities plus $9 million of ASM/VAC transaction costs. Guidance was not raised: the company said it hit the low end of full-year processed-pound guidance, targets the low end of sales guidance (1.5 million lbs), and is only 'hopeful' of reaching the low end of mining guidance after Pinyon Plain grades of 1.04% came in below expectations. Strategic milestones (ASM close, VAC pending, Donald conditional AUD 180 million debt commitment) advanced, but no near-term ASM financial contribution is expected.

Unity reported Q3 FY2026 strategic revenue of $597M, up 59% YoY, with Strategic Grow of $432M (+90% YoY) driven by Vector revenue growing 126% YoY and 40% QoQ, roughly double the guided 20% sequential growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $257M at a 41% margin, up 1,800 bps YoY, and the company posted its first GAAP profit since IPO at $122M net income (20% margin), with record free cash flow of $220M and a $2.65B cash balance. Q4 guidance calls for strategic revenue of $683-691M (+65-67% YoY), Grow growth of 105-107% and adjusted EBITDA of $290-295M (42% margin), implying further acceleration from Q3.

10X Genomics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $150.7 million, up 1% year-over-year, as consumables grew 5% (spatial +16%, single-cell +1%) while total instrument revenue fell 43%. Gross margin expanded to 75% from 67% a year ago on lower inventory write-downs and mix, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $625-635 million from $610-630 million. Management also lifted its Atera shipment expectation to ~50 units by year-end from ~40, but guided Q4 gross margin down to the low-to-mid 60s as Atera instrument shipments ramp and flagged lower margins for 2027 amid an instrument-heavy year.

Total Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 20% YoY to $50.1 million, with record systems integration revenue up 75% to $16.1 million (32% of revenue vs 22% a year ago) and adjusted EBITDA up 225% to $4.7 million. Gross margin expanded 610 bps to 17.2% and net income swung to $1.1 million ($0.04 per diluted share) from a $1.5 million loss. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $21-$23 million and guided Q4 systems integration revenue above the Q3 level, with growth continuing into 2027. Procurement returned to its $20-$40 million range at $32.4 million (+4%), while facilities management revenue fell 30% YoY to $1.1 million.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $405.6 million, up 11% YoY, with subscription revenue up 14% to $287.9 million and total subscription pets up 6% to 1.145 million. Adjusted operating income hit an all-time high of $47 million (up 15%), subscription AOI was $45.4 million at a 15.8% margin, net income was $9.3 million or $0.21 per share, and free cash flow reached a record $28.5 million. FY2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $1.59-1.597 billion and total AOI guidance to $179-182 million, with the subscription revenue midpoint rising to 14% YoY growth; Q4 revenue is guided to $407-414 million. Net new pets rose over 28% YoY, retention improved for a seventh consecutive quarter to 98.38%, and the company repurchased roughly $25 million of shares during the quarter.

Wynn reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted property EBITDA of $158.8 million in Las Vegas (27.6% margin) on $575.2 million of revenue, $50.1 million in Boston (25.8% margin) on $194.7 million, and $255.3 million in Macau (27.8% margin) on $919.2 million. Las Vegas results absorbed just under $24 million of unfavorable hold plus a soft summer market, partially offset by 3% RevPAR and ADR growth and retail lease revenue up 8%; Macau VIP hold added just under $12.3 million. October trends were strong across Vegas (drop, ADR, RevPAR and retail tenant sales all up), while Macau volumes declined into month-end after a Golden Week in line with last year. Capital return continued with $58.1 million of buybacks, a $0.25/share dividend, and a $150 million Macau interim dividend (up from $125 million), and the Al Marjan Island budget and timeline (Sept 2027) were unchanged.

Molson Coors reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net sales revenue of $2.9 billion, down 1.2% YoY, underlying pre-tax income of $349 million, down 17.4%, and underlying EPS of $1.46, down 12.6%. The company cut full-year 2026 guidance across all key metrics: NSR now expected -1% to -2% (vs. prior flat +/-1%), underlying pre-tax income -21% to -24% (vs. prior -15% to -18%), underlying EPS -16% to -19% (vs. prior -11% to -15%), and underlying free cash flow to $1 billion +/-10% (vs. prior $1.1 billion +/-10%). Management cited U.S. category softness (industry down more than 4%), increased U.K. promotional activity, elevated Midwest Premium and aluminum costs, and a tighter freight market, with Midwest Premium alone driving roughly $30 million of YoY cost increase in the quarter and expected to add approximately $130 million for the full year (about 10 points of pre-tax income impact, or more than $0.50 of EPS).

Xponential reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $62.3 million, down 21% from $78.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $24.3 million, down 27% or $9.2 million year-over-year. Same-store sales fell 7.5% overall and 5.6% at Club Pilates, while North America systemwide sales of $424 million declined 2%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $250-260 million and systemwide sales of $1.70-1.75 billion were unchanged, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $91-94 million and net new studio openings cut to 124-130. Management cited a softer Q4 consumer backdrop, a tighter real estate environment, and continued merchandise logistics disruption, while announcing a new CFO and reiterating an ongoing strategic alternatives review.

ePlus reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $667.9M, up 9.7% YoY, with product sales up 12.8% to $547.1M and record gross billings of $1.07B. Gross profit rose 11.2% to $180.3M, gross margin expanded 40 bps to 27%, operating income grew 15.8% to $56.5M, and non-GAAP EPS rose 19% to $1.82. Management raised FY2027 guidance to upper single-digit growth in net sales and gross profit, with adjusted EBITDA up low double digits. Open orders rose nearly $750M YoY to about $1.8B, driven by AI, data center, and cloud demand, while professional services revenue declined 11.3% on retail project delays.

Tapestry reported Q1 FY2027 revenue up 12% pro forma to $1.9 billion, operating margin up 230 bps to over 23%, and EPS up 32% to $1.82, beating guidance by about $0.27. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.5-8.6 billion (6-7% constant-currency growth), operating margin above 24%, and EPS to $8.25-$8.35 from a prior $7.80-$7.90, with increased shareholder returns of about $2 billion including $1.7 billion in buybacks. Coach grew 16% constant currency with broad regional strength (North America +7%, Greater China +41%, Europe +27%), while Kate Spade declined 10%, in line with guidance, with gross margin up 190 bps. Gross margin expanded 220 bps to 78.7%, including a 70-bp tariff benefit, and Q2 revenue is guided up 5-6% constant currency with EPS of about $3.05.

GHM reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $69.8M, up 6% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $10.3M (14.8% margin, up 64%) and adjusted EPS of $0.52 (up 68%). Gross margin expanded 650 bps to 28.2%, though this was partly due to lower material receipts versus an unusually high prior-year quarter; the company reaffirmed FY2027 revenue guidance of $285-295M and adjusted EBITDA of $35-40M, while raising its gross margin outlook by ~50 bps. Backlog hit a record $561M (up 12% YoY, seventh straight record), orders were $73.7M (1.1x book-to-bill), and space revenue grew 59% while energy and process fell 17%. The key change versus prior periods is the sharp margin improvement and the FlackTek contribution (revenue $9.5M), offset by softness in large capital projects.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 66.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.97, $0.04 above the midpoint of guidance. However, roughly $53 million of the quarter was one-time (patent licensing, a distribution pricing effect, and a customer contract), so the underlying product growth was more modest. December-quarter guidance calls for revenue of down 3% to up 1% (midpoint -1%), non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.87-$0.95, a step down sequentially, which management frames as roughly 5%-7% above normal seasonality after stripping the one-offs. Bookings were strong and book-to-bill remained above one, backlog built, and management cited supply constraints and stretched lead times of six to 32 weeks limiting shipments of high-margin products.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.97 beating the guidance midpoint by $0.04; non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5% and operating margin 39.5%. About $53 million of infrequent, 100%-margin items (patent licensing, distribution price-protection catch-up, a $10 million customer contract) boosted the quarter and do not repeat. December-quarter guidance is down 3% to up 1% sequentially (midpoint -1%), with non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65% and EPS of $0.87-$0.95; management frames this as 5%-7% above normal seasonality but below what it expected a quarter ago. Management cited supply constraints at foundries, OSATs and internal fabs, with lead times stretching to six to 32 weeks and unsupported high-margin backlog pushed to later quarters; bookings were strong and book-to-bill well above one.

National Grid reported H1 FY2027 underlying operating profit of GBP 2.6bn (+13% YoY) and underlying EPS of GBP 0.365 (+22%), with capital investment up 32% to a record GBP 6.7bn. Full-year capital investment guidance was upgraded to GBP 13.5bn and EPS growth guidance nudged up to 15%-16% from a prior 13%-15%, though operating cash flow growth guidance was cut to 15% from 20% on higher capex and interest. The interim dividend rose 3.8% to GBP 0.1697 per share and the five-year 8%-10% EPS CAGR and GBP 70bn capex framework were reiterated, with 80% of the programme now under supply-chain mechanisms and net debt up GBP 4.5bn to GBP 48.6bn.

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations rose 15% YoY to $192.4 million, with Water Solutions adjusted EBITDA up 17% to $178.3 million (93% of the total) on record produced water disposal of 3.45 million barrels per day, up 23% YoY. Management raised FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $10 million to $735-$745 million (second raise this fiscal year) and lifted FY2027 growth capex to roughly $250-$270 million from about $200 million. Water Solutions opex fell to $0.20 per barrel from $0.22, while Crude Oil Logistics adjusted EBITDA declined to $11.9 million from $16.6 million on Grand Mesa volumes of 64,000 bpd versus 72,000 bpd. Leverage is expected to reach about four times by fiscal year-end, with the credit agreement repriced 50 bps lower and the ABL accordion raised $50 million to $475 million.

Q2 constant-currency revenue rose 10%, above the prior mid-single-digit outlook, with Asia +28% (China +35%), North America +6%, and Europe +3%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 220 bps to 70.2% and operating margin 140 bps to 15.5%, with AUR +9%. FY2027 guidance was raised: revenue growth to ~6%-7% from 5%-6%, gross margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 50-70 bps, and operating margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 60-80 bps. Europe's outlook was trimmed to low single digits from low-to-mid single digits on weaker traffic and consumer confidence, and the company repurchased ~$250 million in shares in the quarter, completing FY2027 buyback plans.

Peloton reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $559 million, up 2% YoY and $4 million above the midpoint of guidance, its third consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. Gross margin was 61.3% (up 975 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was $168 million, both well above guidance, though roughly $25 million of the beat came from tariff favorability and lower recall costs; ex-those items adjusted EBITDA was $143 million, $3 million above the midpoint. Ending paid connected fitness subscriptions of 2.475 million hit the high end of guidance with 1.7% net churn. Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.3-2.4 billion (down ~4% at midpoint), ~54% gross margin, $475-525 million adjusted EBITDA and at least $350 million free cash flow were all unchanged from last quarter.

Sony reported record Q2 FY2026 results with sales up 10% YoY to JPY 3,429.4 billion and operating income up 45% to JPY 622.3 billion, with net income up 44% to JPY 449.6 billion. Full-year guidance was raised across all three metrics: sales +4% to JPY 13 trillion, operating income +9% to JPY 1,870 billion, and net income +10% to JPY 1,330 billion. Segment guidance was lifted for G&NS (OI +6% to JPY 700 billion), Music (+6% to JPY 445 billion), Pictures (+33% to JPY 200 billion), and I&SS (+7% to JPY 450 billion), while ET&S was unchanged. Offsets include a JPY 16 billion earthquake loss at Kumamoto, a JPY 30 billion Sony Honda Mobility loss, a ~20% YoY smartphone market decline, and a delayed God of War Laufey release.

Universal reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $622 million, down 18% YoY, operating income of $43 million versus $68 million, and net income of $13 million versus $34 million. Tobacco segment revenue fell 19% to $534 million and operating income fell to $44 million from $65 million on delayed shipment timing; Ingredients revenue fell 8% to $88 million and swung to a $2 million operating loss. Management maintained that full-year expectations are unchanged, with shipments and results heavily weighted to the second half, and reported uncommitted flue-cured and burley stocks down 45 million kilos to 134 million kilos (19% of inventory, within target range). Net debt rose $82 million YoY to $1.15 billion, with management citing plans to delever as working capital moderates.

Revenue rose 3% to $1.2 billion with DAT up 20% and Communication Services down 3%; net loss widened $68 million to $129 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to $370 million. Full-year EBITDA guidance was cut to roughly flat versus prior year, while free cash flow guidance improved to over $225 million and CapEx was trimmed to $850-900 million. Management disclosed that recent airline announcements will ultimately affect 15%-20% of aviation revenue and guided FY2028 aviation revenue below FY2027, offsetting an awards pipeline that includes about $2 billion of DAT awards planned for FY2027 versus $1.6 billion last year.

Merger-announcement call that also covered both companies' Q3 results. Array reported Q3 revenue of $330 million (including one month of AWM; $321 million excluding), adjusted gross margin of 22.8% including a 330 bps charge for a 45X rebate reserve, and adjusted EBITDA of $32 million (10% margin), with a record $2.6 billion order book up 42% YoY and book-to-bill of 1.6x. Shoals reported record revenue of $195.3 million, up 44% YoY, gross margin of 31.9% (up 160 bps QoQ), adjusted EBITDA of about $40 million (20.4% margin), and $186 million of new orders, with results above its guided range. The deal is stock-for-stock (1.6931 Array shares per Shoals share, Shoals holders owning about 65%), targets $100 million of annual synergies by year three, includes $161.3 million of preferred redemption within 90 days, and carries a preliminary 2027 outlook of $2.2-2.4 billion revenue and $410-480 million adjusted EBITDA against a $3.4 billion backlog.

H1 FY2027 operating income was JPY 2.2 trillion on sales of JPY 26.96 trillion, with net income of JPY 2.24 trillion; OI rose year-on-year as cost reduction, price revisions, value-chain profits and tariff mitigation offset Middle East disruption and material costs. Toyota revised full-year operating income guidance up JPY 500 billion to JPY 3.9 trillion, with revenue forecast at JPY 53.5 trillion on FX assumptions of JPY 157/USD and EUR 182. Consolidated vehicle sales fell 25,000 units YoY (but rose 26,000 ex-Hino), while Toyota/Lexus unit sales fell to 96% of the prior year on weak China demand and the Middle East, and the electrified ratio reached 55.6%. Shareholder returns were expanded: interim dividend of JPY 50 (up JPY 5), FY dividend of JPY 100, buyback authorization raised JPY 300 billion to JPY 1.3 trillion, and an additional 1 billion treasury shares cancelled.

Q3 2026 RevPAR rose 8.3% (above expectations) to an all-time-high $161, with GOP margin of 44.7% (+110 bps) and hotel EBITDA margin of 38.7% (+190 bps); hotel EBITDA was $35 million, adjusted EBITDA $31.9 million, and adjusted FFO $0.46 per share, up 31% YoY. Management raised full-year adjusted FFO per share guidance roughly 28% from an original $1.09 midpoint to $1.38-$1.40, with FY RevPAR growth of 4%-4.5% and adjusted EBITDA of $104.2-$105.3 million. Silicon Valley RevPAR surged 23%, portfolio occupancy hit 83% (highest since 2019), and October RevPAR rose 7.9%, though management guided Q4 RevPAR growth to a more conservative 3.5%-4%. Leverage was 29.3% with approximately $25 million of expected 2026 free cash flow after dividends and capex.

Hyperliquid Strategies reported Q1 FY2027 results dominated by treasury movements: net income of ~$621 million after a ~$172 million tax provision, driven by ~$803 million of unrealized HYPE gains as the token rose from $65.04 to $90.99. NAV rose ~82% to $3.4 billion, cash increased to ~$255 million with zero debt, and the company raised ~$911 million net, deploying $785 million into 9.1 million HYPE at an average $86.44 and $17 million into buybacks at $6.36. The company announced it is applying to form its own FCM as a neutral bridge for U.S. Hyperliquid customers, with a timeline of roughly three to six months and single-digit-million-dollar one-time cost; no formal financial guidance was provided and results are non-operating, driven by token price.

Paylocity reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $451.7 million, up 11% YoY, with recurring and other revenue of $424.5 million up 12%, coming in $7.2 million above the top end of revenue guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $159.5 million at a 35.3% margin, $3.5 million above the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2027 total revenue guidance by $30 million at the midpoint to $1.910-$1.925 billion and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $711.5-$721.5 million, passing through more than the Q1 beat; the raise reflects stable demand, strong retention, and the September 25 bp rate hike. GAAP gross margin was pressured year-over-year on staffing timing ahead of year-end, which management characterized as timing rather than structural.

Total revenue was $108.2 million in Q3 2026, with net product revenue up 2% sequentially as the China commercial business stabilized; the text gives no YoY growth figure and no EPS. Management reiterated that China remains profitable and expects a return to year-over-year product revenue growth only in 2027, with R&D and SG&A roughly flat versus the prior year. The cash position was $659.7 million at September 30, 2026, plus about $250 million raised in October equity at no discount. Forward narrative centered on zoci (81.8% confirmed ORR in first-line SCLC, 6-month PFS 81.9%, grade 3+ zoci-related AEs 9.1%) and a potential U.S. BLA in 2027 with launch as early as 2028.

IBEX reported record Q1 FY2027 results with revenue of $175.2 million (up 16% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $25.2 million (up 29% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for revenue to $720M-$735M and adjusted EBITDA to $96M-$99M, citing strong momentum from new logos and the Sierra partnership. The company maintained a robust outlook with double-digit organic growth expected to continue.

Zoetis reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.4 billion, down 1% on both reported and organic operational bases, with a 1% price decline and flat volume, adjusted EPS up 1% to $1.75 on a lower share count, and adjusted net income down 7% organically. Companion animal fell 5% to $1.6 billion, led by a 16% drop in key dermatology to $396 million (US down 13%), with US segment revenue down 6% to $1.2 billion while international grew 4% to $1.1 billion. Livestock rose 7% to $797 million and diagnostics rose 13% to $122 million. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $9.22-9.32 billion (organic decline of 2% to 1%), while adjusted net income was raised to $2.6-2.64 billion and adjusted EPS to $6.25-6.35; for 2027 management said it will not assume macro improvement or easing competition and expects limited launch contribution.

Air Products reported FY2026 adjusted EPS of $13.45, up 12%, on 8% sales growth, with operating margin up 70 bps to 24.4% and ROC up 100 bps to 11.9%; Q4 EPS rose 6%. FY2027 EPS guidance of $14.15-$14.50 implies 5-8% growth, including a ~2% non-operating headwind from higher interest expense and a 19% tax rate, flat equity affiliate income, and no buybacks assumed. The industrial gas backlog rose to $3.3 billion from ~$3 billion, with over $2 billion in electronics project wins in the last 12 months, while FY2027 CapEx is targeted at $3-3.5 billion and management expects positive net cash flow. Full-year results came in above original FY2026 guidance, but the FY2027 EPS growth guide decelerates versus the 12% delivered in FY2026.

Kura Sushi reported Q4 FY2026 total sales of $88.9 million versus $79.4 million a year ago, but comparable sales fell 5.7% on an 11.5% traffic decline, partially offset by 5.8% price/mix. The quarter swung to a net loss of $0.3 million (-$0.02 per share) from net income of $2.3 million ($0.18), with adjusted net income of $0.9 million ($0.08) versus $2.5 million ($0.20), and restaurant-level operating margin contracted to 19.1% from 19.8%. FY2027 guidance calls for total sales of $376-381 million, 17 new units, G&A of ~11.5% of sales, and restaurant-level margin of ~19%, with management guiding to flat-to-slightly-positive comps at the high end and negative comps at the low end. Management also said it will take no pricing to offset the 3.5% that rolled off in November, and Q1 comps to date are -3.1%.

Q1 FY2027 core revenue was $316.4M, up 14% YoY, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 39% (up 900 bps sequentially) and non-GAAP net income of $119.1M, up 70% YoY. Management called the quarter a beat, with TPV exceeding expectations by ~250 bps, AP/AR take rate of 16.2 bps, core ARPU up 4.1% YoY, and GAAP net income of $60M. FY2027 guidance reiterates core revenue of $1.28B-$1.31B (11%-14% growth) and ~33% non-GAAP operating margin, while GAAP profit guidance was raised to more than $180M and non-GAAP EPS guidance implies ~47% YoY growth. Management flagged Q2 as a growth trough (core revenue growth of 10%-13%) tied to a tough prior-year compare and continued restructuring adjustments, with improvement expected in the back half.

Organic net sales rose 0.6% excluding EABL (1.4% including), with volume -0.1% and price/mix +0.7%; reported net sales were up 1.2% to $4.9 billion. North America organic sales fell 3.6% (U.S. -3.7%) on weakness in Don Julio, Casamigos and Crown Royal, partly offset by Johnnie Walker and double-digit Guinness and Smirnoff Ice. Asia-Pac grew 4.1%, LAC 4.8%, India 3.4% and EMEA 2.4%. FY2027 guidance was reiterated unchanged: broadly flat organic net sales, low-to-mid-single-digit organic operating profit growth, and free cash flow of around $2 billion.

Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue fell 11.1% to $171.4 million from $192.7 million on a continuing-operations basis, with E-Commerce down 12.3%, wholesale and other down 10.7%, and BloomNet down 3.6%; a Hebron, Ohio fire cost roughly 1% of revenue. Gross margin contracted 120 bps to 34.1% on lower volume, fuel surcharges, and promotional testing, and Adjusted EBITDA loss was essentially flat year-over-year at $31.9 million versus $31.7 million. Net Order Demand on primary websites improved to an 8% decline from 12.6% a year ago, while other websites fell 36%; management issued FY2027 guidance of revenue down 2%-5% and Adjusted EBITDA of $10-15 million, reflecting the completed PersonalizationMall and Things Remembered divestitures. The two-site sale closed at roughly $45 million, with $22 million applied to the term loan lowering it to $111.3 million, and a Jacksonville facility sale for about $10 million is pending.

IRSA reported a net loss of ARS 6.3 billion for Q1 FY2027, driven by fair value adjustments on investment properties due to inflation outpacing currency devaluation in Argentina. Despite the headline loss, rental EBITDA increased 20% in dollar terms and reached a record $205 million over the last 12 months. Management raised the dividend yield to 11% (ARS 211 billion) and guided CapEx for the full year at approximately $150 million.

Phibro reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $386.8 million, up 6% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 4% to $64.3 million and net income up 11% to $29.5 million. Growth came from Mineral Nutrition (+17%) and Performance Products (+16%), while Animal Health grew 3% and its adjusted EBITDA fell 1% on higher SG&A and a $5.2 million virginiamycin decline in Brazil. Fiscal 2027 guidance was maintained at $1.55-1.6 billion net sales, $258-268 million adjusted EBITDA, and $3.41-3.59 adjusted EPS, with management attributing the hold to expenses shifting from Q1 into Q2 rather than a raised outlook. Management described poultry producer margin pressure and inventory trimming as temporary but flagged soft near-term protein producer profitability; the CFO also cited excess inventory as a priority to reduce.

BrasilAgro reported Q1 FY2027 net income of BRL 81 million and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 95 million, driven by a BRL 50 million gain from farm sales and BRL 37 million in financial effects from soy price rallies. Management highlighted that operational results fell short of the BRL 150 million target due to lower corn sales volume compared to the prior year and tight sugarcane margins caused by low ATR prices. The company reduced its net debt/EBITDA ratio to 1.05x following the farm sale but noted that high interest rates are currently hindering further expansion or purchases.

Lesaka reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of ZAR 1.58 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of ZAR 0.72, beating the top of guidance while meeting all three measures. Group Adjusted EBITDA was ZAR 220 million at the midpoint of guidance, though down 17% YoY due to exceptional items in merchant and higher group costs. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenue (ZAR 7-7.7 billion) and adjusted EPS (ZAR 7.50-8.50), noting that Bank Zero completion is expected by end of January 2027.

LSI reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $226 million, a 44% year-over-year increase driven by the Royston acquisition and strong C-store/grocery verticals, while lighting sales declined 6%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $22.2 million with improved margins across all brands, supported by cost synergies and pricing discipline. Management noted continued softness in QSR and lighting markets due to customer budget delays but highlighted a new 3,000-store QSR award and positive momentum from the NACS trade show.

Net sales increased 29.9% to $252.9 million driven by Saxdor and Cobalt growth, though this modestly missed the guided range due to a softer ski/wake category. Adjusted EBITDA rose 21.7% to $14.3 million at the low end of guidance, while legacy adjusted EBITDA declined as Malibu volumes fell. Management provided updated guidance for the transition period (July-Dec) with net sales expected between $489M-$501M and adjusted EBITDA between $27.3M-$29.3M.

Revenue increased 4% to $219.4 million and gross margins expanded 150 bps to 8.2%, driven by improved execution and overhead absorption. The company reported its third consecutive quarter of profitability with positive EPS of $0.22, while liquidity remains strong at $222 million. Management noted that award activity will pick up in the second half of the fiscal year, though current awards primarily solidify revenue for fiscal 2028.

OpenText reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $1.237B, within the expected outlook range, with Core revenue of $864M up 2.4% year over year (2.7% constant currency) and Core Cloud revenue of $339M up 11.2% (11.7% cc). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 35.8%, down 50 bps year over year but above the 32%-33% outlook range, and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.05, flat year over year. Q2 revenue guidance is $1.26B-$1.29B with adjusted EBITDA margin of 33%-34%, and full-year FY2027 outlook ranges were maintained on all metrics, with growth investments weighted to the second half. The quarter was in line with the company's own outlook, with Content Cloud growing 20.7% while ITOM and cyber declined double digits and $116M of products were reclassified from Core to non-Core.

Revenue returned to growth at $84.7 million, up 5.3% YoY, but gross margin fell to 34.9% from 37.4% on product mix and higher promotional, tariff and freight costs, and Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $8.1 million from $11 million. GAAP net income rose to $4.4 million ($0.24/diluted share) from $1.7 million ($0.08), helped by $1.9 million of prior-year debt extinguishment and current-quarter insurance recoveries. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $335-355 million revenue and $44-48 million Adjusted EBITDA, requiring a substantial Q4 that management ties to retailer holiday replenishment shifted out of Q3, new products and major releases including GTA VI. Retailers bought only to normal seasonal levels in Q3, pushing holiday load-in into Q4, while October watch-through and orders accelerated; inventory rose ~$23.2 million sequentially to $79.8 million and no shares were repurchased after ~$25 million in Q2.

Q3 FY2026 net income fell to $9 million ($0.18/diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA to $165 million from $126 million and $324 million in Q2, with the prior quarter boosted by a $125 million Leer South insurance settlement; stripping that out, adjusted EBITDA was $33 million lower sequentially. Cash costs rose across segments (PRB to $13.75-$14.00, High CV Thermal to $40-$41, met tightened to $88-$90), driven by persistent input inflation (diesel, tungsten bits) and geology-related variability at multiple longwalls. Free cash flow was $80 million and the company returned $90 million (112% of FCF) to shareholders, with total liquidity over $1 billion. Management said operations are back on track, guiding to stronger Q4 ASPs ($62-$63 High CV) and a large contracted book (29.4 million tons through 2031), but formal EBITDA/EPS guidance was not provided.

Starling Oncology reported record Q3 revenue of $169.8 million, up 24.3% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $3.4 million (versus $0.2 million in Q2 and a $3.5 million loss a year ago) that exceeded the top end of the guided Q3 range. Specialty pharmacy revenue rose 44% to $109.3 million at a 24.2% gross margin, which management attributed partly to rebates and favorable drug price moves it does not expect to recur, guiding pharmacy margins to normalize to the high teens. Total gross margin expanded roughly 420 bps to 18.1%, and the MLR improved to 81% from 85.5% in Q2. However, the capitated revenue target for 2027 was cut to roughly $220 million from a prior $300 million after anchor Florida partners did not expand statewide, which analysts pressed on throughout; management reaffirmed 100% capitated revenue growth in 2027 versus 2026 and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $4 million-$6 million.

BCE reported Q3 revenue up 2.2% YoY to support adjusted EBITDA growth of 0.9%, with EBITDA margin down 60 bps to 45.1% partly on lower-margin product sales; adjusted EPS fell CAD 0.05 and free cash flow was CAD 854 million, down YoY on higher CapEx. Excluding Ziply, revenue grew 0.9% and adjusted EBITDA was stable. Management reconfirmed all 2026 financial guidance targets (including ~CAD 5 billion CapEx), and guided to wireless service revenue and ARPU growth by mid-2027 if pricing momentum continues. Key events: CAD 2.45 billion sale of 49.9% of TowerCo to La Caisse (implying ~CAD 4.91 billion valuation, closing Q1 2027), postpaid churn improved 7 bps to 1.06%, AI-powered solutions revenue up 41%, and Bell Media revenue up 9.7% with EBITDA up 8%.

GPN reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net revenue of $3.18 billion, up over 4% on a constant-currency basis excluding dispositions, with adjusted EPS of $3.58 (+10%) and adjusted operating margin of 42.5%, up 220 bps. All three segments grew: SMB normalized revenue +5% at a 60% contribution margin, Enterprise +8% at 79%, and Platforms +8% at 45%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (4-5% normalized revenue growth, ~150 bps margin expansion, EPS $13.60-$13.80), while the Worldpay run-rate expense synergy target was raised to $600 million-$650 million by end-2028. Management declined to discuss reported take-private speculation and deferred a 2027 outlook to the Q4 call.

GPGI reported Q3 pro forma adjusted net sales of $509.6 million, up ~5% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $146.3 million, up ~7%, and 28.7% margins, up ~60 bps, with ~$81 million in adjusted free cash flow. CompoSecure set records at $140.7 million sales (+16%) and $61.2 million EBITDA (+23%) with 43.5% margins, while Husky sales were flat at $368.9 million (+0.5%) and EBITDA fell 0.9% to $88.8 million on 24.1% margins. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is intact at the high end of the prior range (~$2.03-2.06 billion, +1%), but adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $520-550 million (-2% YoY at midpoint) and margins cut ~80 bps due primarily to ~$20 million of delayed Husky cost actions and unfavorable mix.

Q3 2026 revenue was $112.9 million with a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $67.1 million and AFFO of $48.3 million, or $0.22 per share. GNL raised the low end of full-year AFFO per share guidance to $0.83-$0.85 from $0.82 and lifted the low end of gross transaction volume guidance to $750-$800 million, while reaffirming net debt/Adjusted EBITDA of 6.5x-6.9x. Office exposure fell to 23% of straight-line rent from roughly 27% last quarter, and 6.6 million shares were repurchased for $58.5 million in the quarter. Leverage temporarily rose because Modiv closed mid-August, so debt reflects a full quarter while EBITDA includes only a partial quarter.

Globus Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $763.7 million, down 0.7% as reported and 0.5% constant currency, as base Globus sales grew 3% to $690 million but Nevro fell 25.7% to $73.7 million; non-GAAP EPS rose 4.4% to $1.23 and adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 69.5%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut to $3.09 billion from $3.18-$3.22 billion, while non-GAAP EPS guidance of $4.95-$5.05 was reiterated (24.4%-26.9% growth). Management attributed softness to delayed new product launches (SCRIPT, XLIF Prone), weaker competitive rep recruiting, and a slower-than-expected Nevro recovery, with benefits pushed into 2027. Record free cash flow of $225 million and an added $500 million buyback authorization offset some of the top-line weakness.

Avino reported Q3 2026 revenue of $33.4 million, gross margin of 44% (49% cash basis), net income of $6.1 million ($0.03/diluted share) and adjusted earnings of $14.3 million ($0.08/share), with operating cash flow of $12.7 million (up 52% YoY) and free cash flow of $6 million. Silver production rose 15% YoY to 303,000 ounces, though the company revised full-year production guidance down to 2.2-2.5 million silver-equivalent ounces and revised cash cost and AISC per ounce to midpoints of $23 and $31, respectively, with AISC per ton revised to $90. Margins were pressured by peso strength (7-10% stronger YoY) and La Preciosa development costs running over 30% above budget, while lower-grade development material was processed. Cash position was $138 million and working capital $142 million after an $8.75 million final royalty payment.

Genmab reported 22% YoY total revenue growth for the first nine months of 2026, with DARZALEX up 19%, EPKINLY sales up 47% to $491 million, TIVDAK up 9% to $131 million, and the remainder of the portfolio up 30%; adjusted operating profit grew 9%. Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at ~$4.325-4.525 billion revenue (19% growth at midpoint, now expected in the upper part of the range) and adjusted operating profit of $1.065-1.35 billion, with the company guiding operating profit above the midpoint. The key change was three positive phase III readouts announced in October — EPCORE DLBCL-2 (PFS HR 0.49), RAINFOL-02 for Rina-S (PFS HR 0.29 plus OS benefit), and LiGeR-HN1 for petosemtamab (OS HR 0.5 plus ORR) — with prior peak-sales estimates ($3B+ EPKINLY, $2B+ Rina-S, multi-billion petosemtamab, $1B peto in 2029) reaffirmed.

Q3 revenue rose 36% YoY to $361M from $265M, with oncology up 25% to $231M, screening up 180% to $68M on Shield volume of 83,000 tests (+246%), and biopharma/data up 8% to $59M. Non-GAAP gross margin was 67% vs 66%, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $37M from $46M, and Shield cost per test fell to $330 from $410, ahead of the $350 target. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.36-1.37B (38-40% growth) from 36-38%, with screening raised to $233-238M and oncology volume now expected up more than 50%. Free cash flow burn guidance widened to $205-220M from $195-205M on a $10-15M CMS claims timing shift for Guardant360 Liquid CDx.

Aspen reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $85.2 million, above the $65-80 million guidance range and up 17% year-over-year (71% quarter-over-quarter), with adjusted EBITDA of $19.8 million versus a $7-15 million guide. GAAP gross margin was 24% (7% in Q2), or 41% on an adjusted basis excluding $14.7 million of East Providence incident costs, and GAAP net loss narrowed to $10.4 million from $23.3 million. Q4 guidance was set at $60-75 million revenue and $5-13 million adjusted EBITDA, below Q3 on the absence of subsea project revenue, with the low end assuming GM production below the IHS forecast; European thermal barrier 2026 revenue is now expected near $30 million with a target of $50-60 million in 2027.

Net sales rose just 0.7% to $352.4 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 30.3% to $18.9 million (5.4% margin, down 230 bps), with adjusted EPS of negative $0.01 versus $0.47 a year ago. Management cut full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $140-$150 million from $160-$175 million, citing a 200 bp price-cost gap (~$7-8 million in Q3) and asphalt delivery shifts into 2027. Offsetting that, total backlog jumped 49.2% to $670.5 million, Infrastructure Solutions implied orders rose 43.4% YoY with a 149% book-to-bill, and Q4 EBITDA is guided to $48-$58 million versus $44.8 million a year ago.

Genius Sports reported Q3 FY2026 group revenue of $270 million versus guidance of $260 million and adjusted EBITDA of $87 million versus guidance of $85 million, a 32% margin up 12 points year-over-year from 20%. Betting revenue grew 33% and media revenue grew 126%, with gross margin expanding to 34% from 25% and $54 million of free cash flow at 61% conversion. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $1.015-1.035 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $287-297 million, with year-end cash of approximately $260 million and net leverage near two times by year-end 2026. The 2028 targets of 35% adjusted EBITDA margin and over 60% unlevered free cash flow conversion were reaffirmed, and management said the guide does not assume an NFL prediction-market deal.

Genpact reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.385 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year despite roughly two points of drag from work being transitioned away, with gross margin expanding ~160 bps to 36.9% and adjusted operating margin at 17.7%. Adjusted diluted EPS rose 10.3% to $1.07 and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.89. Advanced Technology Solutions accelerated to 30.3% growth ($405 million, 29% of revenue) from 24.1% in Q2, while Core Business Services was flat at $980 million. Full-year 2026 guidance is at least 7% revenue growth, ATS at least 25%, gross margin raised to 36.9% (~90 bps expansion) and adjusted EPS growth of at least 13%, with 2027 revenue growth expected similar even as the transition-away impact grows modestly.

Astrana reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.02 billion, up 7% YoY, and record adjusted EBITDA of $77.2 million, up 13% YoY and at the high end of the $72.5M-$77.5M guide, with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.71 and $105 million of YTD free cash flow. Full-year guidance ranges were narrowed while maintaining each midpoint ($3.9B-$4.0B revenue, $261M-$274M adjusted EBITDA, $107.5M-$130M FCF), and net leverage fell to 2.2x after $116 million of YTD debt repayment. The quarter was offset by continued Medicaid and exchange membership attrition (10%-15% Medicaid decline now expected in 2027) and a fourth quarter guided sharply lower on non-recurring MSSP and risk-adjustment sweeps. Management reiterated confidence in at least mid-teens medium-term adjusted EBITDA growth while withholding details on the September cyber incident.

FrontView reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted cash revenue up 4.4% to $17.1 million (5.6% excluding other income), with adjusted cash NOI of $17.4 million and an exiting run-rate of about $17.2 million, reflecting percentage rent and loan-repayment items. Full-year 2026 AFFO guidance was maintained at $1.32-$1.34 per share (~7% growth at midpoint, up from an initial $1.28), implying $0.33 in Q4. Occupancy was 99.4% with only two vacancies and no new watch-list additions; acquisitions totaled 16 properties for $50.6 million at a 7.56% cap rate, and leverage fell to 5.0x, or 4.5x pro forma including the final preferred draw. The quarter was largely in-line with steady guidance; the notable changes were higher cap rates on new acquisitions and the appointment of Pierre Revol as President alongside his CFO role.

Q3 FY2026 same-park revenue rose 1.4% to $1.17 billion and adjusted EBITDA grew 1.1% to $493.2 million, with margin essentially flat at 42% (down 13 bps) despite weather and smoke headwinds; reported net loss was $366 million (-$3.59/share) on a $688 million non-cash impairment. For Q4, management guided same-park adjusted EBITDA to roughly $140-150 million versus $166.9 million last year, citing October attendance down 9% (weather plus the fatal Georgia incident and related ride closures), but still expects full-year same-park EBITDA to grow. The prior-period picture included 11% YTD EBITDA growth, ~200 bps margin expansion, and $257 million of free cash flow, while the key change versus the prior outlook is the softer October-driven Q4 guidance.

JFrog reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $179.2M, up 31% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with cloud revenue of $101.5M up 60% YoY and 57% of total revenue. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 22.7% from 18.7%, free cash flow margin reached 37% versus 21%, RPO totaled $812M up 60% YoY, and trailing-four-quarter NRR rose to 124% from 118% YoY. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $680–682M (28% growth at midpoint), lifted baseline cloud growth to 52–54%, and set Q4 revenue guidance of $183–185M with non-GAAP EPS of $0.28–$0.30. A $76M multi-year SaaS agreement with a leading telecom, representing 167% growth in that customer's cloud consumption, anchored the quarter, while on-prem revenue grew only 6% YoY.

A10 reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $91.5 million, up 22.6% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 80%, operating margin of 27.8%, and diluted EPS of $0.31 versus $0.23 a year ago. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to approximately 16% from a prior 12%-14% and guided non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.08-$1.10, up 20%-22%, while setting a FY2029 target of $500 million revenue and $2 in EPS. Revenue excluding the largest customer grew at a double-digit rate, and EMEA and APJ grew double digits. Free cash flow was $57.5 million year to date, up 18%, alongside $27.4 million returned to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS was $0.54 versus $0.23 last year, but consolidated sales fell 10.1% to $338.4M and adjusted EBITDA was only ~$38M excluding $12M of IEEPA tariff refunds — the low end of the preliminary range set on October 16. Management said results were below expectations, driven by a spring supplier disruption and higher costs in Powered Vehicles, upfit operational challenges, softer bike sales, and Marucci weakness ahead of closing. Q4 sales guidance of $287-313M was maintained and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was narrowed to $143-148M ex-tariff refunds; 2027 guidance and CEO search details were deferred. Marucci was divested for $225M EV, cutting net leverage from 3.7x to ~2.4x.

Atlanticus reported Q3 FY2026 total operating revenue and other income of $776 million, up 60% YoY, with a $205 million contribution from Mercury. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.87, up 300%, including $1.87 of one-time gains from the CAR auto finance sale (~$20 million gain on $71.2 million consideration) and the $27.5 million Mercury IP sale; adjusted diluted EPS was $3 and adjusted ROE 30%. Managed receivables reached $7.1 billion, up 8% YoY and 3.4% sequentially, and the principal net charge-off ratio improved to 17.3% from 17.7% last quarter. Management cited record originations and profitability but gave no formal EPS or revenue guidance, and flagged that portfolio-wide CPAs will likely keep rising and delinquencies may increase marginally as the mix shifts to a broader consumer base.

HIFU revenue was $9.8 million, up 26% YoY, but management said revenue fell short of internal expectations because three anticipated U.S. capital system sales slipped on hospital committee timing. Gross margin expanded 482 bps to 51.4% on better standard cost and higher ASPs, while operating loss widened to $7.8 million from $6.7 million on higher opex; net loss narrowed to $4.5 million ($0.10/share) on a $2.6 million warrant fair-value gain. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $50-52 million (34-39% growth) from $50-54 million, with the three slipped systems now expected to revenue in Q4. U.S. procedure volumes grew 32% YoY versus 15% a year ago, and the install base reached 192 systems.

Q3 2026 revenue was flat at $183 million and Adjusted EBITDA flat at $50 million (27.3% margin), with management noting that excluding the U.S. tower portfolio sale, communication services revenue would have grown 1% and Adjusted EBITDA 6%. GAAP net income jumped to ~$19 million, or $1.09 per diluted share, from $4 million/$0.18, aided by higher operating income, lower interest expense, and a discrete non-recurring tax benefit. Operating income rose 32% to $13 million, international revenue grew 2% to $97 million with Adjusted EBITDA up 9% and margin up 240 bps to 37.4%, while domestic revenue fell 2% to $86 million. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was updated to the high end of or modestly above the prior $183-$193 million range, with capex net of reimbursables unchanged at $105-$115 million.

Q3 revenue of $131.1 million grew 19% reported (20% constant currency), above the high end of guidance, with SaaS revenue up 26% to $105.5 million (80% of total). Total ARR reached $495.1 million, up 27% reported and 25% FX-adjusted — the second straight quarter of acceleration — on record net new ARR of $30 million (+34% YoY). Full-year ARR guidance was raised $1 million at the midpoint to $524.8-$528.8 million, and revenue guidance includes the $1.9 million Q3 beat, but the full-year non-GAAP operating margin outlook reflects an investment year with Q4 margin guided to ~18%, below the prior year. Gross margin contracted to 72.8% from 75.1% on lower services margins, while GAAP operating margin expanded 130+ bps to 8.7% and GRR hit the 90% target for the first time.

Reported EPS of $1.06 was flat to last year, but adjusted EPS (excluding retirement-plan investment swings) rose $0.05 to $1.06 from $1.01, driven by 2026 CPUC-approved rate increases across the regulated utilities. Consolidated revenue rose $9.8 million, split $7.6M water and $1.6M electric, while total operating expenses rose $4.2 million on depreciation, ASUS construction, and other opex. ASUS earned $0.17 for the quarter (down $0.02) and is guided to $0.63-$0.67 per share for the year and $0.67-$0.71 for 2027. The dividend was raised 8.2% in the quarter, and the 2028-2030 Golden State water rate case seeking ~$1 billion of capital was filed in July.

Net sales rose 3% with core collectibles up 5% and Europe up 12%; gross margin reached 45%, a five-point improvement YoY, and adjusted EBITDA was $32 million (12% margin). Full-year guidance was reiterated at sales flat to up 3% and adjusted EBITDA of $100-110 million. Offsetting this, Q3 reported POS units fell 4% globally, down 10% in the U.S. and down 13% in D2C, while EMEA POS grew 16%; year-to-date POS remained up 3%. Net debt fell to $155 million from just over $200 million a year earlier.

Q3 revenue of $323M came in above the high end of guidance, up 13% YoY, with subscription revenue +16%, CCaaS +8%, and AI revenue accelerating to 91% growth (~$45M, 17% of subscription vs 10% a year ago). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.82 vs $0.78, adjusted gross margin slipped to 62% from 63%, and LTM subscription dollar-based retention rose to 109% from 107%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to a $1.272B midpoint (up $6M), but FY EPS guidance was cut $0.07 to $3.19 on timing of org changes and a higher share count. The company announced a $325M cash acquisition of Level AI (~$20M ARR, +50% YoY, ~11x forward ARR), expected to dilute 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin by ~1 point.

Q3 revenue was $909M, up 28% YoY, with platform solutions up 106% to $125M, software and services up 43% to $437M (ARR $1.8B, +40%), and adjusted EBITDA up 33% to $236M (25.9% margin). However, connected devices grew only 16% to $472M and TASER declined modestly to $233M on lower TASER 7 sales. Guidance was effectively reset lower: Q4 revenue is guided to $990M-$1.01B and no longer assumes ~$100M of two federal Dedrone deployments, with three programs totaling ~$130M (~500bps of growth) slipping from the second half. Full-year free cash flow guidance was cut to $350M-$400M from $450M on an intentional inventory build of over $100M in Q3, and management announced a $1.2B Skydio investment taking ownership to 37%.

BBUC reported Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $594M vs $575M a year earlier and Adjusted EFO of $337M vs $284M, with $44M of net gains mostly from the partial La Trobe sale. Industrial same-store EBITDA rose ~8% and business services ~3%, while infrastructure services fell to $76M from $104M on the Altera FPSO sale, softer Modulaire demand and Scientific Games contract costs. Management gave no formal updated guidance but framed a ~$2.5B annual EBITDA run-rate falling to ~$2.4B after ~$100M from asset sales, expected to recover toward $2.5B as acquisitions ramp; $1.4B of capital recycling was completed year to date against a $2B target.

Q3 revenue was EUR 164.9 million, broadly flat year-on-year (163.9 million), with D&PD down 2.3% to 120.1 million and JEB up 9.4% to 44.8 million; adjusted EBITDA improved to -1.6 million from -15 million. Nine-month revenue fell 13.1% to 465 million and adjusted EBITDA swung to -44.3 million from -16.9 million due to a weak first half and the prior-year Sandoz license. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (revenue 570-610 million, adjusted EBITDA -105 to -70 million), with management expecting both toward the upper end; Q3 included about 30 million of strategic milestones that will not repeat in Q4. Vertex selected JEB for commercial povetacicept manufacturing, and Horizon cost savings are ahead of plan (>20% delivered).

Total revenue increased 29% year-over-year to $91.6 million, driven by a whole engine sale of $9.3 million and growth in leasing and MRO segments. However, adjusted EBITDA declined to $8.6 million (9.3% margin) from $9.5 million last year due to lower TechOps gross margins and a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $13.4 million resulting in a net loss of $15 million. Management expects significantly stronger fourth quarter results as committed flight equipment sales close, but provided no specific financial guidance for the quarter.

Arrow reported record Q3 FY2026 results with total revenue of $10.7 billion (up 39% YoY) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $6.22 (up 158% YoY). Operating margin expanded 130 bps to 4.1%, driven by volume growth, price inflation in memory components, and operational leverage. The company significantly exceeded its guidance range for both revenue and EPS.

Gulfport reported Q3 2026 results where production, capital, and operating costs all landed in line with guidance, with liquids at 13% of total production on the strength of wet gas Utica TILs and EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow both up meaningfully from Q2. Management reaffirmed it remains on track to execute within original 2026 guidance ranges and expects adjusted free cash flow to grow more than 15% over 2025 at $3 gas. The quarter's key strategic changes are a move to a continuous two-rig program in Appalachia with an electric frac fleet contracted from mid-2027, a target to cut D&C cost per foot by more than 20% by 2028, a reduction in SCOOP activity in 2027, and a 33% increase in the buyback authorization to $2 billion. Formal 2027 guidance was deferred to the Q4 call in February.

ANI Pharmaceuticals reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $290.8 million (up 28% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $83.3 million (up 40% YoY), driven by strong generics growth of 11% and rare disease revenue growth of 36%. However, Cortrophin Gel net revenues came in lighter than expected due to specialty pharmacy network capacity bottlenecks from a successful gout expansion, leading management to revise its 2026 Cortrophin Gel guidance down to $480-$500 million from the prior $520-$540 million range. The company also announced an offer to acquire Egetis Therapeutics for approximately $560 million in equity consideration to gain access to EMCITATE, a first-in-class therapy for MCT8 deficiency.

Alarm.com reported Q3 FY2026 SaaS and license revenue of $191.2 million (up 9% YoY) and total revenue of $279.4 million, exceeding the midpoint of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $66.2 million, with non-GAAP EPS increasing 26.8% to $0.90. Management raised full-year 2026 SaaS revenue guidance by approximately $2 million at the midpoint and total revenue guidance by roughly $10 million.

AMH reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $82.3 million ($0.23 diluted EPS) and core FFO growth of 7.4% YoY. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for same-home core NOI growth to a midpoint of 2.8% and core FFO per share to $1.97, citing solid execution, favorable property tax updates, and healthy leasing spreads. The company deployed $75 million in share repurchases during the quarter.

Amylyx reported positive top-line results from the Phase III LUCIDITY trial for avexitide in post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), demonstrating a 55% reduction in hypoglycemic events compared to placebo. The company completed an oversubscribed equity offering raising $545 million, bringing total cash and equivalents to $768 million at quarter-end. Management remains on track to submit the NDA by year-end with a potential launch anticipated in 2027.

IMAX reported record Q3 revenue of $175M (up 64% YoY), record adjusted EBITDA of $121M at a 69% margin (up ~2,040 bps YoY), and adjusted EPS of $2.21 (up $1.74 YoY), with global box office of $712M nearly double the prior record. Company now expects to significantly exceed its $1.4B 2026 full-year box office guidance and to deliver ~50% adjusted EBITDA margin versus prior mid-40s guidance, while maintaining install guidance of 160-175 systems despite a slower 32 installs in the quarter. Signings reached 105 year-to-date with a pipeline of ~150 potential new and upgraded locations, though 2027 box office guidance was deferred to early next year.

Consolidated revenue of $717 million beat the upper end of guidance by nearly 10%, driven by a $51 million favorable reserve adjustment for prior labor disruption events and strong underlying growth in Nurse and Allied. However, core EBITDA performance was at the low end of the range due to a negative actuarial adjustment for workers' compensation and mix impacts. Management provided Q4 guidance with revenue down 13%-15% year-over-year excluding labor disruption, citing headwinds from international nurse visa delays.

Amphastar reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $207.6 million, an 8% year-over-year increase driven by record sales of BAQSIMI ($58.8M) and Primatene MIST ($31.5M), alongside new launches like ipratropium bromide. Gross margins contracted to 48% from 51% due to lower net pricing on key products and remediation expenses at the IMS facility, though EPS beat expectations with adjusted earnings of $1.14 per share. Management provided Q4 guidance for high single-digit sales growth but noted ongoing headwinds from duplicate discounts and manufacturing remediation.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $556M, up 5% organic/4% reported, with adjusted gross margin of 42% (up ~1pt sequentially from 41%), adjusted EBITDA of $114M (20.5% margin, +8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.44 vs $2.03 last year (+20%). Infusion Systems grew 11% to a record and Consumables grew 5% to a record, while Vital Care fell 10% organic/12% reported on a logistics consolidation that management said was largely a mix issue with no net revenue impact. Full-year guidance now points to the higher end of the prior $415-435M EBITDA and $8.60-9.00 EPS ranges (no change to the ranges themselves), CapEx guidance was cut to $75M from $85M, and net leverage was brought to ~2x after $80M of debt paydown.

ICF reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $470.5 million, up 1.1% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS up 18.6% to $1.98 and GAAP EPS up 37.5% to $1.76. However, full-year revenue guidance was cut to approximately $1.87 billion, roughly flat versus FY2025, as commercial energy add-on work was paused due to utility affordability pressure, costing about $15 million in Q3 and a similar amount expected in Q4. The non-GAAP EPS midpoint of $7.10 and operating cash flow guidance of $135-150 million were maintained, aided by gross margin expansion of 50 bps to 38.1%, a lower 15% tax rate, and reduced interest expense. Management cited Q4 commercial energy growth of mid-to-high single digits and a second-half exit rate near 4%, but deferred 2027 guidance pending federal budget clarity and resolution of the utility add-on pause.

Reported revenue fell 8.6% to $84.6M on Powering Honest Growth exits and weaker diapers, but organic revenue rose 9.2% to $79.3M; underlying adjusted gross margin hit a record 48.9% (up ~1,160 bps) and underlying adjusted EBITDA was $6.3M at a 7.9% margin, up 300 bps. Net income of $91.3M was almost entirely an $89.4M deferred-tax valuation-allowance release; adjusted net income was $3.1M. FY2026 guidance was raised on all lines: revenue $322-325M (from $319-325M), organic growth 6-7% (from 5-7%), adjusted gross margin 45.5-46.5% (from mid-40s), and adjusted EBITDA $25-26M (from $23-25M). The key negative versus prior periods: total consumption growth moderated to 1% and diaper consumption fell 27%, partly attributed to the Prime Day timing shift.

Q3 FY2026 orders were $191 million (up 12% YoY, down 7% QoQ), revenue $171 million (flat QoQ), adjusted EBITDA $38 million (down 3% YoY at a 22.3% margin), and free cash flow was negative $12 million. Product revenue collapsed 69% YoY to $17 million on pushed-out equipment orders, and full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised down to $135-$140 million with Q4 roughly flat to slightly below Q3. Management framed the weakness as timing (rig reactivation delays, Middle East disruption, equipment order slippage) and guided to 10-25% YoY growth in key floater activity for 2027, with ~85% of base-case 2027 activity supported by backlog or options. Lower Middle East activity is estimated to cut 2026 order intake by $50-$60 million, partly offset by 16% YoY service order growth and an expanding North American land business.

Q3 revenue was $246.8M, up 8.5% sequentially, with gross margin of 34.2% (in line with ~34% guidance, up from 33.1%) and EPS of $0.107, above the $0.080-$0.100 guidance range on lower opex. Q4 guidance calls for revenue down 22%-26% sequentially and EPS of $0.045-$0.065, excluding an expected $19-20M after-tax divestiture gain, driven by an abrupt correction in automotive driver IC orders from Chinese-export-exposed panel makers. Management still expects full-year 2026 automotive IC revenue to grow about 10% and guided to double-digit 2027 revenue growth (excluding CPO), while flagging foundry/backend price increases as a gross margin challenge it expects to largely offset.

Aemetis reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $88.2 million, a 49% year-over-year increase driven by California ethanol and dairy renewable natural gas segments, alongside net income of $5.2 million ($0.07 per share) and Adjusted EBITDA of $24.8 million. Management highlighted significant financial inflection points including the approval of seven new Low Carbon Fuel Standard pathways averaging a negative 380 carbon intensity score and a substantial true-up of Section 45Z production tax credits following regulatory model updates. The company expects the mechanical vapor recompression system to be completed by early 2027, with financial benefits materializing in the second half of next year.

Health Catalyst reported Q3 revenue of $56.3 million versus a $55-56 million guide and adjusted EBITDA of $779,000 versus a $0-500,000 range, both above the high end. However, adjusted gross margin fell sharply to 44.3% from 52.6% a year ago, with professional services margin at just 1.7%, and Q4 is guided to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.3-1.8 million as Vitalware's full removal and higher medical claims hit results. Full-year revenue ($246-249M) and EBITDA ($18-18.5M) guidance was reaffirmed, not raised, and bookings are now expected to exceed the high end of the $22-26M target. New CEO Simeon Kohl flagged elevated churn as the top priority, offsetting the modest top-line beat.

Reported revenue fell 1.7% YoY to $371M from $377M, but management said sales would have risen high single digits absent IRA-related drug price reductions. Gross profit rose 14% to $85.2M with margin up sequentially to 23%, Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $33.9M (9.1% margin), and net income doubled to $19M from $9.6M. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $1.44-1.46B from $1.43-1.45B and Adjusted EBITDA to $136-138M from $129-131M. Prescription volumes rose 10% and residents served grew high single digits to ~218,000.

rows.company_name: Hannon Armstrong Sustainable Infrastructure Capital, Inc.
rows.key_quote: HASI reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.82, helped by a fair value gain on the SunStrong Management affiliate; year-to-date adjusted EPS reached $2.34 (up 15%) and adjusted ROE rose to 15.6% from 13.4%. Adjusted recurring net investment income grew 23% YoY to $330 million and managed assets rose 26% to $19 billion, with $2.8 billion of transactions closed YTD at yields above 11%. Management reiterated 2028 guidance of $3.55-$3.65 adjusted EPS and at least 17% ROE, and expects 2026 adjusted EPS in line with the 10% long-term growth target, while taking a $21 million RNG impairment charge (offsetting part of the $35 million SunStrong gain) that moved about 1% of the portfolio to category three.

Artivion reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $123.8 million, up 9% constant currency, while adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $22.5 million due to costs associated with the Endospan acquisition and manufacturing investments. Management narrowed full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted constant currency growth to 8%-10% (previously higher) and adjusted EBITDA to $93-$98 million, citing a one-time AMDS milestone payment and expected Q4 timing reversals in preservation services. The company highlighted strong implant adoption for AMDS despite administrative hurdles with starter sets and exited the quarter with a robust supply position for On-X ahead of the NEXUS launch.

APA reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $698 million ($2.00 diluted EPS) and adjusted net income of $676 million ($1.94 diluted EPS).
