Free cash flow was approximately $700 million, with total shareholder returns exceeding $500 million via dividends and buybacks. Management raised full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance to $2.9 billion and increased upstream capital guidance by $30 million to $2.1 billion.

Appian reported Q3 FY2026 results with total revenue of $235 million (up 25% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $43 million, significantly beating the guidance range of $30-33 million. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for cloud subscription revenue to a midpoint growth rate of 23% and total revenue to 20% YoY, citing strong AI traction and new business momentum. The company highlighted a record net ARR expansion of 120% driven by upgrades in regulated industries and the public sector.

Arcturus Therapeutics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $18.3 million, an increase from $17.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by a $12 million termination payment from CSL Seqirus and remaining deferred revenue. Net loss narrowed to $7.4 million compared to $13.4 million last year due to reduced clinical activities and lower personnel costs. Management provided updated guidance for the cystic fibrosis program (top-line data in Q2 2027) and confirmed plans to initiate Phase II dosing for the OTC deficiency program (ARCT-2601) in Q1 2027.

HALO reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $493 million (+39% YoY) and record royalty revenue of $341 million (+44% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of $336.2 million (35% growth, 68% margin) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.39 vs $1.72 prior year. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: total revenue to $1.86-$1.925 billion (up $20 million at midpoint), royalties to $1.235-$1.255 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $1.24-$1.29 billion, and non-GAAP EPS to $8.75-$9.05 (up $0.08 at midpoint). Royalty growth broadened across DARZALEX (+20% to $153.5 million), VYVGART (+89% to $88.1 million), Phesgo (+23% to $34.3 million), and other royalties (+92% to $65.1 million). Separately, the Dutch Patent Court ruled KEYTRUDA QLEX infringes EP622 and barred Merck from marketing it across eight European markets, while U.S. patent validity rulings have gone against HALO with appeal expected into 2028.

Ardent Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.62 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $138 million, driven by a 4% year-over-year reduction in salaries, wages, and benefits (SWB) to 39.9% of revenue. Management raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by 1.5%, updating the range to $500 million-$535 million from the prior $485 million-$535 million. The company also announced a definitive agreement to divest its Kansas hospital ownership, expected to close in Q4 and enhance margins by 40 basis points.

Arhaus reported record third quarter net revenue of $368 million, up 6.8% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding 50 basis points to 39.2%. Management raised full-year net revenue guidance to a range of $1.465 billion-$1.485 billion and maintained profitability expectations despite higher SG&A expenses driven by marketing investments and variable compensation timing. The company highlighted strong demand quality, with new customer acquisition up over 20% in September and orders exceeding $100,000 increasing significantly.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 5% to $16.3M, but net income fell to $1.0M ($0.03 diluted) from $1.7M ($0.06), driven by a $1.1M increase in depreciation and higher net interest expense; operating expenses rose 10.4% to $13.9M. Adjusted EBITDA was roughly flat at $7.8M, and G&A held near $4.8M. The GW-Santa Cruz rate case was unanimously approved, adding $2.3M of annual revenue effective December 1, 2026, partly offset by a $0.4M GW-Palo Verde reduction; the larger Palo Verde case is now deferred, with four new rate filings planned for the first half of 2027 and new rates estimated in 2028. Active connections grew 2.4% to 69,797, while Phoenix MSA building permits fell 10% year-to-date.

ARKO reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $75.7 million, up from $75.2 million in the prior year, driven by a 10.4% increase in same-store fuel margin to $0.488/gallon and merchandise margin expansion to 34.8%. Management raised the low end of full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance from $245 million to $250 million, resulting in a revised range of $250-$265 million, citing strong year-to-date performance and the expected closing of the USPP acquisition.

Arlo reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $149.2 million, up 7% year-over-year, driven by subscriptions and services revenue of $96 million (up 20%) which now comprises nearly two-thirds of total revenue. Adjusted EBITDA surged 58% to $26.9 million with a margin of 18%, while non-GAAP EPS reached $0.24. Management raised visibility for 2027, targeting roughly 30% ARR growth driven by strategic partners like Comcast and Aloe Care, and approved a substantially larger stock buyback program.

Grindr reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 22% YoY to $141 million with Adjusted EBITDA of $62 million (44% margin, down from 47% a year ago on higher capitalized product development last year); app revenue rose 22% to $118 million and advertising 23% to $24 million. GAAP net loss was $7 million, driven by a $33 million one-time U.K. litigation settlement charge and $3 million Freddie transaction costs; excluding those, net income was $21 million and operating income $40 million (28% of revenue). Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to at least $560 million revenue (from ~$540 million) and at least $236 million Adjusted EBITDA (from ~$232 million), and initial 2027 guidance calls for at least $705 million revenue (~26% growth) and at least $275 million Adjusted EBITDA (~39% margin) including the Freddie acquisition and Edge launch. Management flagged moderated ad growth back toward 15%-16% of revenue and the loss of ~$10 million of telehealth direct ad revenue, with Edge ($120/month, ~400,000 early-access registrations in 72 hours) and Freddie integration (expects ~12,000 U.S. patients at year-end) as the 2027 drivers.

Evolent reported Q3 revenue of $725 million, up 11% sequentially, and Adjusted EBITDA of $34.3 million, up roughly 22% QoQ and slightly above the $4-7 million step-up guided last quarter. MER improved to 93% from 95%, a ~220 bp sequential gain driven by favorable in-year claims development. Full-year revenue guidance of $2.6-2.7 billion was reiterated while Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $130-135 million from $120-135 million; Q4 EBITDA step-up is now $11-16 million versus $7-15 million prior. Management reiterated confidence in a 2027 Adjusted EBITDA midpoint of $150 million or higher but deferred specific 2027 revenue guidance to February, citing Medicaid work-requirement attrition, renewal scope adjustments, and higher AI capex.

Eve Holding reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $58 million and R&D of $48 million, with SG&A down to $6 million from $7 million a year ago. Cash burn for the first nine months was $174 million, tracking toward the low end of the $225-275 million full-year guidance, and management said $356 million in cash plus $114 million in undrawn credit supports operations through 2028. Development milestones advanced, with 170 of 185 engineering test points (91%) validated and a first full transition flight targeted before year-end; no financial guidance was raised, but capex and burn guidance were tightened favorably. The commercial backlog stayed roughly flat at about 2,500 aircraft ($12.6 billion list) with a new 12-aircraft FlyBIS agreement (2 firm, 10 options).

Stoneridge reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $180 million, up 30% (nearly 26% core, excluding FX and $6 million Mexico contract manufacturing), the fastest organic growth in over three years, with adjusted EBITDA up over 40% YoY to $7.3 million (4.1% margin, +34 bps). However, adjusted gross margin fell 382 bps to 19.9% on inventory-related expenses and legacy warranty settlements ($3 million incremental), and reported results absorbed a ~$24 million non-cash pre-tax charge tied to a $25.5 million arbitration award on former Control Devices PM sensor claims. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $690-700 million ($37.5 million higher at midpoint), but adjusted EBITDA is now expected at the bottom of the $20-25 million range due to memory-chip inflation, unfavorable FX, and the legacy-matter costs. MirrorEye hit a record $37 million in sales (+48% YoY), and a new non-MirrorEye vision system win is expected to add ~$180 million through 2028, ramping from early 2027.

Q3 revenue of $151.4 million grew 2.7% YoY but came in just below the low end of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA of $45 million met the midpoint at a 29.7% margin versus 31.5% a year ago. Full-year 2026 guidance was set at approximately $600 million revenue and $170 million adjusted EBITDA, incorporating flat vendor rebates, top-of-funnel lead generation pressure, healthcare claims costs, and incremental Q4 paid-media investment. NRR slipped to 93.3% on declining third-party partner revenue, though payments in the top six solutions grew 15-16% and multi-solution customer counts rose 27%. New CEO Alex Goor disclosed decelerating revenue supported mainly by price actions and flagged that growth investments could weigh on near-term results.

CoreCivic reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.49 vs $0.24 a year ago (+104%), normalized FFO per share of $0.75 vs $0.48 (+56%), and adjusted EBITDA of $117.8 million vs $88.8 million (+33%), beating consensus by $0.06 on adjusted EPS and $2.7 million on EBITDA. Residential occupancy rose to 84% from 76.7%, the highest since the pandemic, with federal partner revenue up 22.2% and ICE revenue up $75.2 million (+34.8%). Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $1.74-$1.80 from $1.64-$1.73 and adjusted EBITDA to $442.5-$445.5 million from $434.5-$439.5 million. The quarter was dominated by the $2.2 billion gross sale of four facilities to DHS ($1.6 billion net), over $700 million of debt repayment, and a $500 million accelerated share repurchase plus a $500 million authorization increase.

CVRx reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $13.8 million, down 6.1% YoY and within guidance, with U.S. revenue down 4% to $13 million and Europe down 27% to $0.9 million; gross margin held at 87% and net loss widened to $14.2 million ($0.52/share) from $12.9 million ($0.49). Full-year guidance was cut to $56-57 million from a prior $58-60 million, and Q4 is guided to $11.7-12.7 million, reflecting continued degradation at the largest Medicare Advantage payer (30-day approval rate down to ~12% from 83% in 2025), physician champion turnover, and slower recovery in four less-tenured regions. Operating expenses were held at $99-101 million via cost actions including severance, cash stood at $58.7 million with at least 18 months of stated runway, and $6 million was raised through the ATM. Two written Medicare Advantage coverage policies (21% of MA lives) and a raised national inpatient rate to $45,000 were cited as offsets.

Centuri reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 40% YoY, with gross margin of 9.5% (vs 7.2% in Q2), adjusted net income of $42 million ($0.42/share) versus $17 million ($0.19) a year ago, and Adjusted EBITDA of $108 million, up 44%. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to revenue of $3.8-3.9 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of $290-300 million, and adjusted net income of $80-90 million, assuming no Q4 storm work, though free cash flow guidance was cut to $25-50 million on higher working capital. Management introduced a 2027 outlook of mid-teens revenue growth to above $4.4 billion with gross margin of 8.5%-9%, and noted the preliminary 2027 view outpaces the 2029 targets set earlier this year. Outstanding bids more than doubled to $4.8 billion and the opportunity pipeline rose 46% to $19 billion, while backlog grew 5% to roughly $6.2 billion.

CytomX reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.7 million versus $6 million in Q3 2025, with the decline attributed to the conclusion of the Astellas collaboration; operating expenses rose to $25.2 million from $21.7 million. Cash and investments were $348 million at September 30 versus $330 million at June 30, including $37 million received from Regeneron for two additional targets, with runway projected into H2 2028. Management did not provide a revenue or EPS guide; the key forward item is the Varseta-M update moved from year-end 2026 to January, when the company expects a first look at overall survival plus an integrated Phase 1 update and potential registrational strategy, with a first registrational study targeted for H1 2027. No new clinical data was disclosed on the call; initiation of the bevacizumab/5-FU/leucovorin Phase I/II study remains on track for year-end.

Cadre reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $202.9 million, up 30% year over year and 10% organically excluding distribution, with net income up 46% and Adjusted EBITDA of $41 million (margin up 110 bps to 20.2%) — both ahead of guidance. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised for the second consecutive quarter to $756-769 million in sales and $140-144 million in Adjusted EBITDA, implying ~18.6% margins and ~$197 million of Q4 revenue. The beat was driven largely by the NGABS EOD R&D program shipping a quarter early, partially offset by lower distribution revenue, while backlog fell ~$29 million sequentially on the NGABS shipment and TYR timing. Management also announced a first-ever $100 million buyback and a small precision-fabrication bolt-on (~$4-5 million revenue).

Q3 revenue fell 2.4% to $100.3M as cemetery comparable revenue dropped 7.8% to $32.5M, offsetting funeral comparable revenue growth of 3.6%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 16% to $27.7M (27.6% margin vs 32.1%) and adjusted diluted EPS came in at $0.59 vs $0.75, partly due to trust taxes; excluding those, EPS would have been $0.70. Management cut full-year guidance: revenue to $415-420M from $435-445M, adjusted EBITDA to $125-130M from $135-140M, and adjusted EPS to $2.90-3.05 from $3.35-3.55. Cemetery preneed weakness (concentrated in California) is the largest driver of the reduction, partially offset by a return to positive funeral contract growth (+2.3% same-store) and a pipeline of five pending acquisitions representing over $14M in annual revenue.

Celcuity reported Q3 FY2026 with no product revenue recognized since REVTORPYK shipments only began September 30, 2026, and product was not delivered to any treatment location until after quarter-end. Net loss widened to $73.3M ($1.33/share) from $43.8M ($0.92/share) a year ago, with opex up to $77.3M from $42.8M, driven by $25.3M of commercialization-related SG&A. Cash was $642.7M, expected to fund operations through 2029. Early launch metrics: 78% of top 36 strategic accounts ordered, 91% of commercial/Medicare lives covered, and NCCN category 1 context within two weeks; no formal guidance was issued, with a Q4 sales flash report expected mid-January.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $367 million, up 6% YoY and $17 million above the high end of the $320-350 million guide; non-GAAP EPS was $0.13 versus $0.06 a year ago and adjusted EBITDA rose 38% to $22.4 million, both above the high end of guidance. Memory revenue hit a Q3 record of $167.3 million, up 43%, while peripherals grew only 3% to $116.5 million due to $6-8 million of logistics and hub-transition timing that pushed revenue into Q4. Full-year guidance was raised: revenue midpoint up $36 million to $1.456-1.486 billion and adjusted EBITDA midpoint up $3 million to $127-131 million. Q4 revenue is guided to $420-450 million, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $38-42 million is expected below last year as memory gross margin normalizes to 18-20% from an unusually high ~35% in the prior-year quarter.

Q3 revenue of ~$847M rose ~17% YoY, aided by roughly $20-25M of shipments pulled forward from Q4, with Alani Nu net sales ~$410M (+24%, scans +58%) while brand CELSIUS net sales fell ~6%. Gross margin contracted to 46.8% from 48.1% in Q2 and 51.3% a year ago on higher aluminum and diesel, though adjusted EBITDA rose sequentially to ~$199M (23.4% margin) on SG&A leverage. Management guided Q4 reported growth below the year-to-date pace, citing a ~$25M non-recurring prior-year DSD build, the shipment pull-forward, and higher trade investment, and said commodity-driven gross margin recovery to the low 50s will take longer than previously expected.

Century Aluminum reported Q3 net sales of nearly $1 billion, up $209 million sequentially, with net income of $303 million ($2.89 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $332 million, driven by record shipments of ~173,500 tons (+33% QoQ) as Mt. Holly and Grundartangi returned to full capacity. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $275-$300 million implies a $35-$45 million sequential decline due to lower lagged LME ($3,150/ton) and premiums. Cash rose to $755 million against $486 million of debt, with $365 million of quarterly cash flow, and management said Oklahoma financing terms are largely agreed with FID pending.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $94.9M, up 4% YoY on a continuing operations basis, with software up 11% to $48.8M (first double-digit organic software growth in two years) and services down 2% to $46.1M but up 3.5% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $30.2M at a 31.8% margin, up from 31.5% a year ago and 28.1% in Q2, while adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.09 and GAAP net loss from continuing operations narrowed to $3.6M. Full-year revenue growth guidance was narrowed to 2%-3% (from the prior range), with the 29%-31% adjusted EBITDA margin outlook maintained for Q4 and adjusted EPS updated to $0.31-$0.34. Management declined to give 2027 guidance and said the services transition and APAC expansion are 2027 impacts.

Cronos reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $63.5 million, up 75% year-over-year, with gross profit of $32.3 million (up 76%) and record Adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, an $11.4 million year-over-year improvement. Israel grew 33% year-over-year (19% constant currency), Canada retail sales grew 41% versus 1% industry growth, and other international markets rose 7x to $13.2 million on German demand. Operating expenses rose 23% while OPEX fell to 37% of revenue from 52%, and cash and investments reached $841 million, up $14 million sequentially. Management gave no numeric forward guidance, citing Q4 Canadian provincial purchasing softness and lumpy international export timing, and closed the CanAdelaar acquisition in the Netherlands at under 3x trailing Adjusted EBITDA.

CF reported Q3 2026 net earnings of $436 million ($2.87/diluted share), EBITDA of $822 million and adjusted EBITDA of $833 million, with nine-month adjusted EBITDA near $3 billion already above the company's $2.9 billion mid-cycle estimate. Management flagged fall ammonia volumes among the highest in 10 years, Q3 UAN shipments near two million tons (largest this decade), and a constructive global S&D balance into 2027 on roughly 9 million tons of lost Middle East urea supply and over 35% of European ammonia capacity curtailed. Growth projects (Blue Point One, Yazoo City, Donaldsonville CCS) are expected to add $400 million to mid-cycle EBITDA by 2030, lifting it to $3.3 billion, while the company repurchased 3 million shares for ~$367 million in Q3 and returned $1.3 billion over 12 months.

Carlyle reported Q3 FY2026 distributable earnings of $433 million, or $1.12 per share, up 17% year-over-year, driven by a fivefold increase in net realized performance revenues to $100 million. Fee-related earnings were $293 million at a 47% margin, with year-to-date FRE a record $950 million and full-year FRE expected to be the highest in firm history. Inflows were $11 billion in the quarter and $41 billion year-to-date, with at least $20 billion expected in Q4 to bring the full year to about $60 billion, over 10% above last year. Pending fee-earning AUM rose nearly 50% year-over-year to $28 billion, representing more than $230 million of annualized management fees, though management noted full-year FRE growth may fall slightly short of the mid-single-digit target.

Ceragon reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $95.5 million, up 11.7% YoY, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 8.5% from 6.2% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.07 versus $0.02 a year ago. North America revenue reached $37.8 million on the anticipated rebound at the key Tier 1 carrier plus higher software mix, while India came in at $33.6 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $365-375 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 33.5%-34.5% and non-GAAP operating margin of 5%-6% at the midpoint, which the CFO said is maintained from prior guidance. The wide revenue range for Q4 was attributed solely to component supply turbulence rather than demand, with cost pressures and supplier delays expected to persist into 2027.

Q3 2026 production averaged 1.3 BCFE/d, up 8% QoQ and 9% YoY, on oil and gas sales after hedging of $359 million, EBITDAX of $266 million, and cash flow of $208 million ($0.71/share). GAAP profit was $22 million ($0.08/share), but adjusted net income was only $6 million ($0.02/share) excluding a $35 million pre-tax mark-to-market hedge gain. Management announced a $1.65 billion divestiture of 20% Legacy Haynesville / 15% Western Haynesville / 15% Pinnacle interests to SOCAR, which pro forma cuts net debt from $3.4 billion to about $1.7 billion and leverage from 3.2x to 2x, plus a Jerry Jones drilling venture funding 85%/80% of 27 wells. No explicit updated production or capex guidance was given beyond restating 2026 drilling plans and noting Q4 free cash flow.

Collegium reported record net product revenue of $216.3 million, up 3% year-over-year, with JORNAY PM up 24% to $51.9 million and AZSTARYS contributing $26.5 million in its first full quarter. Offsetting gains were in the pain portfolio: XTAMPZA fell 9% and NUCYNTA dropped 44% year-over-year, driving adjusted EBITDA down 9% to $121.6 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.96 from $2.25. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $825-855 million product revenue and $445-470 million adjusted EBITDA (essentially flat versus 2025), and management disclosed no signals yet of a Teva generic BELBUCA launch after the January 23, 2027 settlement date.

Cognex reported record Q3 revenue of $313 million, up 19% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.53 (+89%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35.5% (+1,240 bps). Adjusted gross margin expanded 360 bps to 71.3% on favorable mix, volume, and pricing. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.14-1.16 billion (~16-17% growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 31-32% (~1,000 bps expansion), with adjusted EPS of $1.68-1.72 (+67-75%). Q4 guidance was initiated at revenue of $270-290 million (~11% growth) and adjusted EPS of $0.37-0.41 (+44% at midpoint), with the comparison noted as more challenging against a strong Q4 2025.

Americold reported Q3 FY2026 same-store warehouse revenue up 4.9% YoY with NOI up 5.5%, handling margin at a record 15.9% (up 230 bps), physical occupancy of 70% (up 460 bps YoY) and economic occupancy of 78.5% (up 210 bps YoY). AFFO of $0.35 per share beat expectations, and management raised FY2026 AFFO guidance to $1.31-$1.33 and same-store NOI to $680-$700 million (about $13 million higher at the midpoint), the second consecutive raise. The $1.3 billion EQT JV closed August 31, repaying $1.15 billion of debt, eliminating 2026-2028 maturities, cutting leverage a full turn to 6.2x and saving nearly $50 million in annual interest, but adding about $0.03 of Q4 dilution and $0.07-$0.08 in 2027. Management characterized demand as stabilizing but not inflecting, guiding Q4 pricing up about 100 bps and warning of Q1 2027 pressure from retail customer rationalizations and seasonality, with AFFO lowest in Q1 and building through the year.

Chord reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted free cash flow of approximately $442 million, with the majority returned to shareholders via buybacks on top of a $1.30/share base dividend; shares outstanding are down ~10.8 million (17%) since the Enerplus combination. Q4 volume guidance was set well above both August expectations and consensus, oil guidance was raised twice in 2026 (159 to 162.5 mboe/d), and management sees holding 162.5 flat into 2027. Capital guidance rose to about $146 million on more operated and non-operated activity plus $20 million of incremental midstream investment, and new marketing savings of $35-$55 million bring total annual savings to roughly $85 million. Prior guidance had not included the Q4 volume raise or the incremental marketing savings.

Cigna reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $73.8 billion, adjusted after-tax earnings of $2.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $7.98, led by Evernorth revenue growth of 6% to $63.8 billion and Cigna Healthcare revenue growth of 9% to $11.7 billion. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $30.60 and tightened its MCR range around a maintained 84.2% midpoint while raising the Cigna Healthcare segment earnings guide to at least $4.6 billion. Forward commentary was two-sided: Specialty and Care Services earnings grew 15% to $1.1 billion, but management guided Evernorth to low single-digit earnings growth in 2027, with Pharmacy Benefit Services down single digits on gross rebate compression, lower employer GLP-1 coverage, fewer specialty/biologics launches and the ACA exchange exit (roughly $200 million headwind, or about $0.60 of run-rate EPS).

Canadian Natural reported Q3 2026 total production of ~1.65 million BOE/d, up ~31,000 BOE/d YoY, with thermal in situ at a record ~300,000 bbl/d (+9% YoY) and North American conventional liquids at a record ~358,000 bbl/d (+16% YoY), despite a planned Horizon turnaround. Adjusted funds flow was ~CAD 5.5 billion (CAD 2.68/share), adjusted net earnings CAD 3.4 billion (CAD 1.67/share), and net debt ended at ~CAD 12.1 billion, hitting the CAD 13 billion target ahead of schedule and moving the buyback to 100% of free cash flow. Management guided to a very strong Q4, with the Horizon turnaround completed 7 days early (adding ~23,000 bbl/d in Q4), extended turnaround intervals to three years (+~5,000 bbl/d average capacity), and targeted buybacks of CAD 800 million per month in November and December. No formal financial guidance ranges or comparisons to prior guidance/consensus were provided in the transcript.

Q3 FY2026 revenue from continuing operations was $534 million versus $605 million in Q3 2025 (down ~12% YoY) but up sequentially from Q2. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $36 million from $31 million, with margin up 160 bps YoY to 6.7%, while commercial revenue fell 16% on contract losses including the largest commercial client rolling off, and government revenue fell to $226 million from $238 million. New business ACV was $61 million versus $70 million in the prior-year quarter, with the $2.9 billion qualified pipeline up modestly from the start of the year. Full-year 2026 guidance ($2.15-2.25 billion revenue, $140-170 million Adjusted EBITDA) was unchanged, and Q3 free cash flow was negative $117 million, attributed to a paused factoring facility.

Q3 revenue of $84.2 million landed in line with the $82.5-$85.5 million guide, while non-GAAP operating income of $8 million (9.5% margin) beat the $3.3-$5.3 million range, aided by roughly $3 million of savings pulled forward from Q4. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $339-$342 million and non-GAAP operating income was raised $2.3 million at the midpoint to $35.3-$37.3 million, with roughly $5 million of in-year operating-plan savings versus $3 million previously. Offsets included total ARR down $2.9 million sequentially to $357.6 million, net revenue retention falling to 94.7% from 95.8%, and non-GAAP gross margin down about 110 bps sequentially to 74.5% on AI infrastructure costs. A $50 million buyback was authorized, and CFO/COO Daniel Lentz is departing effective November 13 with Tyler Duncan as interim CFO.

Cummins reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $9.4B, up 13% YoY, with record EBITDA of $1.8B (18.9% of sales, up ~170 bps ex-items) and record gross margin of 27.7%; net earnings were $1.1B, or $8.25 per diluted share. Revenue came in below management's own expectations, roughly half from a Power Systems supplier constraint (~$200M pushed to Q4) and half from weaker North America pickup truck demand. Full-year guidance was narrowed to the low end: revenue growth of approximately 10% (prior 10%-13%) and EBITDA margin of approximately 18.2% (prior 18%-18.5%), with pickup truck shipment guidance cut to 118,000-122,000 units from 125,000-140,000 and medium-duty truck market forecast lowered. Power generation demand remains exceptionally strong with orders extending into the second half of 2028, and most delayed shipments are expected to recover in Q4.

Chimera reported a GAAP net loss of $193.6 million and a 16.5% decline in book value to $14.82, with economic return of negative 13.98% for the quarter, though EAD of $0.38 per share covered the $1.45 of dividends paid and nine-month EAD of $1.38 exceeded $1.35 of dividends. HomeXpress originated a record $1.12 billion of loans (+27% YoY) but net origination margin was negative 7 bps with EBITDA of only $0.4 million. Management guided to roughly flat HomeXpress profitability in Q4 plus an expected hit to investment portfolio financials from loans held for securitization, with a return to origination profitability expected in Q1 2027. Book value was up about 5% quarter-to-date as rates and spreads tightened, and PRISM 2026-HX1 priced with AAA spreads at 160 bps.

Clean Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $112 million, 66.8 million gallons of RNG distributed (up 9% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA of $27.2 million versus $17.3 million a year ago, and a GAAP net loss of $5.7 million versus a $23.8 million loss in Q3 FY2025. Guidance for 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was raised by $5 million to $75-80 million, driven by improved 45Z values under the DOE's updated GREET model. Results included an $8.3 million catch-up from applying new 45Z values to first-half production plus $5.8 million from third-party producers; management flagged possible one-time Q4 charges tied to organizational changes and will give its 2027 outlook in February.

Coeur reported Q3 revenue up 77% YoY and gold production up 45% YoY, largely from the New Afton and Rainy River acquisitions, but the quarter came in lighter than expected on lower realized metals prices (gold -4%, silver -13% QoQ) and operational setbacks. Adjusted EBITDA was $448 million (~46% margin, up 2% from Q2), GAAP net income ~$109 million or $0.11/share, free cash flow ~$240 million, with $111 million of buybacks (46% of FCF). Management kept full-year guidance ranges but now points to the low end of gold, silver and copper production and the upper end of cost guidance, requiring Q4 gold up 29% and silver up 36% QoQ; costs were adjusted lower for capex, taxes, exploration and G&A. Dilution from wet weather at Rainy River and Palmarejo and a New Afton conveyor failure hit the quarter, partly offset by record Rochester crushing and a Wharf rebound.

Consensus reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $91.0 million, up 3.7% YoY, with corporate revenue at a record $61.4 million (+9.1% YoY) and SoHo at $29.6 million (-6% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA was $47.6 million (52.3% margin, +2.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS was $1.50 (+8.7% YoY). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.00-$6.10 while revenue ($360-364M) and adjusted EBITDA ($188-192M) were narrowed to the above-midpoint/high end of the prior range; Q4 guidance was provided with revenue midpoint of $90.9 million and EPS midpoint of $1.53. Net revenue retention improved to 104.5% from 103.1% last quarter, and free cash flow of $38.6 million was down 13.2% YoY on tax and interest timing but ahead of forecast.

Ducommun reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $227M, up 6% YoY, a record, with commercial aerospace up 28% to $97M offsetting a 7% decline in military and space to $119M. Gross margin set a record at 28.9% (up 140 bps from 27.5%), while adjusted operating margin slipped to 12.3% from 12.7% on stock-based comp timing and adjusted EPS was $1.21 versus $1.22. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $885-890M from $880-890M, essentially intact, with no EPS guide. Bookings were a record $354M at 1.6 book-to-bill and defense RPO hit a record $1.3B, though missile framework order conversion is not expected until late Q1/Q2 2027.

DTE reported Q3 2026 operating earnings of $481 million, or $2.30 per share, with DTE Electric earnings down $73 million YoY on tax timing, higher rate base and storm costs, partly offset by rate implementation and warmer weather. Management said it remains positioned for the high end of 2026 EPS guidance (6%-8% growth off the 2025 midpoint), supported by RNG tax credits and Vantage earnings above its guidance range. The company announced the ~$3 billion sale of DTE Vantage to J.P. Morgan Asset Management infrastructure investors (expected close H1 2027) and raised its five-year utility capex plan to ~$44 billion, up nearly $10 billion, alongside a 2027 pro forma operating EPS baseline of $7.59-$7.73 and >9% annual EPS CAGR thereafter. Vantage results included a $69 million YoY increase to $110 million on higher RNG and investment tax credits, and a 7% dividend increase was cited for 2027.

Entravision reported Q3 2026 consolidated revenue of $226.3 million, up 88% YoY, with operating income of $28.3 million versus a $9.1 million loss a year ago, driven by ATS revenue up 133% to $177.2 million and ATS operating profit up 261% to $35.2 million. However, ATS revenue fell 3% sequentially and ATS operating profit fell 12% QoQ on newly onboarded staff and temporary multi-cloud migration costs, while media revenue rose 10% to $49.1 million on $6 million of political ads and swung to a $0.1 million profit from a $3.5 million loss. Management reaffirmed Q4 ATS revenue growth of more than 100% YoY, extended the Univision affiliation to March 31, 2027 while exploring strategic alternatives for the TV business without Univision, and agreed to watch Tampa TV stations for $30 million. 2026 political revenue of approximately $25 million came in at the low end of the internal range, well below $34 million in 2024 and $32 million in 2022.

Total Q3 revenue rose 10% to $24.0M with diagnostic testing up 16% to $23.0M and test volume up 24% to ~19,400, but management said results 'did not meet our expectations'; gross margin held at 81% and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 16% to $3.9M. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reset to $101M-$103M (~15% growth at the midpoint), and Q4 diagnostic revenue growth normalizes to roughly 2% YoY after stripping ~1M of prior-year back-claims collection. The shortfall was attributed to fewer sales reps (101 averaged vs plan, now 110, targeting 115 by year-end), primary care seasonality, and customer-delayed development services projects that slipped into 2027, with Q4 development services guided to ~$1M and 2027 to 7%-8% of revenue. Average revenue per test fell 6% YoY on a mix shift toward Nodify CDT.

BGC reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $832.6 million, up 13% YoY, with total brokerage revenue up 14.8% to $772.8 million and post-tax adjusted EPS of $0.34, up 17.2%. Pre-tax adjusted earnings rose 20.9% to $187.5 million on a 33.9% incremental margin, and adjusted EBITDA jumped 48.9% to $249.5 million. Q4 guidance of $805-865 million revenue and $178-196 million pre-tax adjusted earnings implies about 10% revenue and 16% earnings growth at the midpoint; the prior guidance comparison was not provided in the text. Leadership transition: JP Aubin moves to Vice Chairman at year-end, with two co-CEOs remaining.

EPAM reported Q3 revenue of $1.426 billion, up 2.3% year-over-year (2.5% organic constant currency), beating the high end of guidance; non-GAAP EPS rose 14% to $3.51 and GAAP EPS rose 32.5% to $2.53, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 32.8% from 31% and GAAP operating margin up to 12.3% from 10.4%. The company raised its AI-native revenue target for 2026 to at least $650 million from $600 million and lifted full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $13.23–$13.31, but Q4 revenue guidance of $1.405–$1.420 billion implies roughly -0.2% to 0.9% year-over-year growth (0.5%–1.6% organic CC), a sharp deceleration. Management also flagged that 2027 gross margin may be modestly lower as the Poland R&D tax benefit falls from about $40 million in 2026 to about $20 million in 2027, and that 2027 non-GAAP operating margin is expected in the 15%–16% range versus 16% guidance for Q4. Growth remains concentrated: financial services rose 13.7%, life sciences and healthcare rose 9.9%, while software and high tech fell 6.1% and consumer goods, retail, and travel fell 2.5%, with Americas up only 0.2%.

Revenue hit a record $82.7 million, up 171% year-over-year and 20% sequentially on a 23% sequential rise in cube shipments. Adjusted gross margin improved 18 points sequentially and 58 points year-over-year on a GAAP basis, with Adjusted EBITDA of -$63.8 million (a 27-point sequential improvement), but net income of $125 million was driven by non-cash mark-to-market gains on warrants and debt, not operations. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $300 million to $325 million, with Q4 Adjusted gross margin guided to -25% to -20% (another 19-24 points of improvement), while 2027 guidance was deferred to the Q4 call. Backlog fell sequentially to $765 million (about 3.2 GWh) from $807 million in Q2 because shipments exceeded bookings, though it was up 19% year-over-year and the company cited 3.5 GWh of late-stage opportunity.

Enovis reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $559M, up 2% reported and 5% organic, with Recon +6% organic (extremities +8%, hips/knees +3%, international Recon +8%) and P&R +3% organic. Adjusted gross margin was 60.9% (+60 bps, including $8M tariff refunds), adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5% (+120 bps), and adjusted EPS $0.88, up 17%; free cash flow was $35M in the quarter. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $2.32-2.35B (~5% organic), while adjusted EBITDA was raised to $428-438M and adjusted EPS to $3.58-3.79, partly offset by a $4M enabling-tech R&D investment and $1M FX headwind in Q4. Management characterized the quarter as in line with August expectations in a choppy market, announced a new $200M buyback authorization, and declined to discuss 2027 beyond prior September commentary.

Excelerate reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $60 million, up $10 million sequentially, and record adjusted EBITDA of roughly $133 million, up $13 million QoQ on the new Jordan charter and higher LNG/gas/power direct margins. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $495-515 million, maintenance capex lowered to $65-75 million on deferred work, and committed growth capex raised to $400-410 million for the FSRU conversion timing, with total capex broadly unchanged. The company announced an 11-year AxDo LNG supply agreement underpinning a Bahamas LNG Hub ($85-95 million FSU, ~$6 million 2027 EBITDA rising to ~$15 million), extended the Sequoia charter through 2038 adding over $400 million of backlog, and reiterated $250-300 million of incremental EBITDA growth by 2029 from Iraq, Colombia, Caribbean, and reliquefaction projects. Net debt was $871 million at 1.8x trailing leverage with $357 million of cash and a $0.09 quarterly dividend targeting low-double-digit annual growth through 2028.

Q3 sales of $309 million rose 51% YoY, including ~$67 million of sulfur cost pass-through, and Adjusted EBITDA of $61 million was up over 6% and above the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $208-$212 million (a 4.5% midpoint increase from $195-$207 million), sales to $1.05-$1.07 billion, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow to $50-$60 million, with a $3 million turnaround deferral into early 2027 aiding the raise. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 19.8% from 28.1%, though management said it would have been ~550 bps higher excluding the sulfur pass-through. Q4 Adjusted EBITDA is guided to $54-$58 million.

BJ's reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $358.6 million, up 8.6%, with same-store sales up 8.1% on 8.3% traffic growth and a 0.2% check decline. Restaurant-level operating margin expanded 220 bps to 14.7% on $52.9 million of profit, and adjusted EBITDA rose $10.3 million to $31.4 million (8.8% margin, up 240 bps). Management raised full-year comp guidance to approximately 4.7% from 3%-4%, lifted restaurant-level operating profit to $233-$237 million and adjusted EBITDA to $149-$154 million, and lowered capex to approximately $80 million; Q4 expectations were held largely unchanged with an approximately 100 bps holiday calendar headwind.

Black Hills reported Q3 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.54 including $0.03 of merger costs, or $0.57 adjusted vs $0.45 in Q3 2025; YTD adjusted EPS was $2.89 vs $2.68. The company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.25-$4.45 (about 6% growth at the midpoint) and said it expects to deliver in the upper half of its 4%-6% long-term EPS growth rate. The key change was the executed definitive agreements to serve Google's planned Wyoming data center, involving $1.8 billion of non-regulated generation investment, 2.1 GW of managed third-party resources, roughly $700 million of transmission, and approximately $150 million of net income expected in 2030, to be added to the 2027-2031 plan in February. Regulatory progress included Arkansas Gas approval of $17.9 million and South Dakota Electric settlements of $27.4 million (SD) and $4 million (WY); the NorthWestern merger awaits a Montana decision by November 12.

DXP reported record Q3 sales of $587.2 million, up 14.3% YoY, with 8.7% organic growth and $48.8 million from acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $67.3 million (11.5% margin), operating income grew 20.1% to $52.5 million (8.9% margin), and diluted EPS increased 25.2% to $1.64 from $1.31. Gross margin fell 70 bps to 30.7% on mix shifts in Service Centers and IPS, partly offset by 108 bps of SG&A leverage. No formal guidance was issued; management cited unchanged priorities (organic growth, margin expansion, DXP Water, acquisitions, cash generation) and noted October average daily sales of $9.03 million versus $9.60 million in September.

BlackSky reported record Q3 revenue of $42.8 million, up 118% year-over-year and ~30% sequentially, with space-based intelligence and AI services at $32.7 million (+107% YoY), Mission Solutions at $4.7 million (~5x), and Advanced Technology Programs at $5.4 million (+80%). Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $12.8 million at a 30% margin, more than double Q2, net income was $18.5 million versus a $15.3 million loss a year ago, and operating cash flow turned positive. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $140-150 million and Adjusted EBITDA to $18-24 million for the second time this year, maintaining CapEx guidance at $50-60 million, and cited a $355 million total backlog with ~$45 million expected in Q4.

BKV reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDAX of $133 million versus $101 million a year earlier, adjusted net income of $40 million ($0.36 per diluted share), and adjusted free cash flow of ~$31 million excluding strategic power capital. Upstream production of 981 MMcfe/d came in above the top end of guidance, with cash unit costs 9% below the prior two quarters and development capital of $51 million below the low end; total capex of ~$187 million was under the $245 million midpoint. Guidance was updated to reflect the closed Barnett acquisition, now expecting production above 1 Bcf/d while keeping original capital guidance other than higher anticipated strategic power capex ($240-270 million in Q4). Power results fell short of expectations as solar and battery additions pressured peak pricing realizations, partly offset by a 72% capacity factor and $34 million gross power adjusted EBITDA.

Total revenue declined sequentially by 1.8% to $231.2 million and decreased year-over-year, driven primarily by a 19.5% drop in off-net revenues ($76.6M) as the company rotates away from lower-margin acquired Sprint customers. Adjusted EBITDA grew sequentially by $2.8 million to $73.9 million with margins expanding 150 bps to 32%, supported by cost reductions and a shift toward higher-margin on-net services which now comprise 67% of total revenue. Management suspended its dividend program while addressing the maturity of $700 million in 2027 notes, citing a deliberate evaluation process for refinancing options.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $193.4M, up 8.5% but at the low end of guidance, with ARR up 7% to $735M, calculated billings up 6%, and NRR at 103.5% on lower user adds. Non-GAAP operating margin was 25.9% (up ~450 bps YoY, above the top end of guidance), adjusted EPS $0.64 (up 25%), and free cash flow $58M at a 30% margin. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut to $759.5-761.5M (8.4-8.7% growth) from the prior outlook, with nearly half the reduction from professional services; Q4 revenue is guided to $195-197M (6.5-7.6% growth) on softer September close rates and no assumed recovery. The key change versus prior periods is extending deal-slippage timelines, below-plan agentic AI consumption, SolEx hesitancy, and Middle East/public sector award delays, partly offset by platform ARR reaching 23% of eligible ARR and RPO up 14%.

Total revenue was $32.9 million, up 1% YoY and in the top half of guidance, while non-GAAP operating income of $4.9 million beat the high end of the range. However, management lowered Q4 revenue guidance to a decline of 8%-15% YoY due to a significantly deteriorating macro environment with refinance volume down roughly 60%. The company highlighted strong Autopilot adoption and new deals but warned that 2027 growth will rely on converting this pipeline rather than market volume.

Bob's Discount Furniture reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $680 million, a 10% increase year-over-year, driven by 3.8% comparable sales growth and contributions from 11 new store openings. Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% to $75.5 million with an 11.1% margin, though gross margin decreased 30 basis points to 45.7% due to higher fuel and inventory costs. Management maintained full-year guidance for net revenue of $2.6 billion-$2.63 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $255 million-$265 million despite expecting a full-year gross margin decline of 20-30 basis points.

Bentley Systems reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $422 million, a 12.2% year-over-year increase driven by strong subscription growth and asset analytics expansions. The company raised its full-year ARR growth outlook to 12.5%-13.5%, excluding the impact of the recent Cohesive divestiture which reduced Q4 revenue guidance by approximately $12 million. Management highlighted that ARR growth accelerated to 13% YoY, surpassing the high end of the original annual range.

B2Gold reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $836 million and adjusted net income of $183 million ($0.14/share), driven by 195,000 ounces of gold sold at an average price of $4,287/oz. Management lowered full-year all-in sustaining cost guidance to a range of $2,230-$2,410/oz (down from the prior midpoint) and free cash flow for the quarter was $48 million. The company remains on track for full-year production targets despite lower Q3 grades at Fekola due to waste stripping.

Total revenue for Q3 FY2026 was $26 million, down from $46.3 million in the prior year period, primarily due to the absence of a $7 million Amazon Prime Day event in 2025. The company reported a net loss of $18.7 million and an adjusted EBITDA of -$4.8 million following a workforce reduction that generated one-time restructuring expenses of $7.1 million. Management deferred financial guidance as they integrate the Allen Family Digital transaction and restructuring changes.

Cable One reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $332.2 million, a decrease of approximately $44 million year-over-year compared to $376 million in the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $159.8 million from $201.9 million, driven by declines in residential data and video revenues alongside lower advertising sales due to a third-party transition. While net subscriber losses narrowed significantly to approximately 7,500 (best in seven quarters), the company explicitly acknowledged that ARPU declined $2 sequentially and business services revenue was impacted by divested assets.

Diversified reported Q3 FY2026 production of ~1.2 BCFE/d, commodity revenue of $470 million (~$4.29/Mcfe), adjusted EBITDA of $256 million at a 56% margin, and adjusted free cash flow of $153 million. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at ~$1 billion adjusted EBITDA and ~$440 million adjusted free cash flow, excluding the Birch acquisition expected to close before year-end. Year-to-date the company repaid ~$313 million of debt principal and returned ~$157 million to shareholders, and the credit facility was upsized to $1 billion after quarter-end. The quarter was in-line with no guidance change, with the main swing factor being the pending Birch deal (pro forma production +~35%, EBITDA +~55%).

Revenue rose 10.9% YoY to $99.3M on an adjusted basis, with all four strategic markets growing nearly 30% collectively; non-GAAP gross margin expanded 420 bps to 35.5% and Adjusted EBITDA improved $13.1M YoY to +$3.1M. Non-GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.06, a $0.02 improvement. Q4 guidance is revenue of $100-103M with Adjusted EBITDA of -$2M to break-even, reflecting customer order timing variability and less year-end concentration. The company launched an ATM equity program and plans to exchange its 2030 secured notes for new unsecured notes due 2031.

Q3 revenue was $437 million, down 6% year-over-year due to strategic launch timing and lower tariffs, but exceeding expectations. Adjusted EBITDA of $36 million rose 17% year-over-year, driven by gross margin expansion of approximately 520 basis points to 45.0%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by approximately $14 million at the midpoint and increased Adjusted EBITDA guidance by $23 million at the midpoint.

CarGurus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $258 million, a 12% year-over-year increase at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $89.7 million and a margin of 35%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.0115 billion-$1.0165 billion (up 11.5%-12.1% YoY) and provided Q4 guidance of $258.5 million-$263.5 million. The company highlighted strong adoption of new products like StockVantage and VINMax, though it noted that dealer enthusiasm has not yet returned to 2025 levels due to margin pressure.

Q3 revenue of $182 million was within guidance and up slightly year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 30.7%, outperforming the high end of guidance by 120 basis points. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for flat to 2% revenue growth and a 29%-30% adjusted EBITDA margin, expecting year-end performance toward the lower end of the revenue range due to OEM spending trends. The company highlighted strong free cash flow generation enabling a $74 million share buyback year-to-date against a $90 million target.

Allient reported record Q3 FY2026 results with revenue of $164.4 million (up 18% YoY) and gross margin expanding 330 bps to a record 36.6%. Operating income surged 83% to $22.3 million, driving net income more than double to $15.3 million ($0.91 EPS). Management raised the full-year capital expenditure guidance range to $12-$15 million and highlighted record backlog of $351.5 million.

Allogene reported Q3 FY2026 results with a business update highlighting strong enrollment momentum for the ALPHA3 trial in lymphoma and brisk activity in the Asia-Pacific region. Management expressed high confidence in the outpatient/community setting delivery of cema-cel, noting a significant surge in interest from community practices over the summer. The company reaffirmed its guidance to complete ALPHA3 enrollment by the end of 2027 and maintain the mid-2027 update timeline for the interim futility analysis.

Revenue of $70.2 million came in $0.2 million above the guidance midpoint, up 31% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, with core business up ~14% quarter-over-quarter to $40.7 million and Wuxi up ~5% to $29.5 million. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $7.2 million from $11.3 million a year ago, and non-GAAP net loss per share improved $0.02 to $0.05. Q4 guidance of $73-81 million ($77 million midpoint) implies ~33% year-over-year growth, and management said its 2027 revenue outlook is in line with current analyst estimates. Gross margin ticked down sequentially to 41.6% on Wuxi mix pressure, with a modest Q4 uptick expected and blended margins moving to the low 50s after the Wuxi divestiture.

Allstate reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17.3 billion, Property-Liability net premiums written up 2.5% to $16 billion, and policies in force up 3.9% (Property-Liability 3.3%). Adjusted net income was nearly $2.5 billion, or $9.76 per share, with a 39.7% adjusted ROE; the Property-Liability combined ratio was 86.6, 6.5 points above the prior year on 7.1 points of higher catastrophe losses, partly offset by 2.4 points of favorable prior-year reserve releases. Auto underlying combined ratio adjusted to 91.4 (better than mid-90s target) and homeowners underlying 60.1; management characterized results as strong while noting auto loss-cost inflation and taking 0.4 points of rate across 39 locations. No explicit forward EPS or combined-ratio guidance was quantified; the key change versus prior periods is continued policy growth alongside softening average auto premiums due to ASC mix.

PDF Solutions reported record Q3 revenue of $68.3 million, representing a 20% year-over-year increase and an 11% quarter-over-quarter rise. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance for 20% annual revenue growth and maintained its long-term target gross margin model of 77%. Gross margins expanded to 77% from 73% in the prior quarter, driven by reduced eProbe costs and controlled personnel spending.

PAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $137.1 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $532.5-$536.5 million from the prior $516-$523 million range, citing strong ARR growth and multi-product adoption. The company delivered record free cash flow of $17.7 million and improved non-GAAP subscription margins sequentially.

Pan American Silver reported Q3 FY2026 attributable free cash flow of $377 million and net earnings of $357 million ($0.86/share), though silver production of 6.1M ounces missed the quarterly outlook range due to sequencing at Juanicipio and Cerro Moro, and gold production was impacted by delays at Timmins and Shahuindo. Management revised full-year gold production guidance downward to 660k-680k ounces and raised full-year gold all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,000-$2,150/oz due to lower production, increased development costs, and El Niño weather impacts. While silver segment costs came in below expectations at $11.21/oz, the company faces operational headwinds including a 40-day downtime at Huaron for mill repairs and ongoing remediation work at Jacobina affecting 2027 production.

Consolidated revenues grew 9% YoY to $145M OIBDA (up 6%) and $103M AFFO (up 5%), driven by strong 20% growth in transit and mid-single-digit growth in billboard. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance to approximately 25% growth compared to the prior year, citing robust Q4 bookings and continued investment in AI-enabled sales tools. The quarter included roughly $50M of incremental FIFA World Cup revenue, with management expressing high confidence in sustaining momentum into 2027.

Net product revenue declined 70% year-over-year to $45.5 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by a contraction in the skin substitute market following CMS policy changes and discarded product comments. Operating loss widened to $29.5 million compared to income last year due to lower revenue and reduced gross margins (52% vs 76%), though operating expenses decreased significantly by $55.2 million year-over-year. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to a net revenue range of $179-$200 million, representing a decline of 65%-68%, which is slightly wider than the prior guidance of 62%-68%.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Ormat reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $275 million (up 10.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $153.8 million (up 11.1%), driven by a 145% surge in energy storage revenue to $49.9 million. Management raised the full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.17-$1.20 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $640-$650 million, citing strong momentum in storage and electricity segments despite a temporary Puna outage impact.

Third quarter revenue was $1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, while Contribution Profit rose 70% to $34 million despite a weaker housing market. Contribution Margin declined sequentially to 3.3% from Q2's 5.8% due to watching spring acquisitions into a difficult market and deeper price cuts for clearance. Management expects margins to decline again in Q4 as the company continues clearing inventory and increases marketing spend.

Third quarter revenue was $203 million, a decrease of $22 million year-over-year primarily due to the normalization of recovery services following a significant environmental event in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $36 million with a record margin of 17.7%, and full-year 2026 guidance remains unchanged at the midpoint implying approximately 150 basis points of margin expansion compared to 2025.

OceanaGold reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $655 million and adjusted EPS of $0.94, representing a significant beat against consensus estimates. The company generated $155 million in free cash flow and returned $79 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, ending the quarter with $729 million in cash and zero debt. Management confirmed they remain on track to meet full-year production guidance, expecting Q4 to be the strongest quarter of the year driven by higher production at Haile and Didipio.

Orion reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $67 million (up 16% YoY) and generated $46 million in free cash flow, aided by a one-time timing benefit of approximately $17 million from EU emission allowances. Management raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance while reaffirming free cash flow targets, noting that year-to-date results are not materially affected by the allowance timing. The company expects Q4 to be subdued due to seasonality and planned turnaround costs, but remains focused on deleveraging with net leverage at 4.1x.

Nyxoah reported Q3 FY2026 global net revenue of EUR 9.2 million (up 19% sequentially and 365% YoY), with U.S. revenue reaching EUR 6.7 million. Gross margin expanded to 63.1%, but the company adjusted its full-year 2026 revenue guidance down to a range of EUR 33-35 million, citing a need for revenues to be more reflective of historical ramps for the new technology. Management emphasized financial discipline and reduced cash burn while maintaining confidence in the Genio product's differentiation.

Nexstar reported record Q3 net revenue of $2.13 billion and record Adjusted EBITDA of $756 million, driven by the TEGNA acquisition and a record-breaking political advertising cycle totaling $1.1 billion for the year. Non-political advertising declined low single digits excluding political crowd-out, while distribution revenue grew 4.2% on a legacy basis. Management reiterated that legacy Nexstar's net distribution guidance remains intact despite the election cycle ending.

Q3 revenue grew 14% YoY to $78.8 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $10.3 million (13% margin), finishing above the high end of guidance. Platform WAU reached a record 24.5 million, up 7% sequentially and 14% YoY, driven by organic reactivation without paid user acquisition. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance to $78-$80 million and Adjusted EBITDA to $10-$11 million, citing strong advertiser demand and new product rollouts.

NorthWestern Energy reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $0.50 versus $0.62 in the prior year quarter, while non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.58 compared to $0.79 last year. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance range of $3.68-$3.83 with a bias toward the lower half due to weak market prices and weather impacts offsetting margin improvements. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.67 per share and anticipates completing the merger with Black Hills Corporation by year-end pending final Montana PSC approval.

Nova reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $287.8 million (up 28% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $2.64, exceeding the top end of guidance. The company raised its H2 2026 growth guidance to >33% and provided Q4 revenue guidance of $305-$315 million with non-GAAP EPS of $3.03-$3.18. Management highlighted record profitability, strong memory segment performance, and successful acceptance of the AncoScene platform.

Nu Skin reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $311 million and adjusted EPS of $0.10, both within the previously issued guidance range. Gross margin contracted to 65% from 70.5% in the prior year due to revenue mix shifts between core and Rhyz businesses. Management reiterated full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $0.55-$0.65 while noting ongoing pressures in the core business.

Natera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $794 million, up approximately 34% year-over-year (north of 40% excluding true-ups), driven by a record 1.1 million tests processed and strong growth in oncology MRD volumes which rose 56%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $3.005-$3.035 billion, increasing the midpoint by approximately $140 million compared to prior guidance. The company also set a long-term goal to double revenues to $6 billion by 2029.

Insight Enterprises reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $2.4 billion (up 22% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.59 (up 34%). Gross profit grew 20%, driven by strong infrastructure hardware growth (>50%) and cloud services, while management raised its full-year 2026 gross profit growth guidance to 12.5%-14% and adjusted EPS midpoint to $13.75.

NerdWallet reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $240 million (up 11% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $30 million, both missing the company's guidance range due to a $17 million decline in auto insurance revenue. Management lowered full-year expectations for NGOI to $85-$91 million, citing continued negative impact from vertical integration investments and AI projects. While consumer revenue grew 12% YoY, organic search traffic has stabilized after severe declines, and the company expects Q4 revenue of $191-$203 million.

The company delivered combined revenue of CAD 438 million, up CAD 47 million year-over-year driven by an acquired entity in Australia and organic growth in Canada, though gross margins were pressured by a significant project loss on the Fargo joint venture. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a midpoint of CAD 385 million from CAD 400 million due to operational challenges in Australia and the Fargo impact, while raising revenue guidance slightly to a midpoint of CAD 1.75 billion. The CFO noted that Australian margins are expected to normalize to the 15%-20% range in 2027 following Q4 recovery.

National MI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $187.5 million and adjusted net income of $93.7 million ($1.23 EPS), beating the prior quarter's results despite a sequential decline in NIW volume to $13.6 billion from $14.0 billion implied by the YoY comparison. The company ended with a record $229.7 billion of primary insurance-in-force and maintained strong credit performance with a 1.23% default rate, though persistency dipped slightly to 80.8%. Management expressed confidence in the business outlook while noting that macro risks remain and that Q4 expenses may be seasonally higher.

NHP reported Q3 FY2026 same-store cash NOI growth of 13.6% and a same-store cash NOI margin expansion of 150 bps to 24.3%, driven by higher occupancy and pricing power following the deployment of short-term concessions. Management raised its full-year 2026 SHOP same-store cash NOI growth guidance to 16.5%-18.5% and confirmed the completion of a significant OMF portfolio exit with $1.1 billion in gross proceeds. The company is transitioning to a pure-play senior housing REIT with a strengthened balance sheet, having retired preferred equity and reduced secured debt.

Third quarter sales were $305 million, down approximately 8% on a reported basis primarily due to the divestiture of the Road Markings product line, while excluding that segment sales increased 2%. Adjusted EBITDA was $108 million (down 2%), with margins expanding 230 bps to 35.4%, and diluted adjusted EPS rose 24% to $1.63. Management maintained the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook at a midpoint of $390 million despite higher input costs and softer demand in Pavement Technologies.

MGIC reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $175 million and diluted EPS of $0.85, beating the prior year's $0.83 despite a slight decline in insurance in force growth to 3.6% YoY. Management maintained its initial claim rate assumption at 7.5% while acknowledging that ultimate loss rates are trending upward from historic lows, leading to a cautious outlook on future yields. The company reiterated a commitment to capital returns via dividends and share repurchases, though buyback pace remains price-sensitive.

Third quarter EBITDA was $2 billion, up 34% year-on-year, driven by structural margin improvements and the new European trade framework (TRQ). Management expects shipment growth to accelerate in Q4 with double-digit year-on-year improvement as destocking normalizes. The full benefits of the TRQ and capacity restarts are expected to materialize fully in 2027.

Monster Beverage reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.56 billion, a 16.7% increase year-over-year driven by strong international growth (28.1%) and solid U.S. performance (9.5%). Gross margin decreased to 54.7% due to higher aluminum costs and geographic mix shifts, while operating income rose 6.4% to $718.7 million. Management highlighted robust category health globally but declined to provide specific forward guidance or raise expectations.

Third quarter revenue was $101.9 million, up 24% year-over-year, driven by a doubling of commercial product revenue to $45 million led by FUROSCIX ReadyFlow. GAAP net loss widened to $23.2 million due to $11.6 million in CVR expenses and $5.2 million in amortization related to the scPharma acquisition. Management expects to return to profitability in Q4 2026 on both GAAP and non-GAAP bases, with full-year 2027 profitability anticipated.

PENN reported record Q3 FY2026 retail revenue of $1.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $502 million, representing a 5% YoY increase in revenue and 7.7% in Adjusted EBITDA. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for retail revenue to $5.89 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $1.973 billion, citing strong performance from new development projects like M Resort and Hollywood Columbus. Interactive segment revenue was $348.4 million with a loss of $18.3 million, though margins expanded significantly due to iCasino mix improvements.

Perma-Fix reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17.9 million and a net loss of $3.5 million, representing a decline in profitability compared to the prior year quarter due to lower gross profit in the treatment segment. Management noted that while backlog grew 25% to $19.6 million and pricing increases began implementation, full operations were delayed until September by customer-directed protocol changes and scheduled maintenance. The company expects revenue recognition from the Hanford DFLAW waste stream to continue ramping up over the next few months.

Park Hotels & Resorts reported Q3 FY2026 results with RevPAR increasing 8.4% year-over-year to $201 and hotel adjusted EBITDA rising 8% to $135 million. Management raised full-year guidance, updating the RevPAR outlook midpoint by 200 basis points to a range of 5.5%-6.0% and increasing adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $13 million at the midpoint to $635-$645 million. The quarter was driven by broad-based strength across the portfolio, including record performance at Orlando Bonnet Creek and significant recovery in Hawaii despite weather disruptions.

Reforation reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue up 19.1% YoY to $173.6 million, its 22nd consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with DTC up 16.7% to $152.8 million and wholesale up 40.8% to $20.8 million. Gross margin expanded 250 bps to 60.4% (200 bps excluding ~$800,000 of tariff refunds) and adjusted EBITDA rose 64.2% to $23.1 million at a 13.3% margin, though GAAP swung to a $1.1 million net loss ($0.02/share) on $10.5 million of IPO-related stock comp and a 165.9% effective tax rate. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $610-612 million (20-21% growth, above the mid-to-high teens algorithm) and put adjusted EBITDA margin at ~14.2%, the high end of the prior range. Q4 is framed as prudent given a back-half-weighted holiday and a dynamic macro backdrop.

Total company revenue was $274.3 million with adjusted operating income of $39.2 million; the Sphere segment grew revenue 14% YoY to $198.9 million and segment AOI rose to $32.4 million from $17.1 million on 241 Wizard of Oz performances versus 220 combined prior-year showings. MSG Networks deteriorated sharply, with revenue down to $75.4 million from $88.4 million and AOI to $6.8 million from $19.3 million on a ~15.5% subscriber decline, prompting a non-cash goodwill impairment charge. No quantitative guidance was given, but management said it still expects growth in 2027, reaffirmed 3-4 Sphere Experiences by end-2027, and guided to a new venue announcement likely this quarter. The main negative changes were the MSG Networks impairment and the scrapping of the From the Edge concept.

SPG reported Q3 real estate FFO of $3.37/share, up 4.7% YoY, with domestic property NOI +6.6% and portfolio NOI +6.7%. Comparable mall and outlet sales rose 4.9% and occupancy reached 96.5%, the highest combined level since 2016, while initial new-deal rents jumped 17% YoY with tenant allowances down 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 real estate FFO guidance by $0.10 to $13.30-$13.40/share (about 5% growth at the midpoint) and declared a $2.30 Q4 dividend, up 4.5% YoY. Reported FFO of $3.09 was reduced by $0.27/share of non-cash mark-to-market and equity revaluation losses, and management flagged roughly $0.30 of interest expense headwind for 2027.

Same-store weighted occupancy reached 88.6% (+200 bps YoY), same-store RevPOR rose 4.6% to $5,413 and resident revenue grew 7.3% to $163.5 million, lifting same-store NOI 15.6% with 230 bps of margin expansion to 31.8%. Normalized FFO was $0.46 per share and Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.2% to $46.8 million, while total SHOP NOI margin of 29.1% was up 240 bps YoY but down 80 bps sequentially on Q3 seasonality. Net leverage rose to 8.1x from 7.8x at June 30, and formal 2027 guidance is deferred to the Q4 call, with management only indicating occupancy and rate growth should be consistent with recent years.

NuScale reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $0.3 million versus $8.2 million a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to the absence of RoPower FEED Phase II work in the current quarter. Operating expenses fell to $65 million from $549 million in the prior-year period, and liquidity rose to roughly $1.9 billion from about $916 million. No revenue or margin guidance was issued; management said OpEx should stay fairly constant until an ENTRA1/TVA project ramps, and that margin clarity requires an OEM agreement. The key business development was a first-article manufacturing agreement with Doosan Enerbility, though TVA and RoPower commercial agreements remain unfinalized.

Core FFO was $0.64/share vs $0.60 a year ago (+6.7%), driven by 4.2% same-center NOI growth and accretive acquisitions; other revenues rose 11%. Full-year 2026 core FFO guidance was raised to $2.49-$2.53 from $2.45-$2.52 (+8% at midpoint), and the low end of same-center NOI growth was lifted to 3.5% from 2.75% with the high end unchanged at 4.25%. Occupancy reached 97.3% (+70 bps from June), blended cash rent spreads were 11% on ~560 leases signed over 12 months, and TTM tenant sales were $487/sq ft (+2.5%), with the occupancy cost ratio steady at 9.7%. The board authorized a $0.3125 quarterly dividend, a 7% increase year over year.

Q3 FY2026 net revenue was $16.2 million, up 38% YoY, with implant unit volume up 34% and gross margin expanding to 78.5% from 76.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $68-70 million (44-48% growth) from a prior $67-69 million (42-46%). Net loss narrowed to $7.0 million from $8.7 million, and Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $5.5 million, with cash of $92.3 million. Q4 is guided for similar gross margins but higher SG&A as a percentage of revenue and moderately increased cash burn.

Serve reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 million, up over 300% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12 million from a prior $9-10 million (implying ~$3 million in Q4 and ~4.5x prior-year revenue). Gross loss was $7.6 million at a negative 266% gross margin, but this marked a third consecutive quarter of improvement, with fleet margin up over 100 percentage points sequentially and cost of revenues down 14%. GAAP net loss was $59.2 million (-$0.68/share), non-GAAP net loss $44.6 million (-$0.51/share), with non-GAAP opex down $1.2 million sequentially to $39.2 million and $198 million in cash and marketable securities. Management also launched Serve Physical AI Services and flagged a $20 million reduction in full-year non-GAAP opex expectations versus the start of the year.

Q3 revenue rose 3% YoY to $738 million, in line with expectations of flat to low single-digit growth, while normalized adjusted EBITDA grew 13% to $170 million, beating the $155 million guide by $15 million and expanding margin 200 bps to 23%. Air marketplace bookings fell 1% on a 300-400 bps Middle East conflict and fuel-price headwind, though total marketplace bookings were flat and management expects sequential improvement into Q4. Full-year pro forma EBITDA guidance was raised $10 million to approximately $610 million and FCF guidance improved, while revenue and bookings growth outlooks were reaffirmed. Reported free cash flow was negative $48 million, attributed to $15 million of refinancing fees and $40 million of accrued interest, absent which it would have been positive.

Rayonier reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $0.41 on net income of $123 million, including $91 million of income from the ~36,000-acre Washington disposition; excluding that and $7 million of merger costs, EPS was $0.13 and adjusted EBITDA was $145 million, up sharply YoY on PotlatchDeltic contributions. Southern Timber adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to $52 million on 56% higher harvest volumes with delivered sawlog prices down 5% and pulpwood down 15% YoY (both up low-single digits sequentially), while Northwest Timber EBITDA jumped to $32 million from $6 million on doubled volumes and 29% higher sawlog prices. Wood Products EBITDA of $27 million was the best since Q3 2022 at $528/MBF lumber realization, but management guided Q4 realizations lower with quarter-to-date prices ~6% below Q3 and the Random Lengths composite 12% lower. Real Estate Q4 EBITDA is guided to $60-70 million, implying full-year toward the upper end of the $180-200 million range, buybacks totaled $60 million in Q3 with a $300 million authorization increase, and more timberland dispositions are planned over 12-18 months.

RLJ reported comparable RevPAR of $153, up 9.7% YoY, on ADR +6.4% to $203 and occupancy +230 bps to 75.4%, with each month beating expectations. Hotel EBITDA rose 17.5% to $93.9 million at a 26.5% margin (up 190 bps), adjusted EBITDA was $85 million (+17.3%), and adjusted FFO per share was $0.34 (+25.9%). Full-year comparable RevPAR guidance was raised to 5.75%-6.25% (up 200 bps at the midpoint), and corporate adjusted EBITDA guidance rose $9 million at the midpoint to $352-$358 million. The company also sold seven Chicago Midway hotels for $110 million at a 14x 2026 forecasted EBITDA multiple.

Rigel reported Q3 FY2026 net product sales of $72.3 million, up 13% YoY, driven by $6.6 million from newly launched VEPPANU (six weeks of availability) on top of TAVALISSE $46 million (+3%), REZLIDHIA $9.9 million (+20%), and GAVRETO $9.8 million (-11%). Total revenues were $80.9 million with net income of $13.2 million, down from $27.9 million a year ago on higher costs and expenses of $63.8 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $290-$295 million from $285-$295 million, while the non-VEPPANU product sales range was trimmed to $255-$260 million from $255-$265 million and contract revenue raised to $35 million. Management struck an upbeat tone on the VEPPANU launch (100+ patients in six weeks, 88% PA approval) and reiterated R289 dose selection and registrational trial initiation plans for 2027.

Regenxbio reported Q3 2026 cash, equivalents, and marketable securities of $251 million versus $241 million at year-end 2025, driven by a $100 million AbbVie NAAVIGATE milestone and $108 million in net proceeds from a July public offering; the total excludes a $39 million October Sarepta settlement payment. Royalty revenue came in slightly above one analyst's model on Itvisma pickup as U.S. Zolgensma IP has expired, though no explicit revenue or EPS figures were disclosed. Management guided to cash runway into late Q4 2027, spanning sura-vec wet AMD top-line data this quarter, a Q1 2027 RGX-202 BLA filing (switched from rolling to a single submission), and a 2027 sura-vec regulatory submission, with RGX-202 potential U.S. approval in H2 2027. No hard revenue, EPS, or margin results were reported, leaving the quarter defined by pipeline milestones rather than financial performance.

First quarter as Real REMAX Group: revenue $728M up 28% YoY (pro forma combined ~$770M, +20%), Adjusted EBITDA $34M up 66%, but GAAP operating loss of $72M and net loss of $67.2M driven by $78.7M of non-recurring acquisition costs. Management introduced 2027 guidance of $2.6-2.8B revenue and $175-190M Adjusted EBITDA on assumptions of 5-10% lower existing home sales and 3-4% lower prices, and Q4 revenue of $575-625M with $32-38M EBITDA. Cost actions exceeded plan — $40M+ gross savings actioned and 2027 synergy target lifted above $30M versus the original $30M — but North American RE/MAX agent count fell 3% and management off-boarded over 1,000 agents, with Tamir calling 2027 'another very challenging year.'

Park-Ohio reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenues of $459 million, a 15% year-over-year increase and 4% sequential growth, alongside a gross margin expansion of 120 basis points to 9.5%. Management raised full-year sales guidance to $1.75-$1.77 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.35-$3.50 per share, citing strong demand in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and AI data center markets. The company expects Q4 free cash flow to be significant as working capital levels normalize.

AVITA Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $26.1 million, up 53% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, led by U.S. RECELL revenue of $22.4 million (up ~20% QoQ) on 3,196 units. Gross margin expanded 270 bps to 84%, operating expenses held flat at $24.6 million, net loss narrowed to $6.2 million ($0.20/share), and net cash use fell to ~$600,000 from $3.2 million in Q2.
