Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $92-$94 million from $86-$89 million and reaffirmed Q4 cash flow breakeven, while noting Q3 likely benefited by roughly $1 million from summer burn seasonality. The going concern doubt was alleviated and the remaining $10 million Perceptive tranche was drawn.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $212,000 from $552,000 a year ago, with nine-month revenue of $814,000 versus $2 million; gross margin was 35% for the quarter and 39% year-to-date. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at approximately $1 million, while adjusted OpEx guidance was lowered to $87 million or less from $98 million and total cash usage to $87 million or less from $93 million. Adjusted operating expenses were $18.2 million versus $21.4 million a year ago and declined sequentially, with roughly $12 million in annualized savings from the August restructuring; net loss narrowed to $22.3 million from $35.7 million. Proteus remains on track for a Q2 2027 launch, but AI-driven demand is lengthening lead times on certain components, prompting earlier orders and incremental working capital, with cash of $149.4 million funding operations into Q4 2028.

Q3 revenue was $9.1 million, up 233% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 74.6%. Bookings were $98 million in the quarter and roughly $104 million year to date, with full-year bookings expected above $120 million. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $31-$34 million from $28-$32 million and reiterated greater than 100% revenue growth for 2027 off the higher base. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $80.5 million from $45.3 million as R&D rose to $97.5 million, and the company ended with over $1.9 billion in cash and no debt.

Q3 global system-wide sales fell 5.6% in constant currency to $1.15 billion, revenue dropped 10.5% to $455 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell $10 million to $38 million. North America comps and international comps (down 1.8%) both declined, with management citing an intensely promotional environment and soft new-customer acquisition; full-year guidance was cut to roughly -5% system sales, ~-8% North America comps, and approximately $175 million adjusted EBITDA, and Q4 is implied similar to Q3. CEO Penegor conceded top line came in below expectations and introduced the 'Unbox Better' strategy alongside a franchisee marketing framework approved by 98% of votes, a supply-chain margin reduction to 4%, and a tech-fee cut to 1.5%. Free cash flow was $19 million YTD versus $59 million last year; guidance assumes no improvement in the consumer environment and no benefit from Unbox Better.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $202.1M, down 1% YoY but up 32.5% sequentially from $152.5M, with net income of $29.9M ($1.30/diluted share) versus $1.20 a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 29.7% from 23.9% YoY, though that included a $3.8M tariff refund worth ~188 bps, and operating income was a record $40.9M (20.2% margin); operating cash flow was $40.9M and net cash reached ~$34M. Management raised its second-half outlook to net sales above 2H 2025 (prior: roughly in line), but guided Q4 gross margin down from Q3 on the non-recurring tariff refund plus a modest mix-driven further decline, and said it is not predicting a specific data center revenue level. Oil and gas softness continued (Power Systems sales down $6.2M YoY), partly offset by data center demand, and a new $220M three-year revolver cut borrowing spread 80 bps to SOFR+180.

Privia raised its 2026 outlook above the high end of initial guidance across all key financial metrics: implemented providers ~6,000 (11.5% growth), practice collections +13.1% at the midpoint, care margin +16.3%, and adjusted EBITDA +23.9% to a midpoint above the prior high end. Year-to-date practice collections rose 12% to $2.91 billion and adjusted EBITDA grew 21.9% to $114.7 million, or 28.8% of care margin, with $446.3 million of cash and no debt. Management is exiting the Montana Surgery Partners partnership (~$23 million annual practice collections, 69 providers) effective January 2027 with no material EBITDA impact, and announced the ~$36 million cash acquisition of Cano Health's American Choice MSSP ACO (~36,000 attributed lives). Cash flow conversion guidance was trimmed to ~70% of EBITDA from the prior 70%-80%, citing MSSP payment timing and full cash taxpaying status.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 1.1% to $506.5M as attendance dropped 4.7% (~320,000 guests) on weather, calendar and international headwinds, partly offset by total revenue per capita up 3.8%. Adjusted EBITDA declined $11.2M to $205.1M and net income fell to $80.0M from $89.3M; nine-month revenue was down 1.6% and Adjusted EBITDA down $31.4M. Management gave no formal 2026 or 2027 guidance, declining to commit to Q4 EBITDA growth given continued weather disruption, but cited a positive paid pass base (+0.3% through October), 2027-specific pass products up over 15%, deferred revenue up 4.9%, and a new $40M-$50M 2027 gross cost-savings target on top of the $50M 2026 program. The company bought back ~$218M of stock (~12% of shares) year-to-date but made no Q3 purchases due to cash flow timing.

Adjusted operating revenues rose 8% to $902 million and diluted adjusted operating EPS rose 7% to $6.77, but adjusted net operating income grew only 2% to $209 million on a smaller remeasurement gain ($9 million vs $23 million prior year). The investments business set records, with total ISP sales up 19%, variable annuities up 29%, managed accounts up 27%, AUM up 10% to $140 billion, and $407 million of net client flows. Term life was the weak spot: issued policies fell 7%, premiums fell 5%, and recruiting declined 10% year-over-year, with management guiding full-year 2026 issued policies down 8%-10% and year-end sales force down about 3%. Q4 guidance points to term life issued policies down low-single-digits and ISP sales up mid-single-digits.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 1.9% to $215.9 million with net income of $44.4 million ($0.70 diluted) versus $39.9 million ($0.60), and adjusted operating income grew 8.4% to $66.1 million with adjusted EPS of $0.77, up 18.5%. Total enrollments increased 1.6%, with AIU System up 7.5% to 10,830 and St. Augustine revenue up 9.8% to $41.7 million, while CTU enrollments were roughly flat at 31,870. Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $260-263 million versus $237.9 million in 2025, with Q4 adjusted EPS guided to $0.68-0.72 versus $0.59. The company declared a $0.17 quarterly dividend and repurchased 610,000 shares for $19.9 million, and announced a definitive agreement to acquire South University (~10,500 students) expected to close as early as April 2027.

Permian Resources reported Q3 FY2026 oil production of 208,000 bbl/d (up ~10,000 bbl/d QoQ, ~8,000 organic) and total production of 458,000 BOE/d, with record free cash flow of $0.98 per share. Controllable cash costs fell 6% QoQ to a company-low $7.05/BOE (LOE $5.11/BOE, cash G&A $0.73/BOE), and gas revenue swung from -$90 million in Q2 to over +$50 million. The company raised full-year oil guidance to a 202,000 bbl/d midpoint (7% above February guidance) and now expects ~$300 million (~$0.35/share) more free cash flow than its original plan, while announcing $1.15 billion of acquisitions including Ridge Runner. Q4 oil is guided to more than 210,000 bbl/d, and cash CapEx was updated to a $2.025 billion midpoint.

Playtika reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $673.8M, down 7.8% sequentially and essentially flat year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $252.1M (up 15.9% YoY, 37.4% margin) and net income of $40.4M. Guidance was reaffirmed, not raised: full-year revenue of $2.75B-$2.85B and adjusted EBITDA of $750M-$790M, now expected around the midpoint of both ranges versus last quarter's cautious second-half view. The quarter was driven by DTC revenue of $275.1M (40.8% of total, up 31.4% YoY), June's Journey up 12.1% and Slotomania stabilizing, offset by Bingo Blitz down 18.2% and Disney Solitaire down 21.9% sequentially. The board concluded its strategic review, opting to remain independent, with refinancing of upcoming maturities the stated priority.

Pulse Biosciences reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $395,000 versus $86,000 in the prior year period, with GAAP net loss widening to $23.1 million from $19.4 million and non-GAAP net loss to $17.5 million from $13.5 million. The company completed NANOPULSE-AF pivotal enrollment at 169 evaluable patients (189 total) in under six months, three months ahead of plan, and ended the quarter with $189.2 million in cash and marketable securities after raising $95.8 million through its ATM during the quarter. Management guided future quarterly non-GAAP costs and expenses to rise 15%-25% above the Q2/Q3 average of approximately $20 million, citing persistent AF IDE, additional studies, and manufacturing build-out; no revenue guidance was provided.

Third quarter revenue was $212.2 million, up 18.8% year-over-year, with diluted EPS of $0.53 compared to $0.27 in the prior year. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $850 million-$900 million and expects gross margins to be approximately 14%, slightly higher than previously anticipated due to a decrease in chassis sales. The company returned $5.1 million to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases.

Third quarter revenue reached a record $652.6 million, beating the high end of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA of $156 million and EPS of $2.07 also finished above the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue to $2.519-$2.534 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $589-$593 million, and adjusted EPS to $7.13-$7.29. The company announced a CEO succession with Steve Spittle taking over on April 1, 2027, following the separation of its food processing business.

Q3 revenues of $426 million rose 13% YoY, driven by M&A revenue up 40% and a record quarter in capital structure advisory, partly offset by softer capital markets after a record H1; first nine months revenue hit a record $1.15 billion, up 10%. Adjusted comp ratio improved to 65.8% from 66.2%, but adjusted pre-tax margin slipped to 21.4% from 22.2% as non-comp expenses rose, with full-year non-comp growth guided to approximately 19%. Management cited new business origination and announced pipeline up roughly 20% YoY with total pipeline at a record, while flagging macro and AI-financing volatility and a softer capital markets quarter. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was given, though management reiterated an expectation of some full-year comp leverage and flagged a few points of tax-rate headwind from Section 162(m) in 2027.

AGNT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion, up 6% YoY and within the $1.35-$1.45 billion guide, with gross profit of $91 million (up 6%) and adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, down 3% YoY within the $17-$22 million range. GAAP operating income fell 23% to $3.1 million on elevated legal costs, and Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $1.0-$1.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of negative $7 million to breakeven, with full-year revenue lowered to $4.85-$5.05 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $40-$47 million. Transactions of over 131,000 rose 8% YoY including NextHome but only 1.7% excluding it, while agents grew 5% to 87,457 and international revenue rose 27% with a narrowed operating loss. Management cited continued mortgage-rate pressure above 7.3% and peak 2026 legal matters as the drivers of the softer outlook.

First quarter after the merger/internalization closed August 6: ACR reported a GAAP net loss to common of $5.16 per diluted share and EAD loss of $2.64 per share, with book value per share of $16.81. The loss was driven by $38.3 million of one-time transaction-related charges ($13.7 million non-cash) and an $8.3 million CECL build to $29.4 million (137 bps, from $21.1 million). The $2.1 billion loan portfolio was stable (WA risk rating 2.6, 14% in rated 4/5 loans vs 17% at prior year end) and net growth was only $9 million. Management gave no specific guidance, declining to detail AUM cadence, and set a $2-$3 per share run-rate EAD objective for the coming years versus prior illustrative EAD cases of $2.24/$3.11/$4.09; stabilized G&A was indicated at $29-$32 million.

Enact reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted operating income of $164 million, or $1.19 per diluted share, down from $1.26 in Q2 but up from $1.12 a year earlier, with adjusted ROE of 12.4%. New insurance written was $14 billion, down 7% sequentially on lower refinance activity, while insurance in force rose 1% YoY to $275 billion and persistency held at an elevated 81%. A $37 million reserve release drove a 20% loss ratio even as total delinquencies rose 7% sequentially to 26,100 (2.8% rate) on seasonality. Management raised 2026 capital return guidance to approximately $600 million from the prior range and now expects expenses at the low end of the $205-210 million range.

Total revenue fell to $54.4 million from $59.4 million a year ago, with GAAP operating loss of $3.6 million and a GAAP net loss of $5.6 million (-$0.06 per diluted share) versus adjusted net income of $4.3 million ($0.04 per share). Deflecto was the clear weak spot, with revenue down to $27.2 million from $30.8 million and adjusted EBITDA down to $1 million from $2.6 million on soft Canadian and U.S. housing demand plus higher input costs, while Benchmark ($9.1 million adjusted EBITDA) and Printronix ($1.5 million) held up and public securities generated $8.2 million of realized gains. No formal guidance was given; management sized Deflecto's long-run EBITDA potential at $8 million-$10 million, said it was not committing to timing on incremental Cherokee wells, and disclosed a post-quarter up-to-$47.5 million non-recourse Cibolo facility for Cleveland drilling. Book value per share slipped to $5.65 from $5.71, hit by a $6.1 million hedge loss at Benchmark and $6.3 million of parent expenses.

AFC reported Q3 2026 net investment income of $3.5 million, or $0.16 per weighted average share, on total investment income of $8.6 million, with total expenses down to $5 million from $5.2 million in Q2. NAV per share rose $0.30 to $8.55, up $1.09 (~15%) year to date, helped by $0.13 of net unrealized appreciation and $0.06 of buyback accretion, while the $0.05 quarterly distribution was maintained. The portfolio held $361.1 million of principal across 18 investments at a 13.3% weighted average yield, with non-cannabis lower middle market loans at $93 million (32% of fair value); gross debt-to-equity fell to 1.03x from 1.1x. Management gave no formal guidance but flagged lumpy near-term deployment, a ~$1.1 billion pipeline including an expected $43 million healthcare facility, and continued work on the Devi and Justice Grown non-accruals, with collateral auctions set for November 12 and 19.

Aflac reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.43 (Dan's figure; CFO cited $2.46 ex-FX, down 1.2% YoY), aided by a $447 million pre-tax actuarial assumption unlock that added $0.71 per share and $40 million of Japan cybersecurity expense. Japan sales fell 4% to JPY 18.8 billion against a tough Miraito Cancer launch comparison but were up 3% for the first nine months, while U.S. sales rose 3.5% with net earned premium up 3.3% and a 27.7% pre-tax margin. Management raised the 2026 Japan pre-tax margin range to 35%-38%, called for benefit ratios below prior ranges in both Japan and the U.S., and said U.S. pre-tax margin will exceed the 17%-20% range, while Aflac Japan ceded roughly JPY 500 billion of reserves to Bermuda, releasing about $1 billion of capital. The quarter returned $1.1 billion to shareholders via $804 million of buybacks and $305 million of dividends, with ESR of 225% (238% with USP) and combined RBC slightly above 575%.

Kimbell reported record Q3 average daily production of 27,565 Boe/d, up 7% quarter-over-quarter, on oil, gas and NGL revenues of $96.9 million, with consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $80.4 million. Cash G&A was $2.48 per Boe, near the midpoint of guidance, and the company declared a $0.45 per unit distribution (75% of cash available for distribution, ~11% annualized tax-advantaged yield). Q4 2026 guidance ranges were reaffirmed rather than raised, with management citing a record line-of-sight well count, 93 active rigs, higher oil prices, and roughly 84% of estimated Q4 oil production unhedged. Since June 2026 the company has closed $367 million of acquisitions, and the revolver borrowing base was increased to $750 million in October.

Karman reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $202 million, up 66% YoY (25% organic) and 11% sequentially, with gross margin of 43%, net income of $21 million (+174%), adjusted EBITDA of $61 million (30% margin, +60%), and adjusted EPS of $0.19. Backlog reached a record $1.7 billion on bookings of nearly $465 million, more than double year-end 2025. The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $755-$760 million and adjusted EBITDA to $225-$227 million (about 29.8% midpoint margin), while reiterating 20%-25% organic growth for 2027 at roughly 30% EBITDA margins. Space and launch revenue declined 7% YoY on a ULA Vulcan cadence shift, and the free cash flow target for the second half was lifted to at least $20 million from a prior $15-$20 million goal.

Kimberly-Clark closed its acquisition of Kenvue during the quarter and framed Q3 as solid but impacted by discrete headwinds, including a ~130 bp retailer inventory drag in North America and a postponed major new product launch. Standalone FY2026 guidance was maintained; the company reiterated ~$1.9B of cost synergies, mid-single-digit adjusted EPS dilution in 2027 versus standalone KC, and mid-to-high single-digit compounded EPS growth for 2028. Management flagged softness in North America personal care (including ~1 point of club distribution headwind in diapers) while citing tissue share gains and Kenvue organic growth of ~3%. Much commentary covered integration, with consolidated financials and 2027 outlook deferred to CAGNY and February guidance.

First Majestic reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $394 million, up ~38% YoY, with EBITDA of $228 million (up 78%), silver production of 3.4 million ounces, and gold output of 30,000 ounces. Average realized silver price was $61.52/oz for the quarter versus $70.22 year-to-date, reflecting declining metal prices through the year. A 12-day labor disruption at San Dimas began mid-September and continues unresolved, with a court process underway over disputed income tax gross-up on union bonuses. Management declared a record dividend and bought back 1.3 million shares; no formal guidance ranges were provided on the call, with Jerritt Canyon and settlement details deferred to future updates.

Q3 revenue was $927M, down 0.8% YoY but within the flat-to-down-2% guidance, while underlying revenue grew 2.3% versus the 1%-2% guide; adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to $21.3M and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 2.3%, at the top of the range. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.07 from $0.17 on discrete tax items, and Education revenue declined 6.4%, below expectations on K-12 enrollment pressure. Management guided Q4 revenue to flat to up 1% (including a ~3-point extra fiscal week) with 180-200 bps of EBITDA margin expansion, and revised down its prior Q4 view on a slower Education recovery plus incremental pressure from one large ETM client, while reaffirming the full-year revenue and margin plan.

Agios reported record total net revenue of $55.4 million, more than 4x the $12.9 million in Q3 2025, with U.S. revenue of $48.7 million and ex-U.S. of $6.6 million; net loss narrowed to $65 million from $103.4 million. U.S. AQVESME net revenue rose 20% sequentially and ex-U.S. rose 74% QoQ; 177 start forms were added in Q3, bringing the cumulative total to 619 (roughly 15% of the ~4,000-patient launch population), with ~75% persistency at six months. The mitapivat sickle cell sNDA was classified a major amendment after an FDA REMS information request, extending the PDUFA to February 1, 2027, though management reported no liver-injury signal and unchanged benefit-risk. R&D headcount is being cut more than 35% (>100 roles) with $11 million of one-time Q4 charges, and the company targets non-GAAP profitability in 2028 with 2026 opex roughly flat ex-items.

Farmer Mac reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $122.7 million and core earnings of $52.6 million, or $4.82 per diluted share, with net effective spread of $113.9 million up 16% year over year. Nine-month revenue of $357.9 million and core earnings of $163.1 million rose 18.3% and 14.1% respectively, and outstanding business volume reached a record $38.5 billion. Management said it is on track to hit the $40 billion volume target two years early and reiterated 8%-11% annual volume growth through 2030, while net effective spread narrowed to 116 bps from 120 bps a year ago. Credit was the offset: the $11.1 million provision included a $4.4 million charge on a bankrupt telecom/fiber exposure, substandard assets rose to 2.1% from 1.7%, and 90-day delinquencies ticked up 17 bps sequentially to 54 bps.

ITT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue over $1.4 billion, up 44% reported and 8% organically, with orders up 58% (20% organic) at a 1.08x book-to-bill and adjusted EPS of $2.26, up 20%. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 bps to 21%, aided by 100 bps of CCT margin expansion to a record 22%. Management raised full-year organic revenue guidance to 7%-9% and lifted adjusted EPS to a midpoint of $8.58, a $0.36 increase with the low end of the new range now exceeding the prior high end; free cash flow guidance midpoint was raised to $610 million. SPX FLOW cost synergies now project over $20 million for 2026 versus a $15 million target, an annual run rate above $30 million against an original $80 million multi-year target.

ACM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $367.7 million, up 36.6% year-over-year, with shipments of $343.5 million up 30.6% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.55 versus $0.41. Operating margin expanded to 18.0% from 13.6%, though gross margin slipped to 41.6% from 42.1% on product mix, FX, and an inventory provision. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.24-$1.28 billion (up 38%-42%) from a prior $1.125-$1.175 billion range. Backlog reached $2.5 billion, up 88% year-over-year, and year-to-date orders rose 147%.

Arteris reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $25.8 million, up 48% YoY and above the top end of guidance, with record ACV plus royalties of $104 million (+39% YoY), trailing-twelve-month royalties of $9.4 million (+71% YoY), and record RPO of $135 million. Non-GAAP gross margin was 89%, non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $1.2 million, and non-GAAP net loss was $0.02 per diluted share. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance on revenue ($98.5-$99.5 million, up $2.5 million), ACV plus royalties (up $1 million), and non-GAAP operating loss (improved by $0.3 million), with free cash flow guidance unchanged. Q4 revenue guidance of $25.7-$26.7 million implies continued growth, and the CFO reiterated an OpEx growth model of roughly half revenue growth.

Q3 revenue was $1.122 billion, up 6% YoY (7% constant currency), with CIS revenue of $109 million up 34% and security up 9% to $622 million, offset by delivery down 3%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 25% and non-GAAP EPS was $1.77, down 5% YoY. Q4 revenue is guided to $1.145-$1.170 billion (5%-7% growth) with operating margin of ~24% and EPS of $1.50-$1.70, while full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $4.44-$4.465 billion reflects roughly $30 million of CIS revenue pushed from Q4 into 2027 due to supply chain and third-party data center delays. Management laid out 2027 CIS revenue of $1.1-$1.3 billion, total 2027 growth of 17%-22% constant currency, and 2028 revenue above $7 billion, driven by the $14 billion of signed CIS commitments.

Ironwood reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $133 million with LINZESS U.S. net sales of $325 million, GAAP net income of $60 million and record adjusted EBITDA of $98 million; YTD LINZESS sales of $880 million already exceed full-year 2025. Management raised full-year 2026 LINZESS net sales guidance to $1.2-1.25 billion (up $50 million at the midpoint, >35% YoY growth) as the second raise this year, with total revenue guidance of $485-510 million and adjusted EBITDA above $350 million. The company paid down $60 million of its revolver to $325 million outstanding and expects to end 2026 with under $300 million debt and gross leverage below 1X. STARS-2 site activation remains on track with primary completion estimated October 2028 and NDA submission in 2029.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue fell to $36.9M from $58.8M a year ago, with Vafseo net product revenue of just $14.8M (up 3% YoY despite ~140% patient growth) as a ~$4-5M inventory drawdown on lower-than-expected dose (~810mg vs 900mg) and dialysis non-compliance hit sales, while Auryxia collapsed to $20M from $42.5M on generic competition. Net loss was $14.4M versus prior-year net income of $0.5M, though SG&A fell to $23.5M and cash stood at $159.3M. Management guided to continued Q4 patient growth but expected further inventory reduction into the January 1, 2027 TDAPA expiration and flagged a post-TDAPA annual cost of therapy of $1,000-$1,500, far below typical pricing. Reported revenue missed the underlying end-user demand of $19-20M, and large dialysis providers remain largely unpenetrated.

Q3 revenue was $221.6M, up 14.9% YoY with Zio monitor ahead of expectations but Zio AT flat versus prior expectations of growth, and adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 23.1% (gross margin 74.2%, up 310 bps with ~140 bps from ~$3M one-time tariff refunds). Adjusted EPS was $0.82 versus a $0.06 loss a year ago, though GAAP net loss was $29.9M ($0.90/share) on a $50M IP litigation settlement charge. Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $890-895M (19-20% growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin to 15.5-16%, incorporating the earlier-closed VitalConnect acquisition (~$16M Q4 revenue, $65M run rate), while pushing the Zio MCT FDA submission to 2027. The key change versus prior periods is the Zio AT slowdown and the shift to VitalConnect as the near-term MCT platform alongside a fresh 2027 framework of ~$1B organic revenue, organic mid-teens growth, and at least 15% adjusted EBITDA margin.

Q3 revenue was EUR 8.9M against EUR 17.7M for 9M 2026 versus EUR 11.9M for 9M 2025 (+49% YoY), with gross margin of 47% (up from 46% in Q2). Order intake was EUR 42.2M, led by a EUR 33M LUMI-IQ Halocene contract with CSC, lifting backlog to EUR 102.5M from EUR 69.1M at June end. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at EUR 65-75M order intake and EUR 42-47M revenue, structurally Q4-heavy and dependent on acceptance of the first two 150-qubit systems already being installed. Operating loss was EUR 171M, including EUR 13.5M of one-time listing transaction costs and a EUR 127M non-cash share-based listing expense; cash stands at EUR 260M with runway into Q2 2028.

Clinical-stage business update with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed; the key financial datapoint is cash of EUR 96.8 million at September 30, 2026, with runway guided to end of Q1 2028. The Sobi lacutamab partnership closed, bringing a $75 million upfront plus up to $40 million in near-term Sezary milestones and $465 million in further milestones with tiered double-digit royalties; TELLOMAK-3 is initiated with first patient dosing expected Q1 2027. The PACIFIC-9 monalizumab readout slipped to H1 2027 from prior expectations, which management attributed to event-driven timing and declined to interpret. CFO Frederic Lombard will depart at end of December and a successor search has begun.

Iovance reported record Q3 FY2026 total revenue of ~$122M, up 80% YoY and 22% sequentially, with AMTAGVI sales of ~$102M (+77% YoY, +12% QoQ) and Proleukin ~$20M. Margin hit an all-time high of ~60% (up from 56% prior quarter), R&D fell ~16% sequentially to ~$49M, and cash of ~$382M supports runway into 2029. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $410M-$420M (issued five weeks earlier) and set no new raise, while highlighting pipeline progress (IOV-LUN-202, POSITILITY, SARATOGA) and an sBLA planned for 2027.

INSW reported Q3 net income of $344 million ($6.90 per share), adjusted net income of ~$291 million ($5.84/diluted share), and adjusted EBITDA of $345 million, in line with a solid prior quarter. Blended spot TCEs were $67,700/day versus $29,400/day a year ago, and crude tanker revenue hit a record $321 million including ~$77 million of dual-fuel VLCC profit sharing. For Q4, management has booked more than half of expected revenue days at a blended spot TCE above $172,000/day, more than double the record Q3 rate, and declared a $5.05/share dividend while maintaining an 85% payout commitment.

Q3 FY2026 EBITDA came in below consensus, which management attributed primarily to the Brazil online gaming shutdown; the low end of full-year guidance was cut to $109 million. EBITDA margin reached 46%, up roughly 900 bps YoY, aided by divesting the holiday park business, restructuring the pub business, and growing the higher-margin digital segment. Like-for-like revenue rose 9% adjusting for the U.K. tax impact, with interactive segment EBITDA up 20% pre-tax and U.S. GGR up over 30% YoY. Management pushed its multi-year growth targets out by a year, now expecting 2027 only modestly above 2026, and lowered the 2026 free cash flow conversion target from the prior 20%.

Innodata reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $95.6 million, up 53% YoY and 4% QoQ, beating consensus of $83.3 million by 15%. EPS was $0.29 versus $0.17 consensus (a 70% beat), and adjusted EBITDA of $17.7 million exceeded consensus by ~15%. Guidance for 2026 was raised to 42%+ growth from 40%-42%, but the raise was limited by a program termination at the historically largest customer expected to cost ~$12 million in Q4 revenue, which management expects to replace by Q1. The quarter was a clear beat-and-raise despite the Q4 air gap, with strong new program wins across physical AI, RL environments, trust and safety, and federal.

Albemarle reported Q3 2026 net sales of $1.6 billion, up 19% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $646 million, up 186%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 42% and adjusted EPS of $2.58 ($2.15 GAAP). Specialties EBITDA rose 31% and the company raised its full-year specialties adjusted EBITDA outlook to $350-375 million while cutting 2026 capex to $300-350 million from approximately $500 million. However, energy storage shipments fell year-over-year to 56,000 tons LCE and management guided Q4 energy storage net sales and EBITDA to decline sequentially on lower pricing and higher-cost spodumene flowing through COGS. Year-to-date operating cash flow was $1.5 billion with 67% conversion, and the CEO transition to Rag Udd on February 1 was noted.

Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 8.2% to $134.7 million, but management said revenue missed guidance by $2.5 million because chain accounts delayed orders into Q4. Gross margin fell to 33.5% from 34.5%, operating income dropped to $4.9 million from $8.6 million, and adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.24 from $0.37 as resin, ocean freight (14.2% of sales vs an ~11% average), and online shipping costs rose. Q4 guidance is 9%-11% net sales growth with 33%-35% gross margin and high-single-digit adjusted EBITDA margin, supported by October/November price increases and a 3%-13% increase planned for January 2027; full-year 2026 guidance is 9%-11% sales growth, 39%-41% gross margin, and mid-teens adjusted EBITDA margin.
